news.Title: Why Netflix reportedly walked away from Xbox licensing deal
news.Content:
Netflix (NFLX) reportedly wanted seven years of exclusive film and TV rights to Microsoft's (MSFT) Xbox game library, which includes popular titles such as Halo and Gears of War.

The streaming company is said to have offered a deal worth half a billion dollars. But Microsoft wanted much more.

According to Matthew Belloni's report in Puck News, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma asked for $800 million instead, Gadgets Now noted. Then Netflix said no and pulled its offer entirely after an executive change.

How the Netflix-Xbox talks collapsed

The original $500 million offer came from Bela Bajaria, Netflix's former chief content officer. Sharma and her team countered with an $800 million ask, which Netflix CFO Spencer Neumann rejected because it was too expensive, Puck reported. However, the deal was still on the table at the time.

Also read: Bank of America backs Disney stock as your streaming bill climbs

Then a Netflix restructuring in mid-October brought about 1,000 job cuts and the exit of Bajaria after a decade with the company. After Bajaria left, former Disney executive Peter Rice stepped in as her replacement, Netflix announced.

It was only after the replacement that the Xbox offer came off the table.

Why Xbox felt confident asking for $800 million

Xbox had its reason for asking for a higher amount. Amazon's "Fallout" show and HBO's "The Last of Us" both proved that a hit TV adaptation can improve game sales and bring old titles back to life.

And with the 2023 purchase of Activision Blizzard, Microsoft owns the biggest game catalog outside of China.

On Oct. 8, 2026, Microsoft also launched a new division called Xbox XP , led by former Mojang president Kayleen Walters, Xbox confirmed. The group was formed to handle film, TV, merchandise, live events, and brand partnerships.

"Our franchises can mean more to people than the time they spend playing them," Sharma said in a staff message, as Morningstar reported.

More Streaming Stocks:

Now, instead of entering an encompassing exclusive deal with just one company, Xbox is pursuing multiple smaller deals. For example, Amazon gets "Fallout" Season 3, Paramount Pictures gets a "Call of Duty" movie, and Netflix still gets "Gears of War" and "Diablo."

What the walk-away signals for Netflix shareholders

Netflix investors have been worried about the company spending too much, and the stock's third-quarter results suggest their worries are valid.

Story Continues

In Q3, Netflix's revenue grew 12% year over year to $12.9 billion , which sounds fine at first glance, but the company also lowered the forecast for its 2026 advertising revenue from $3 billion to $2.7 billion , an SEC filing confirmed.

A lower ad revenue forecast means Netflix expects less money to come in, which is why investors are paying attention to its spending.

Related: Ackman's $1 billion Netflix return has a remarkable twist

Wall Street was already losing patience before that report. Back in July, Barclays analysts said Netflix was "losing narrative control," meaning investors no longer trusted its growth story, Stocktwits reported. When investors begin to lose trust in a stock, the company's management usually has to prove it can be careful with cash.

Netflix rejecting Xbox's counter can be seen as a sign that the company's new leadership is doing exactly that.

The risk Netflix takes by passing on Xbox IP

If gaming adaptations keep producing hits, Netflix could watch competitors build loyal fan bases that might have helped to improve its own number of subscribers.

Microsoft said Netflix remains a "valued partner," so the other projects they're working on together, like the Minecraft and Diablo shows, are still on track.

news.Title: Google財報暴雷拖累！台積電下殺10元回測季線 分析師：買黑不買紅
news.Content:
Google財報暴雷！台積電（2330） 今（29）日盤中跌10元回測季線，終結連二漲，分析師表示，外資還在觀望中，但台積電基本面表現無虞，一旦不確定性消弭仍有機會挑戰前高 2,590 元，投資人可秉持「買黑不買紅」原則，可趁股價貼近季線2420元附近逢低分批布局。

美國聯準會（Fed）如期維持利率不變，市場目光轉向企業關鍵財報表現，激勵美股四大指數周三（28日）全數收紅，寫下連三漲紀錄，費城半導體指數勁揚 1.75%，台積電 ADR 表現穩健，上漲 2.64 美元（或 0.60%），收在 439.51 美元。

在美股收紅的背景下，台股今（29）日早盤卻未能延續多頭氣勢，權值股台積電開低走低，盤中最低觸及2,415 元，下跌10 元（跌幅約 0.41％）。

國泰證期顧問處協理郭經緯指出，外資目前態度轉趨觀望，使台積電股價於季線約2,420元附近震盪整理。不過從基本面來看，台積電營運表現無虞，先前法說會不僅對第四季展望保持正向，也重申對人工智慧（AI）強勁需求不變，晶圓代工與先進封裝的能見度更已達明年。

郭經緯分析，近期干擾市場的主要因素，來自美國期中選舉的不確定性，以及部分科技巨頭的財報表現。以 Google 母公司Alphabet為例，雖然在 AI 帶動下雲端業務營收翻倍，但龐大的基礎建設資本支出持續消耗現金，加上股權投資出現鉅額虧損，引發市場疑慮。不過，一旦這些短期不確定性逐漸消弭，台積電後續仍有機會挑戰前高2,590元。

針對投資人近期的操作策略，郭經緯建議採取「買黑不買紅」原則，可趁股價貼近季線時逢低分批布局。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 超越"超級循環" 測試設備商愛德萬再升財測 股價飆
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-29 09:22:32 蔡承啟 發佈

AI相關半導體市場進入高速成長階段、超越「超級循環(Supercycle)」，全球半導體測試設備巨擘、輝達(Nvidia)測試設備供應商愛德萬測試(Advantest)再度調升財測，財測優於市場預期，且宣布買回庫藏股。今日股價聞訊飆漲。

根據Yahoo Finance的報價顯示，截至台北時間29日上午8點55分為止，愛德萬飆漲8.02%至37,730日圓，今年迄今股價累計狂飄約92%。

愛德萬28日於日股盤後公布財報新聞稿指出，隨著AI普及，帶動測試設備需求超乎預期，因此今年度(2026年度、2026年4月-2027年3月)合併營收目標自原先(7月)預估的1兆7,140億日圓上修至1兆8,630億日圓(將年增65.1%)、合併營益目標自8,460億日圓上修至9,670億日圓(將年增93.7%)、合併純益目標自6,600億日圓上修至7,415億日圓(將年增97.5%)，營收、營益、純益將續創歷史新高紀錄。此為愛德萬繼7月之後、第2度上修今年度財測預估。

日媒報導，愛德萬集團CEO Douglas Lefever在28日舉行的財報說明會上表示，「AI相關半導體市場正處於高速成長階段，甚至可稱為超越『超級循環(Supercycle)』的『巨型循環(Megacycle)』。愛德萬將提前擴充產能、大幅加快擴產速度」。

路透社報導，分析師平均預估愛德萬今年度純益將為6,637億日圓，愛德萬上修過後的數值優於市場預期。

愛德萬將今年度「測試系統事業」銷售額(營收)目標自原先預估的1兆5,750億日圓上修至1兆7,145億日圓。其中，SoC用測試設備銷售額目標自1兆2,435億日圓上修至1兆3,750億日圓、記憶體用測試設備銷售額目標自2,270億日圓上修至2,290億日圓。

愛德萬同時公布上季(2026年7-9月)財報：合併營收較去年同期暴增81.7%至4,777億日圓、合併營益飆增146.0%至2,668億日圓、合併純益飆增142.7%至1,933億日圓。

就部門別銷售情況來看，上季愛德萬「測試系統事業」銷售額暴增83.9%至4,367億日圓。其中，SoC用測試設備銷售額飆增103.3%至3,533億日圓、記憶體用測試設備銷售額大增21.6%至534億日圓。

就區域別銷售情況來看，上季愛德萬於台灣市場的銷售額較去年同期飆增126.4%至2,613億日圓、中國市場銷售額暴增72.9%至901億日圓、南韓銷售額增加15.1%至646億日圓。

愛德萬並於28日宣布，將祭出庫藏股買回措施，買回上限為2,800億日圓、1,100萬股(佔已發行股數比重1.5%)，買回期間為2026年10月29日-2027年3月24日。

(圖片來源： 愛德萬 )

展望台股後市，工商報導，統一投顧董事長黎方國說，台股短線負乖離過大，並有聯發科、台達電、聯電等電子大廠法說及鴻海科技日等利多登場，上市櫃第三季獲利亮眼，賣壓逐步消化下有助回歸基本面。

news.Title: NiSource Inc (NI) (Q3 2026) Earnings Call Highlights: $40 Billion Capital Plan, Microsoft Deal ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Consolidated Adjusted EPS (Q3 2026): $0.27 vs. $0.19 in Q3 2025.

Year-to-Date Consolidated Adjusted EPS: $1.49.

2026 Adjusted EPS Guidance: Narrowed to upper half of $2.02$2.07 range.

2027 Adjusted EPS Guidance: Initiated at $2.22$2.30, including $0.05$0.09 GenCo contribution.

Long-Term EPS Growth: 10%11% consolidated adjusted EPS CAGR through 2033; base plan 6%8% annual EPS growth.

Capital Plan: $40 billion 7-year plan through 2033 ($32 billion base plan; ~$8 billion GenCo); consolidated investment growth of 9%10%.

GenCo EPS Contribution: $0.32$0.40 expected in 2030, growing to $0.52$0.68 by 2033.

Customer Savings (GenCo Agreements): ~$1.75 billion expected savings to existing NIPSCO Electric customers (up from $1.4 billion last quarter); ~$140 per year for average residential customer at full ramp.

O&M: Higher year over year due to storm response costs; otherwise flat; commitment to flat O&M maintained; more than $40 million of cost optimization initiatives underway.

Usage and Customer Accounts: Up year over year at NIPSCO, Columbia Gas of Ohio, Virginia and Kentucky.

Financing: $750 million junior subordinated notes issued in August; $400 million$600 million maintenance equity annually near term, stepping down to minimal levels starting 2032.

Balance Sheet: FFO to debt commitment of 14%16% in all years of the plan.

Customer Bill Impact: Average annual residential bill increases reduced by over 100 basis points to less than 4% from 2027 through 2031.

GenCo Capacity: ~5 GW of signed capacity advancing; targeting up to 4 GW of potential additional load; Microsoft agreement adds ~1,100 MW (500 MW combustion turbines, 600 MW battery storage) under a 20-year term starting 2028.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 7 Warning Signs with NI.

Is NI fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: October 28, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

NiSource Inc ( NYSE:NI ) extended its long-term capital plan through 2033, totaling $40 billion, with a 10%-11% adjusted EPS CAGR and 9%-10% investment growth.

The company signed a 20-year agreement with Microsoft, bringing total customer savings to $1.75 billion and adding 1,100 MW of generation capacity.

NiSource Inc ( NYSE:NI ) narrowed 2026 EPS guidance to the upper half of $2.02-$2.07 and initiated 2027 guidance of $2.22-$2.30, implying double-digit growth.

The base business remains strong, with 6%-8% annual EPS growth expected through 2033, supported by pipeline modernization and safety investments.

GenCo's EPS contribution is now expected to reach $0.52-$0.68 by 2033, up from prior estimates, driven by customer ramp-ups and efficient financing.

Story Continues

Negative Points

NiSource Inc ( NYSE:NI ) faced a severe derecho storm in August 2026, causing significant damage and higher O&M costs, with restoration efforts ongoing.

The company is undergoing regulatory reviews and rate cases in multiple states, including Ohio, Kentucky, Virginia, and Indiana, which could impact financial results.

NiSource Inc ( NYSE:NI ) plans to issue $400-$600 million of maintenance equity annually in the near term, potentially diluting shareholder value.

The GenCo segment's cash flows are back-end loaded, with full customer ramp-up not until 2030-2032, requiring ongoing financing and execution risk.

Affordability concerns and political scrutiny in Pennsylvania and Indiana could affect regulatory outcomes and the company's ability to recover costs.

Q & A Highlights

Q : Shar Pourreza of Wells Fargo asked whether the Microsoft agreement largely captures the opportunity with Microsoft or should be viewed as a first phase of something larger. A : CEO Lloyd Yates declined to comment on customer sites or their size, but said NiSource is actively engaged with all three major customers and those in the queue, noting significant demand in the pipeline and confidence in executing on it.

Q : Julien Dumoulin-Smith of Jefferies asked how NiSource thinks about the physical requirements (generation and transmission) to serve potential upside Microsoft load beyond the initial 788 MW, and how it views ownership of the battery tolling arrangement over time. A : EVP and Chief Commercial Officer Michael Hooper said Indiana is a favorable location for generation growth and data center service, and the pool portfolio is planned to serve all customers without overbuilding while mitigating risk. He noted the company has grown with Amazon through additional agreements and will continue adding high-creditworthy counterparties. CFO Shawn Anderson added that NiSource uses a mix of owned and tolled batteries to balance financial parameters and maintain flexibility as technology evolves.

Q : Ross Fowler of Bank of America asked what drove the Amazon CCGT timing shift to 2030, how Amazon will be served in the meantime, and who bears the incremental costs. A : Michael Hooper clarified that not both CCGTs are shifting to 2031, and the change reflects optimization rather than delaybatteries are coming online ahead of schedule and incremental acceleration agreements are in place, de-risking construction and improving execution confidence. Shawn Anderson added that capital requirements were unchanged in the disclosure, and pricing signals remain set off the customer ramp rate.

Q : Ross Fowler of Bank of America asked whether adding more GenCo capacity means more GenCo CapEx while enabling regulated CapEx to be funded with the same balance sheet and potentially lower funding requirements. A : CFO Shawn Anderson confirmed that view, citing the strong starting FFO-to-debt position of 16.1% at year-end 2025, the base business's intrinsic cash flow power, over 90% recovery within 12 months, and the GenCo model's ability to shape cash flow through its rate structurereducing regulatory lag and balancing financing requirements while earning above-regulated returns.

Q : Nicholas Campanella of Barclays asked for an update on the strategic review of GenCo regarding execution beyond 9 GW, and whether the review must be completed before executing on the remaining 4 GW. A : CEO Lloyd Yates said the review does not need to happen before executing on the next 4 GW2 GW are in strategic negotiations and 2 GW more are being studied for upsizing. He said the size of GenCo will be rolled out sometime in 2027, and the company is optimistic.

Q : Nicholas Campanella of Barclays asked how legislative discussions in Indiana about resiliency and reliability following the storms inform the capital plan, and whether a wider resiliency package could be put forward. A : CEO Lloyd Yates said NiSource will actively participate in the IURC hearing, acknowledged that long outages are not good for customers, and said investment to harden the system is being studied. The company will make clear what capital investment is required and roll that out to regulators and legislators, with visibility on the investment opportunity expected in the near future.

Q : Jeremy Tonet of J.P. Morgan asked how to think about regulatory positioning and the playbook in Indiana, particularly with the customer savings in mind. A : CEO Lloyd Yates said GenCo addresses affordability, with $1.75 billion now rolling back to customers and growing as GenCo grows. A "Data Center Credit" should appear on customer bills pending IURC approval, likely late in the fourth quarter or early next year, ramping up as customers ramp. Michael Hooper added that GenCo is isolated from the electric utility rate base, so customers do not bear the construction risk.

Q : Steve Fleishman of Wolfe Research asked about the $2.3 billion cost for the two new combustion turbines relative to roughly 408 MW, and whether it includes more than generation. A : Michael Hooper said the cost includes all transmission and infrastructure and associated equipment, not just the two F-frame combustion turbines. The company has not disclosed the generation-only figure.

Q : Gabe Moreen of Mizuho asked about the drivers behind the GenCo EPS contribution range and expectations thereafter. A : CFO Shawn Anderson corrected the range to $0.52 to $0.68 for 2033, the first year of full customer ramp, driven predominantly by capacity fee revenue. He noted financing costs are still being absorbed as construction and development costs are paid down, and he expects the EPS contribution to become more efficient and step up closer to the middle of the next decade, outside the plan horizon.

Q : Gabe Moreen of Mizuho asked about the financing assumptions behind the 7-year plan, including rates and O&M, and whether they changed given the forward interest rate curve. A : CFO Shawn Anderson said the plan never projected material rate cuts and did not need modification due to recent market dislocation. NiSource has flexibility to select different tenors and be opportunistic on both debt and equity, waiting for the right environment to lock in long-term commitments accretive to the plan.

Q : Sophie Karp of KeyBanc asked how the 9 GW pipeline remains at 9 GW after the recent deal, and whether it was backfilled. A : Michael Hooper explained the 9 GW comprises 5 GW of signed capacity, 2 GW in strategic negotiations, and 2 GW in developing opportunities, with expansions to be brought back in 2027. CEO Lloyd Yates added that the pipeline is much larger than 9 GW, and the study is assessing how much more can be accommodated and over what time period.

Q : Sophie Karp of KeyBanc asked what NiSource expects to learn from its self-initiated storm response study and how it interacts with the IURC proceedings. A : CEO Lloyd Yates said the study will be submitted to the Commission and is expected to identify how the company can do better, what investments are needed to harden the system, and how to improve customer communication during significant storms.

Q : Travis Miller of Morningstar asked whether the financing plan includes a pro rata contribution from Blackstone. A : CFO Shawn Anderson

news.Title: What NiSource (NI) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in NiSource, Inc? Here are five stocks we like better.

NiSource reported stronger third-quarter results , with adjusted EPS rising to $0.27 from $0.19 year over year. The company narrowed its 2026 outlook to the upper half of its $2.02–$2.07 range and initiated 2027 guidance of $2.22–$2.30.

The company expanded its seven-year capital plan to $40 billion , including $8 billion for GenCo projects serving large data-center customers. NiSource expects adjusted EPS to grow 10%–11% annually from 2027 through 2033.

NiSource signed a 20-year electricity agreement with Microsoft beginning in 2028, adding roughly 1,100 megawatts of generation and battery capacity. The deal is expected to increase savings for NIPSCO customers, subject to regulatory approval, while GenCo's EPS contribution is projected to grow through 2033.

NIO Inc.'s Geely Deal Is Really a Bet on Battery-Swap Network Utilization

NiSource (NYSE:NI) reported third-quarter 2026 consolidated adjusted earnings per share of $0.27, up from $0.19 a year earlier, and said it was narrowing its full-year outlook to the upper half of its prior $2.02-to-$2.07 adjusted EPS range.

Year-to-date adjusted EPS totaled $1.49. Chief Financial Officer Shawn Anderson said the quarter benefited from cost management and higher customer usage and customer counts at NIPSCO and Columbia Gas operations in Ohio, Virginia and Kentucky. Operations and maintenance expense increased year over year because of storm-response costs, while other activities were flat, he said.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

EVs Are Big Winners of the Iran War—Just Not American Ones

The utility also initiated 2027 adjusted EPS guidance of $2.22 to $2.30 and extended its long-term financial plan through 2033. The company now expects consolidated adjusted EPS to grow at a 10% to 11% compound annual rate from its 2027 expectations through 2033, including contributions from its GenCo business that serves large-load customers.

Capital plan expands to $40 billion

NiSource outlined a seven-year, $40 billion capital plan, consisting of $32 billion for its regulated base business and about $8 billion for GenCo investments supporting data-center customers. The plan includes gas-system modernization and safety work, electric reliability and resiliency investments, generation capacity and infrastructure intended to support economic development.

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

AI's Biggest Bottleneck Could Make These 2 Stocks Soar

Story Continues

Anderson said the plan is designed to convert more than 90% of investments into initial recovery within 12 months. The company expects 9% to 10% consolidated investment growth and said its base business is expected to provide 6% to 8% annual adjusted EPS growth through 2033.

NiSource also maintained its target of 14% to 16% funds from operations to debt throughout the plan. In August, the company issued $750 million of junior subordinated notes. It expects to issue $400 million to $600 million of maintenance equity annually in the near term, with those requirements declining to minimal levels beginning in 2032 as the business generates more of its own funding.

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

The company said Blackstone is expected to contribute its pro rata 19.9% share of investments across the NIPSCO and GenCo capital plans.

Microsoft agreement adds to data-center strategy

NiSource announced that Microsoft will take electric service under a 20-year agreement beginning in 2028. The agreement is expected to increase the GenCo-owned pool portfolio by roughly 1,100 megawatts, including about 500 MW of combustion turbines and 600 MW of battery storage.

Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer Michael Luhrs said NiSource expects to file the special contract with the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission by year-end and is seeking an order during the first half of 2027. The agreement includes minimum capacity charges, pass-through treatment of variable costs and termination protections, according to the company.

The Microsoft deal marks NiSource's fifth GenCo agreement in just over a year and its third signed major technology customer, joining agreements with Amazon and Alphabet. The company said its signed agreements are expected to provide approximately $1.75 billion in savings to existing NIPSCO electric customers, up from $1.4 billion cited last quarter.

At full ramp, NiSource estimates those agreements could lower annual bills by about $140 for an average residential customer. The company said bill credits could begin as early as January, subject to IURC approval, and may appear as a "My Data Center Credit."

Luhrs said the company has approximately 5 GW of signed capacity, 2 GW in strategic negotiations and another 2 GW of developing opportunities. NiSource is studying the potential to expand its GenCo model beyond its current 9 GW pipeline and expects to provide an update in 2027. Management said its agreements are structured so data-center customers pay costs associated with their load, while existing electric customers are insulated from the GenCo assets in the utility rate base.

The company expects GenCo to contribute $0.05 to $0.09 to 2027 adjusted EPS. By 2030, it expects the segment to contribute $0.32 to $0.40 per share, rising to $0.52 to $0.68 in 2033 as customers reach full demand and financing costs become more efficient.

Storm response and regulatory matters

President and Chief Executive Officer Lloyd Yates said an Aug. 11 derecho with wind speeds reaching 110 miles per hour caused severe damage across northern Indiana, followed by additional rounds of severe weather. NiSource activated its incident command structure, suspended noncritical work and brought in more than 1,700 external personnel within 24 hours.

The company completed its broad restoration work by Aug. 25 without injury, Yates said. NiSource is conducting an internal after-action review expected to conclude by late November and has hired an outside expert to independently review its response. It is also participating in reviews by the IURC.

Management said the reviews are expected to identify opportunities to improve storm response, customer communications and investments needed to harden the electric system. The company has not yet quantified potential resiliency investments.

On regulatory matters, NiSource said Columbia Gas of Ohio filed its first three-year forward-looking rate case under the framework established through Ohio Senate Bill 103. Its Kentucky and Virginia rate cases remain on schedule, with Virginia rates effective Oct. 12 subject to refund and decisions in both states expected in the first half of 2027.

NIPSCO also received a fourth federal order in September requiring continued operation of the Schahfer Coal Units. The company said it is pursuing recovery of compliance costs through the FERC-approved MISO tariff schedule while evaluating a potential extension of the units' operations through its integrated resource plan.

About NiSource (NYSE:NI)

NiSource Inc is a regulated energy holding company based in Merrillville, Indiana. Through its operating companies, the company provides natural gas distribution and electric utility services to residential, commercial and industrial customers.

NiSource's natural gas operations include Columbia Gas utilities serving customers in several states, including Kentucky, Maryland, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Virginia. Its electric utility, Northern Indiana Public Service Company (NIPSCO), serves customers in northern Indiana and provides both electric power and natural gas services.

The company's operations include energy delivery infrastructure, utility system maintenance, customer services and investments intended to support reliability and the transition of its generation portfolio.

news.Title: U.S. stock futures drop as Alphabet slides on soft earnings, Microsoft firms
news.Content:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures fell on Wednesday evening, pressured chiefly by a sharp drop in Google owner Alphabet after its third-quarter earnings missed expectations.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Alphabet's drop largely overshadowed gains in Microsoft after its quarterly earnings beat expectations. Markets were also parsing comments from the Federal Reserve that could herald more interest rate hikes in the coming months.

Nasdaq 100 Futures slid 1.2% to 29,619.50 points by 19:39 ET (23:39 GMT). S&P 500 Futures fell 0.5% to 7,743.25 points, and Dow Jones Futures fell 0.06% to 52,663.0 points.

Futures fell after a mildly positive session on Wall Street, where blowout third-quarter earnings from memory chip giant SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) helped spur some gains in tech.

Alphabets slides nearly 10%, Microsoft rises on qtrly earnings

Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) was among the worst aftermarket performers, losing 9.8% after its third-quarter profit missed expectations by a wide margin.

While its revenue just edged past expectations on growing returns from its cloud unit, overall profitability was impacted by continued, outsized spending on artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure.

The earnings release added to growing Wall Street concerns over whether the billions of dollars poured into AI in recent years will be able to generate adequate returns– a notion that battered tech stocks since late-September.

Investors also largely looked past Google's unveiling of a new AI model– Gemini 4 Carbon.

On the other hand, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) rose 2.7% in aftermarket trade after it delivered a top and bottom-line beat in its fiscal first-quarter earnings.

Microsoft's Azure unit grew more than expected in the quarter, indicating that the tech giant was progressing well in its efforts to monetize AI.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Alphabet and Microsoft are among the largest spenders on AI infrastructure– a group dubbed as Wall Street's "hyperscalers," with their earnings offering the most insight into the AI trade and returns from the fast-growing technology.

Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), another hyperscaler, is set to report September quarter earnings on Thursday.

Fed leaves rates on hold, Warsh offers few direct cues

Story Continues

Wall Street ended slightly higher on Wednesday after the Fed left interest rates unchanged at 4.0% as widely expected, with two of the 12-member Federal Open Market Committee calling for a 25 basis point hike.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking after the meeting, highlighted recent strength in the economy, but declined to provide any forward guidance on interest rates.

Still, he reiterated the central bank's commitment to its 2% annual inflation target. The Fed had raised rates by 25 basis points in September, as it moved to cool increasingly sticky inflation.

Warsh's comments on the economy– where he highlighted resilient spending and stable employment– were largely interpreted as hawkish, with Treasury yields rising sharply on his comments.

The 10-year yield rose back above 5% after Warsh's address, although it did trim some gains in evening trade.

Markets were also seen ratcheting up bets on a 25 bps hike by the Fed in December, with CME Fedwatch indicating a 83.5% chance for a hike– up from 72.8% a day earlier.

Focus now turns to upcoming third-quarter gross domestic product data and PCE price index data for September– both of which are likely to factor into the Fed's plans for interest rates.

Core PCE data is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, and is expected to have remained well above the central bank's 2% annual target in September.

news.Title: 台股千點反攻是逃命？專家警告要出大事 台積電季線下彎空頭風暴
news.Content:
台股昨（28）日強勢反彈開高走高，收盤大漲939.35點，以47035.58點作收，但成交量僅7221億。但承通投顧副總陳嘉偉直言，「這個反彈是讓你逃命」，因為量才是價的根本，但今天的反彈成交量太少，其實是台股跌了4千多點後的空頭反彈。

陳嘉偉在個人YT節目中指出，台股昨單日上漲逾900點，但成交量未能同步放大，反彈的持續性仍有待觀察，從技術分析角度來看，價格與成交量必須相互配合。因此他提醒，如果沒有利用昨天大漲跑掉，今天早上一定要賣掉，不然真的就出大事了。」

陳嘉偉預期台股將迎來年線的對稱跌幅，甚至恐下探5年線，11月恐將更慘，因為弱勢反彈會往下跌破頸線。而且他認為這次全球股市是完美風暴，結合1997年亞洲金融風暴、2000年網路泡沫、以及2008年的金融海嘯和2010年的歐債危機利空，正面臨多重風險交錯的環境。

此外，陳嘉偉也將美國科技股及人工智慧（AI）產業的資本支出列為另一項重要風險。尤其大陸開源實驗室占全世界Token使用量達70%，「美國人賺不到一毛錢」，加上美國民眾反對建設資料中心、建設延誤，舉債投資市場上也不買帳，如果投資回收不如預期，企業可能必須重新調整資本支出計畫，甚至尋求其他融資方式。

再從台股指標股台積電來看，10月法說會股價也沒有爬起來，外資拚命倒貨。他認為現在台積電表現遠比台股弱，已形成季線下彎，而台積電很少季線下彎，前一次是因川普關稅大跌32.6%，往前一次季線下彎是俄烏戰爭下跌46.2%。

陳嘉偉分析，萬一這次台積電下跌32.6%，若台股跌幅一樣，將是年線對稱跌幅；如果台積電跌到46.2%，台股則會跌到約26882點，即5年線位置。他再度強調台股M頭已經做完了，第二個頭已經開始崩盤，「空頭大屠殺只是剛開始。」

news.Title: OpenAI Reportedly Plans to Buy Google's AI Chips. Should You Sell Nvidia Stock?
news.Content:
OpenAI plans to buy Google's artificial intelligence (AI) chips, The Information reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27, citing someone familiar with the matter. Reuters, which carried the report, said no financial terms or other details were disclosed. OpenAI declined to comment.

That looks like bad news for Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA). OpenAI is one of the largest buyers of Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs) , and Alphabet's (NASDAQ:GOOGL)(NASDAQ:GOOG) Google builds the best-known alternative, its tensor processing units (TPUs).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Yet the stock hardly moved. Nvidia shares were little changed on Wednesday morning as of this writing, around $218. Tuesday's close of $217.94 had already put them about 9% off their Oct. 6 record of $239.24.

Should investors sell Nvidia stock on the news? I'd argue the report says less than its headline implies. It describes OpenAI adding chips while Nvidia can't make enough of its own.

Image source: Nvidia.

A plan, not a purchase order

OpenAI has used Google's chips before. Reuters reported in June 2025 that OpenAI had begun renting Google's TPUs, but OpenAI said days later that it was just in early testing with some of them and had no plans to deploy them at scale. What's new is ownership: OpenAI would reportedly buy the chips rather than rent time on them, and Google started selling TPUs straight to some customers this year.

Notably, the report, as Reuters relayed it, didn't say OpenAI is cutting back on Nvidia. And OpenAI's Nvidia plans are big.

In August, Nvidia said OpenAI's current and planned commitments add up to around 12 gigawatts of Nvidia computing, and it put the opportunity, including a possible increase to about 16 gigawatts, at about $600 billion through 2030. The same month, Nvidia agreed to guarantees capped at $105 billion that cover parts of the lease and power payments at an Ohio data center campus OpenAI will lease. In return, the campus will house only Nvidia's AI hardware, with limited exceptions.

That's a strange deal for a customer planning to leave.

How much does OpenAI matter to Nvidia?

Nvidia doesn't put a number on it. Its latest quarterly filing, covering the fiscal 2027 second quarter (the period ended July 26, 2026), says only that it estimates one unnamed "AI research and deployment company" contributed "a meaningful amount" of its revenue by buying cloud services from Nvidia's customers.

Story Continues

Yes, $600 billion through 2030 is a lot of money, even for a company that brought in $96.2 billion in revenue in its fiscal second quarter, up 106% from a year earlier. If OpenAI shifted a big part of those plans to Google's chips, Nvidia's sales could take a noticeable hit.

But the report doesn't say that. And today, Nvidia's bigger issue is making enough product.

Nvidia can't make enough chips

On Nvidia's August earnings call, chief financial officer Colette Kress said Nvidia expects revenue to climb around 70% in fiscal 2028 (its year through January 2028). She called it a supply-constrained outlook, adding that customers' forecasts point to Nvidia's growth doubling next year.

"Our demand is much higher than that," CEO Jensen Huang said on that same call, after explaining that Nvidia has supply for around 70% growth.

Showing how hard Nvidia is chasing supply, its commitments to suppliers shot up to $279 billion as of the end of fiscal Q2 from $119 billion three months before and $95.2 billion in late January. Management said the latest rise came largely from memory purchases. In other words, the commitments almost tripled over two quarters, and the increase accelerated sharply in the second of them. That arguably shows Nvidia expects demand to run far beyond what it can make now.

In a market like that, chips OpenAI doesn't buy from Nvidia probably go to the next customer in line.

Sure, that might change when supply catches up to demand. Oracle said Tuesday it plans to offer Google's chips on its cloud starting in 2027, and more options could eventually weigh on Nvidia's pricing. But Kress said she expects supply to stay a bottleneck at least through the end of fiscal 2028.

Nvidia stock is priced for a slowdown

With shares around $218, investors pay about 14 times the earnings analysts, on average, forecast for Nvidia's fiscal 2028. Alphabet's shares, by comparison, cost about 21 times its expected 2027 earnings. At this discount, I think investors already assume Nvidia's growth will slow sharply and rivals will gain share.

Is the report a reason to sell Nvidia stock? I don't think so. OpenAI buying Google's chips would matter more when Nvidia can make all the chips its customers want, and management doesn't expect that before fiscal 2028 ends.

I wouldn't sell the stock over a reported plan with no disclosed terms.

news.Title: 外資上週狂買日股1.18兆日圓、扭轉賣超，日債買超驟減逾九成
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】日本財務省週四(29日)公布最新跨境證券投資統計顯示，截至10月24日止當週，外國投資人淨買進日本股票及投資基金持分1兆1,809億日圓，扭轉前一週淨賣出675億日圓的局面，顯示海外資金重新加碼日本股市。不過，外資同期淨買進日本中長期債券僅433億日圓，較前一週修正後的1兆4,543億日圓大幅縮減約97%，反映外資對日本股票與債券的配置出現明顯分化。從股票市場資金動向觀察，外資在10月初一度大幅加碼日股，截至10月10日止當週買超金額達3兆5,455億日圓，隨後一週小幅賣超675億日圓，最新一週再度轉為逾1兆日圓買超，反映海外資金對日本股市的投資意願仍有支撐。然而，單週資金流入並不代表市場已形成持續買超趨勢，後續仍須觀察海外機構投資人對日本企業獲利、利率政策及股市估值的評估。

債券市場方面，外資對日本中長期債券雖維持淨買進，但買超規模由1兆4,543億日圓驟降至433億日圓，顯示資金流入動能顯著放緩。與此同時，外資淨賣出日本短期債券1兆1,817億日圓，抵銷中長期債券買盤後，外資對日本債券整體仍呈淨賣出。由於日本公債殖利率走高、日銀貨幣政策正常化及全球利率變動持續影響投資配置，外資對不同期限債券的需求差異，仍是觀察日本金融市場的重要指標。

日本投資人海外配置則呈現買股、賣債格局。截至10月24日止當週，日本投資人淨買進海外股票及投資基金持分2,881億日圓，高於前一週的1,283億日圓；海外中長期債券淨賣出926億日圓，較前一週賣超1,605億日圓收斂，顯示日資持續調整海外債券部位，但減碼幅度有所縮小。市場將持續關注日本公債殖利率、日銀利率政策及全球金融市場變化，評估海外資金回流日股與日本投資人調整跨境資產配置的趨勢能否延續。

news.Title: Alphabet, Microsoft earnings reveal surging AI demand as spending soars
news.Content:
Alphabet and Microsoft reported surging demand for artificial intelligence in their quarterly earnings Wednesday, and the technology giants continue pouring billions of dollars into the infrastructure needed to support the growing industry.

Google parent Alphabet expects capital expenditures to increase significantly in 2027 after projecting between $195 billion and $205 billion in spending this year, underscoring the enormous costs associated with expanding AI infrastructure.

Alphabet reported third-quarter revenue of $127.6 billion, up 25% from a year earlier, while Microsoft posted fiscal first-quarter revenue of $92.3 billion, an increase of 19%.

San Francisco Startup Offered $20 An Hour To Walk Robot Dogs For Ai Training: Report

Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, a 103% increase from the previous year, while Microsoft's Azure cloud business reported revenue growth of 48%.

"Our AI infrastructure and solutions are the major drivers for Cloud growth, and our customers see us as the leading provider here, so there's huge demand," Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai said during the company's earnings call.

Read On The Fox Business App

"We are working hard to bring more capacity online to meet this long-term demand."

Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts To 60,000 Employees As Tech Giant Reshapes Its Workforce

Alphabet spent approximately $51.4 billion on capital expenditures during the third quarter, more than double the amount spent a year earlier, with much of the investment directed toward technical infrastructure supporting its AI and cloud businesses.

Chief Financial Officer Anat Ashkenazi also warned that Google Cloud could face near-term margin pressure as the company relies on third-party computing capacity to meet demand.

Microsoft similarly highlighted strong demand for AI services , with Microsoft Cloud revenue rising 30% to $63.9 billion.

The company's commercial remaining performance obligation, a measure of contracted future revenue across its commercial businesses that has not yet been recognized, climbed 73% to $677 billion.

The results underscore the challenge facing both companies as they seek to capitalize on growing AI demand while managing the substantial costs of building the infrastructure needed to support it.

下，預期大盤呈現高檔震盪格局。操作建議保持適度資金彈性，避免過度槓桿，

逢回布局，AI概念及業績題材股，搭配短期營收動能股，長線追蹤族群：台積電

及先進封測、半導體設備、PCB供應鏈、光傳輸、散熱、連接器、貨櫃散裝、塑

news.Title: OpenAI擬向Google採購AI晶片，台積電CoWoS與HBM供應壓力升高
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-10-29 08:33:20 數位內容中心 發佈

- OpenAI據報計劃向Google採購AI晶片，並透過Google Cloud部署最先進模型，市場焦點再度回到算力供應分配[1]。

- 當前最直接的瓶頸仍在先進封裝CoWoS與HBM記憶體供給。台積電傳出擬調漲CoWoS報價、拉長交期，HBM價格也預期大幅走升，短期供給難以同步放大[2][3]。

- 接下來，市場將觀察台積電CoWoS產能釋出進度，以及中國HBM良率是否如業界預期改善；同時，OpenAI採購規模、交期與封裝形式，也將牽動供應壓力如何在供應鏈間轉移[2][4][1]。

2026-10-28，科技媒體The Information引述知情人士報導，OpenAI正計劃向Google採購人工智慧晶片，並已與Google就透過Google Cloud提供最先進模型達成合作意向；報導未披露交易金額或交付規模，雙方也未置評[1]。消息傳出後，資本市場與供應端迅速反應，投資人與業界焦點再度回到最核心的問題：誰能提供足夠算力。

資金轉向記憶體與封裝族群

10月28日，市場資金明顯轉向記憶體與封裝相關族群，外資與投信大舉買超記憶體、台積電及封裝供應鏈個股。報導點名南亞科、台積電與華邦電獲單日巨量買超，顯示投資人正提前卡位可能的漲價與備貨題材[5][2]。同時，市場傳出台積電擬將CoWoS封裝報價調高最高20%，並把設備交期拉長至約8個月；若消息屬實，封裝成本與交期變化將立刻成為下游廠商必須面對的變數[2]。

CoWoS與HBM短期都難解壓

供應緊張並非一時形成。先進封裝CoWoS產能持續吃緊，雖然台積電與外部封測廠都在擴產，但產能釋放需要時間，封裝良率、載板與中介層等協同問題，也讓實際有效產能難以快速提升，訂單已有外溢至聯電、Amkor與其他OSAT業者的跡象[6][7][2]。法人估計，台積電CoWoS月產能正朝逾13萬片推進，長期目標上看20萬片，但短期供需缺口仍須由外溢廠分擔[2][6]。

記憶體方面，研究機構預估HBM供應吃緊恐將延續，明年HBM綜合平均售價（ASP）估計年增約121%。價格大幅上揚，已迫使終端廠調整記憶體搭載策略，業界也開始討論以降低HBM堆疊高度，例如從12hi降為8hi，來局部紓解成本與供給壓力[3][8]。另有陸方消息稱，國產HBM良率可能在半年內由約25%提升至40%至50%；若能實現，將有助擴充可用供給，但良率改善能否迅速轉化為出貨、進一步壓低ASP，仍有不確定性[4]。

產業一線的回應也反映出供給瓶頸。中華精測總經理黃水可在10月法說指出，多家大型IC設計客戶反映，當前最大挑戰在於產能跟不上成長速度。該公司今年HPC營收占比已由第二季的56.3%升至第三季的65.9%，並推動公司對明年營收近五成成長的預期，顯示AI相關拉貨壓力已一路傳導至封裝、HBM與先進製程等上游節點[9]。

全球主要雲端服務供應商（CSP）資本支出仍居高不下，九大CSP未來一到兩年的投資規模預期持續擴張，成為推升AI伺服器、GPU與HBM長期需求的重要背景；同時，GPU租賃價格與二級市場走勢也反映算力資產稀缺，進一步驅使雲端業者與AI實驗室尋找更多供應來源[10][11][12]。

新訂單只會把壓力往上游推

若OpenAI確實向Google大量採購晶片，短期對輝達（NVIDIA）的直接需求衝擊仍難量化，但任何新增系統訂單，都會一路傳導至台積電CoWoS與HBM等上游節點，放大既有缺口或改變分配方式[1][2]。系統整合端的反應已見端倪：ODM廠廣達表示，AI伺服器訂單能見度旺到2028年，顯示CSP及大型客戶拉貨動能仍在，眼前更像是供給受限，而非需求降溫[13][11]。

供應鏈目前主要沿兩條路徑調節壓力：一是台積電持續擴產，並由外溢廠承接部分訂單，縮小CoWoS缺口；二是下游廠商在HBM價格與良率不確定下，調整晶片設計與採購策略，包括降低HBM堆疊、改用不同記憶體組合，或加速自研ASIC，以避開高昂記憶體成本與封裝供給瓶頸[6][3][14]。此外，若OpenAI採購案包含完整系統封裝（如CoWoS套餐），短期壓力可能只是從GPU封裝端轉移到載板、封裝良率及HBM供給上[3][2]。

目前仍有幾項不確定因素待市場驗證：OpenAI採購規模、交期與是否包含系統整合細節尚未明朗，HBM價格走勢與CoWoS交期能否在短期內被供應鏈吸收，以及監管與地緣政治（如出口管制）對跨境算力採購的影響，都將左右供給如何重新分配[3][2][15][16]。

台積電能否如市場預期加快CoWoS月產能爬升，以及中國HBM廠良率提升能否真正轉化為可出貨供給，將影響這輪算力爭奪中，哪些廠商能先緩解壓力、哪些環節仍會持續卡關[2][4]。

news.Title: Microsoft and Alphabet Just Reported Earnings, Putting the AI Boom to the Test
news.Content:
Two tech behemoths -- Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) -- reported earnings today. Both showed strong cloud growth, but the market is treating them very differently. Microsoft shares popped after hours while Alphabet stock sank. Why?

I think a big part of the answer is how each plans to pay for the massive outlays both have planned.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Cloud growth accelerated at both companies

Microsoft beat Wall Street's targets with sales up 19%, reaching $92.3 billion. GAAP -- generally accepted accounting principles -- earnings per share (EPS) came in at $4.92. Adjusted EPS was $4.89, above the roughly $4.72 the Street expected. Azure, its cloud platform, grew 48%, reaching $33.17 billion in revenue.

Alphabet's cloud growth was even stronger than Microsoft's: 103% growth for the unit, earning $11.1 billion in operating income on $30.7 billion in sales. Overall, sales jumped 25%, reaching $127.6 billion, slightly missing estimates, while GAAP EPS actually fell from $2.87 to $2.12. Search and YouTube ads also underperformed.

Alphabet's cash flow is the real problem

Some of Alphabet's EPS drop can be explained by an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, but even if you remove this -- worth $0.55 per share -- the earnings still came in well below what Wall Street was looking for.

While it's not a great look, I think the real issue the market is reacting to is the company's cash picture. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditures (capex), up from $24.0 billion a year ago. Operating cash flow -- the cash the actual business generated -- was $42.3 billion. That left free cash flow (FCF) -- the money left after paying for its capex investments -- at negative $9.1 billion. That's worse than the negative $5.9 billion the company reported last quarter.

During the quarter, Alphabet raised $28.7 billion through senior unsecured notes and $12.4 billion from selling stock. Long-term debt has grown from $46.5 billion at the end of 2025 to $125.1 billion.

Alphabet said its capex guidance for 2026 holds -- $195 billion to $205 billion -- but said it expects capex in 2027 to "increase significantly."

Microsoft is still paying its own way

Microsoft, on the other hand, is still FCF positive, though like Alphabet, that figure is moving in the wrong direction. The company reported FCF of $18.63 billion, down 27% year over year, after $39.37 billion in cash capital spending. Its broader capex figure, which includes finance leases, was $45.2 billion.

Story Continues

CFO Amy Hood said on July's earnings call that the company expects to stay free-cash-flow positive for its current fiscal year, though capex is expected to expand. On that call, she also said demand for its cloud services was running ahead of supply.

The bottom line

Microsoft at this point has a much healthier cushion in its quarterly cash flow -- more room to keep spending while it waits for those investments to pay off. Alphabet is increasingly asking lenders and shareholders to help cover the bill.

Obviously, the growth is hard to argue with, but I still think the jury is out on whether this bet will pay off for both companies. Costs are climbing, and I'm concerned the math won't pencil out long term.

KLA Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in KLA Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

KLA reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion , up 13% sequentially and 29% year over year, with a company-record 46.1% operating margin and earnings above guidance.

AI infrastructure demand is driving strong growth in leading-edge logic, memory and advanced packaging. KLA expects advanced-packaging process-control revenue to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, up more than 70% year over year.

KLA projected December-quarter revenue of about $4.7 billion and raised its 2026 wafer-equipment market estimate to the mid-$150 billion range, while expecting the market to exceed $200 billion in 2027. China's share of revenue is expected to decline to the low-20% range in 2027.

3 AI Winners, 3 Very Different Paths to Higher Margins

KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC) reported record September-quarter revenue of $4.14 billion, exceeding the midpoint of its guidance range as demand for process-control equipment remained strong across leading-edge foundry, logic, memory and advanced-packaging applications tied to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

President and Chief Executive Officer Rick Wallace said revenue rose on continued investment in AI-related semiconductor capacity and growing process-control requirements for advanced devices and packaging. The company also projected December-quarter revenue of approximately $4.7 billion, plus or minus $200 million, signaling an acceleration in growth during the second half of calendar 2026.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

Bearish Pressure Is Building Around These 3 Stocks

"KLA's performance in the quarter was supported by continued strength in leading-edge foundry logic related to AI infrastructure investments and increasing process control intensity across leading-edge devices and advanced packaging," Wallace said.

September-quarter results

Revenue increased 13% sequentially and 29% year over year to $4.14 billion. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.22, while GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.18, both above the midpoint of company guidance.

Gross margin was 62.7%.

Operating margin rose 240 basis points sequentially to a company-record 46.1%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses were $688 million, including $395 million in research and development and $293 million in selling, general and administrative expenses.

Net income was $1.60 billion, while GAAP net income was $1.55 billion.

Cash flow from operations totaled $1.53 billion, and free cash flow was $1.34 billion.

Story Continues

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

Analysts Just Raised Price Targets On These 3 Semiconductor Equipment Stocks

KLA ended the quarter with $4.7 billion in cash equivalents and marketable securities and $5.95 billion in debt.

Services revenue reached $850 million, up 14% from a year earlier. Wallace said the increase reflected a larger installed base, more complex systems and customer focus on tool performance, productivity and availability amid high system utilization.

Advanced packaging and AI demand

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

The company said advanced packaging is becoming more important to AI infrastructure expansion as packaging roadmaps incorporate more sophisticated wafer-front-end processes. KLA expects revenue from advanced-packaging process-control systems to reach approximately $1.1 billion in calendar 2026, representing growth of more than 70% year over year.

Wallace said that growth rate would be nearly twice the growth rate of the advanced-packaging market. In response to analyst questions, Chief Financial Officer Bren Higgins said KLA expects its packaging business to continue growing faster than the market in 2027, with demand increasingly moving toward higher-sensitivity inspection systems as hybrid bonding and other advanced packaging processes expand.

KLA also expects strong memory-related demand. For the December quarter, foundry and logic are forecast to account for about 60% of Semiconductor Process Control Systems revenue from semiconductor customers, while memory is expected to account for approximately 40%. Within memory, DRAM is expected to represent about 84% and NAND about 16%.

Wallace said process-control intensity is rising in DRAM as customers seek higher yields and meet more stringent performance expectations, particularly for advanced memory products. Higgins added that some DRAM products now have process-control intensity comparable with leading-edge logic, aided by greenfield fab investment and demand for high-bandwidth memory.

Industry outlook and capacity investments

KLA raised its estimate for the calendar 2026 wafer-equipment market, including advanced packaging, to approximately the mid-$150 billion range. Higgins said customers are increasing long-term investment plans despite fab-space limitations and that KLA's sales funnel visibility is "unprecedented," supported by new fab investments from a broad customer base.

For calendar 2027, the company expects the wafer-equipment market to exceed $200 billion. Higgins said KLA anticipates sequential revenue growth over the next several quarters, with a more linear progression than the sharp second-half increase anticipated in 2026.

The company said it has been working with supply-chain partners for the past year to expand capacity, particularly for long-lead-time components such as optics. Higgins said average lead times are about 12 months, with some Gen4 and Gen5 product lines taking longer.

KLA is investing in manufacturing, service, engineering and applications staffing, as well as factory capacity. Higgins said capital expenditures should trend higher over the next several years, estimating annual spending of roughly $600 million to $800 million. He noted that a significant land purchase in India for a new campus was a major contributor to the quarter's capital spending.

Management said supply availability had constrained shipments during the first half of 2026, but incremental capacity is now coming online. Wallace also noted that customers can face their own constraints, including delays in clean-room construction, materials and power availability.

Margins, China and December outlook

KLA forecast December-quarter gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, and operating expenses of approximately $710 million. Higgins said persistently elevated memory costs for system image-processing requirements remain a margin headwind, though the company is working to reduce memory usage in its systems, lower product costs and capture value-based pricing on new capabilities.

For the December quarter, KLA expects non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.44, plus or minus $0.11, and GAAP diluted EPS of $1.41, plus or minus $0.11. The company's forecast assumes approximately 1.306 billion fully diluted shares, other expense of about $25 million and a planning tax rate of 14.5%.

On China, Higgins said the country's revenue contribution is expected to decline as a percentage of total sales despite modest growth in absolute terms. He expects China to represent roughly 27% to 29% of revenue in the fourth quarter and to fall to the low-20% range in calendar 2027, as wafer-equipment spending outside China grows more rapidly.

About KLA (NASDAQ:KLAC)

KLA Corporation (NASDAQ: KLAC) develops process control, inspection and yield management solutions for the semiconductor and other advanced manufacturing industries. Its technologies help manufacturers identify defects, measure critical dimensions and monitor production processes to improve quality, reliability and manufacturing efficiency.

The company's product portfolio includes wafer and reticle inspection systems, metrology and measurement tools, defect review and classification systems, and software for analyzing manufacturing data.

news.Title: Google Cloud Revenue Just Grew 103%, so Why Is the Stock Falling?
news.Content:
Amid uncertainty about the future of artificial intelligence (AI), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL) (NASDAQ:GOOG) sought to address investor fears when the company reported its quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

What became immediately apparent is that while relentless demand for AI continues to drive rapid cloud growth, Alphabet is investing heavily to capitalize on that opportunity at hand. Investors viewed falling profits as the canary in the coal mine -- but the devil is in the details.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Partly cloudy

For the third quarter, Alphabet's revenue jumped 25% year over year (15% in constant currency) to $127.6 billion. The company's operating margin ticked higher to 32% from 31%, driving operating income up 30% to $40.6 billion. Unfortunately, diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 dropped 26%, but that requires context -- more on that later.

Analysts' consensus estimates called for revenue of $127.9 billion and EPS of $3.01, so Alphabet failed to meet Wall Street's expectations on both counts.

Google search and the related advertising represent the vast majority of Alphabet's revenue. Investors have expressed concerns that broad advances in AI could siphon away advertising revenue, but those fears appear overdone -- at least for now. Google's search revenue climbed 12% year over year, partially offset by weakness at YouTube, which grew about 9%. In all, Google ad revenue grew 11%.

Speaking of AI, Google's cloud results have become of particular interest to investors, as they are viewed as a proxy for its AI success -- and business is booming. Google Cloud revenue soared 103% year over year to $30.7 billion and marked an acceleration from 82% cloud growth in Q2.

CEO Sundar Pichai noted the cloud results were "powered by huge demand for our AI infrastructure and AI solutions." He went on to say the company was seeing strong demand for Google's flagship Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) -- its homegrown AI-centric semiconductors.

Most telling was the segment's operating margins, which climbed to 36.2%, up from 23.7% in the prior-year quarter and 35.6% in Q2. This shows that Google Cloud is leveraging its assets and driving greater profits.

Given the magnitude of its cloud growth, it should come as no surprise that Alphabet is increasing investment in its cloud and AI. The company expects capital expenditures (capex) spending of roughly $200 billion in 2026, before climbing to $300 billion in 2027. Alphabet's heavy capex spending is weighing on its cash generation, with free cash flow of -$9.1 billion.

Story Continues

The devil is in the details

Alphabet stock took it on the chin, falling as much as 11% in after-hours trading. Investors focused primarily on declining profits, as EPS fell 26%. However, that stands in stark contrast to the company's increasing operating income, which rose 32%. So what gives?

The answer is found in Alphabet's other income and expense line. The company's portfolio of equity investments, which includes Space Exploration Technologies , aka SpaceX, and more than two dozen others -- declined in value in the third quarter. These investments lost $8.2 billion in all, compared to gains of nearly $12.8 billion in the prior year quarter. That represented a hit to the bottom line of nearly $21 billion. Without that swing, Alphabet's net income would have increased by 35%.

Despite the stock price plunge in after-hours trading, the evidence is clear. Google Cloud grew 103%, illustrating that its AI and cloud strategy is paying off. And Alphabet is selling for just 16 times earnings -- near the stock's lowest multiple ever .

That's why Alphabet stock is a screaming buy.

news.Title: Global stocks hold gains after Fed decision, oil prices rise
news.Content:
By Chris Prentice and Amanda Cooper

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 28 (Reuters) - Global stocks and major Wall Street indexes gained on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, as expected, and oil prices rose on renewed concerns over supply disruptions.

In a 10-2 decision, the US central bank said it ‌would maintain its benchmark interest rate within the current 3.75%-4.00% range.

The Fed upgraded its assessment of the economy while acknowledging inflation "remains elevated." After the release, ‌Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters the central bank has made clear its willingness and readiness to act.

US Treasury yields gave up gains briefly after Warsh's comments. [US/]

Spot gold prices advanced in choppy trade. [GOL/]

MSCI's gauge of stocks ​across the globe rose 4.29 points, or 0.38%, to 1,134.03.

On Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI rose 97.53 points, or 0.19%, to 52,475.10, the S&P 500 .SPX gained 21.37 points, or 0.28%, to 7,743.97 and the Nasdaq Composite .IXIC gained 72.04 points, or 0.27%, to 26,549.85.

The pan-European STOXX 600 index rose 0.07%.

MORE EXPECTED FROM CENTRAL BANKS

The Fed's decision "reflects the continued balancing act between inflation concerns and an economy and employment situation that have remained relatively resilient," said Charlie Wise, head of global research at TransUnion in Chicago.

Earlier, market moves had been mostly modest ahead ‌of the Fed decision, outside Asia.

New Zealand's central bank surprised ⁠investors by leaving interest rates on hold, contrary to expectations for a hike, while the Bank of Canada raised rates for the first time in three years.

The European Central Bank and Bank of Japan are expected to issue policy decisions this week as well.

Traders' attention will ⁠also turn to Thursday's US Personal Consumption Expenditures data, which could offer further insight into the trajectory of monetary policy.

Financial markets are pricing in an 85.0% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December meeting, up from 78.3% on Tuesday, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"While the September dot plot suggests just one more hike, another increase in energy prices or further strong ​data ​prints could bring additional tightening into play next year," said Kay Haigh, head of fixed income and ​liquidity solutions at Goldman Sachs Asset Management in New York.

AI RALLY'S ‌LATEST TEST

Technology giants Alphabet and Microsoft reported earnings after the close. Microsoft shares slightly extended gains after beating quarterly cloud revenue estimates.

Story Continues

Meanwhile, Alphabet's heavy spending drove a bigger-than-expected cash burn, sending shares lower after the bell.

A series of AI-related funding announcements from Meta, SpaceX and Broadcom this week has once again tested the market's willingness to pay for further building, though Anthropic's filing for an initial public offering showed results that many investors regarded as stronger than expected, providing support.

CENTRAL BANKS IN THE SPOTLIGHT

Earlier on Wednesday, the Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised investors by keeping interest rates at 2.75% in a narrow vote, sending the kiwi down 1%.

"Today's decision shows the RBNZ is willing to surprise markets, ‌a reminder that central banks do not take orders from markets," Carol Kong, a currency strategist ​at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said.

In the UK, finance minister John Healey delivered a cautious first budget, one ​that prioritised stability in the bond market over the kind of big spending ​moves that Andy Burnham talked about when he became prime minister. Britain's stocks, bonds and currency barely reacted to the statement, in which ‌he pledged to stick to fiscal rules, while accepting a smaller ​fiscal cushion due to rising energy prices and ​borrowing costs.

The pound reversed earlier losses and was last up 0.17%.

Election results in Israel showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc performing more strongly than expected, but still falling short of a parliamentary majority.

In commodities, oil prices rose after an attack on a refinery in Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest crude exporter, renewed ​concerns around the risks to supply in the Middle East. [O/R]

Brent ‌futures added 1% to finish at $115.32 per barrel, while US crude rose 3% to settle at $102.78.

US gold futures for December delivery settled 0.6% lower at $4,051.60 ​per ounce. Spot gold was up 0.27% at $4,070.28 an ounce.

(Additional reporting by Saeed Azhar in New York, Suzanne McGee, and Rae Wee in Singapore; ​Editing by Kate Mayberry, Toby Chopra, Keith Weir, Colin Barr, Nick Zieminski and Aurora Ellis)

news.Title: Microsoft earnings live: Microsoft beats Q1 expectations on top and bottom line on AI growth
news.Content: Microsoft ( MSFT ) reported its first quarter earnings after the bell Wednesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines. Microsoft stock rose more than 4% on the news. For the quarter, Microsoft saw earnings per share (EPS) of $4.89 on revenue of $92.28 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $4.73 on revenue of $90.63 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $4.13 and revenue of $77.6 billion in the same period last year. Q1 marks the first quarter of Microsoft's new segment structure . The Agents and Infra segment includes the revenue from Microsoft's Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud services, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, and frontier and support services. The Devices and Consumer segment includes sales tied to Microsoft's search and advertising businesses, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices. Agents and Infra revenue climbed to $76.8 billion, ahead of expectations of $75.6 billion, with Azure sales climbing 48% to $33.17 billion up from $22.38 billion in the same period last year. Devices and Consumer sales totaled $15.5 billion. Wall Street was looking for $15 billion. Capital expenditures, including leases, topped $39.37 billion, less than the $45.93 billion that analysts were anticipating. Microsoft spent about $39 billion, up from $19 billion, not counting leases. Both came in below Wall Street's estimates, per Bloomberg estimates. Microsoft's spending is paying off faster in the market's eyes. Azure revenue grew 48%. Alphabet burned about $9 billion in free cash flow for a second straight quarter and bought back no stock. news.Title: Notes on FOMC Decision and Earnings After the Close
news.Content:
Major stock market indexes finished in the green today, bolstered somewhat by the expected "no move" decided by the Fed at its latest Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which concluded today. Volatility picked up on the news headline and subsequent press conference with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. The Dow was up +71 points, the Nasdaq +72 and the S&P 500 +21 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 Index gained 6 points on the regular trading session.

Two Dissents as Fed Keeps Rates Unchanged

The FOMC today delivered the expected headline: "No Change to Fed Funds Rate." In a 10-2 vote, the Fed decided to keep interest rates at their +3.75-4.00% range. Only Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack dissented — they voted for a quarter-point raise to +4.00-4.25%. "Resilient," "strong" and "robust" words used to describe the U.S. economy — and in fewer than 200 words altogether.

The statement also cited inflation as being "elevated," although the "accumulation of information will help the Committee determine its policy stance… to the +2% (inflation) goal…" That's about as close to "guidance" investors have gotten from the Fed this time around. In his presser following the statement release, Warsh did say that, while the FOMC will again hold eight meetings next year, only six of these would decide on monetary policy.

Earnings Reports at a Glance: MSFT, GOOGL & More

Microsoft MSFT posted strong fiscal Q1 numbers this afternoon — a day after the company said 60K in the tech giant's workforce are eligible for severance packages. This suggests a new round of job cuts, much like Meta META, Amazon AMZN and others had reported recently. (Spared will be those jobs in Data Center, Cybersecurity, etc.)

Earnings of $4.89 per share rose +19% year over year — higher than the $4.70 per share expected and $4.13 reported in the year-ago quarter. Revenues came in at $92.3 billion, above the $90.58 billion anticipated at +21% year over year. Shares are up +4% in late trading.

Google parent Alphabet GOOGL missed estimates on both top and bottom lines in its Q3 report after Wednesday's close, with earnings of $2.12 per share on revenues of $111.2 billion (ex-TAC; $127.6 billion with TAC not taken out). Cloud gained +103% year over year to $30.7 billion in the quarter. Services were led by Search, up another +12%, with query growth its highest in five years. This is only the second earnings miss for GOOGL in five years, and shares fell -7.5% immediately after.

Speaking of earnings misses, ServiceNow NOW posted its first-ever earnings miss since Zacks began tracking the company in 2014: $1.00 per share versus expectations of $1.02. Revenues, on the other hand, outpaced estimates — $4.107 billion in the quarter, up from an expected $4.09 billion. Even with a new OpenAI deal announced today, ServiceNow shares plummeted -16% on the earnings news.

Ford Motor Co. F rolled over expectations on both top and bottom lines this afternoon, with earnings beating the Zacks consensus by a solid dime to $0.49 per share on $49.5 billion in quarterly sales. In truth, these were pretty low bars to get over — both earnings and sales were expected to trail last year's quarter. A harsh $4 billion loss on Ford's Model e, however, dampened the proceedings, and shares are down -1.9% in late trading.

news.Title: Meta Just Priced a Stock Sale at $625 a Share. I'd Consider Buying at the Same Price.
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) just asked investors for lots of money. The social media giant priced 40 million Class A shares at $625 apiece on Oct. 26, a $25 billion sale. It also priced 250 million depositary shares of mandatory convertible preferred stock at $50 each, worth another $12.5 billion.

All told, Meta is raising about $37.5 billion in new equity, after spending $26.2 billion buying back its own stock in 2025. And the stock trades near $625 as I write this, over 20% below its all-time closing high of $790, set in August 2025.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But is the cost of all the new shares worth what the money buys? I think the cost is lower than the $37.5 billion number makes it look.

Image source: Getty Images.

A raise in two parts

Meta won't get the common stock money right away. Under forward sale agreements with Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs, it issues the new shares and collects the roughly $24.9 billion in net proceeds once the agreements settle, which Meta expects by Nov. 19, 2027.

The preferred stock pays a 6.5% annual dividend, or around $813 million a year. In August 2029, each depositary share converts into 0.0681 to 0.0800 Meta shares, based on the stock's price then, before adjustment for a planned Class C stock dividend.

Meta plans to use the cash for general corporate purposes. But its Oct. 21 earnings release said the investment needed "to compete, sustain growth, expand infrastructure, and pursue new strategic initiatives" during the industry's move to artificial intelligence (AI) "is significant."

What does it cost shareholders?

Meta had around 2.56 billion Class A and Class B shares on Sept. 30. The 40 million new common shares, plus the 17 million to 20 million shares the preferred stock could convert into, would add around 2.2% to 2.3% to that count.

That's on top of a slower climb. Without buybacks since the third quarter of 2025, Meta's average number of shares outstanding has grown in four straight quarters, by 8 million to 9 million shares every time. It hit 2,552 million in the third quarter of 2026, up around 1.4% year over year.

Around 2.3% more shares means each share's piece of future profits shrinks by a little over 2%. At around $625, the stock trades at about 18 times expected 2027 earnings. With those profits spread across the higher share count, the price-to-earnings ratio would still be under 19 times earnings -- even if the new money never added a dollar of profit.

Story Continues

Spending has outrun the cash

In the third quarter, Meta spent around $2.1 billion more on capital expenditures (including principal payments on finance leases) than its operations took in. A year before, operations covered the spending with around $10.6 billion left over. And management expects 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta has also borrowed heavily, raising about $29.9 billion of long-term debt in the fourth quarter of 2025 and $24.9 billion more in the second quarter of 2026. By Sept. 30, long-term debt had hit $80.9 billion, almost matching Meta's $82.5 billion of cash and marketable securities.

I'd say selling stock makes more sense for Meta today than adding more debt.

And the spending seems to be paying off in the core business. Advertising revenue climbed 26% year over year to $63.1 billion in the third quarter. The same release said its AI investments "are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue."

This might not be the last raise. Meta also plans an at-the-market program to sell around $60 billion more stock after its new Class C shares start trading, but it hasn't set the timing. At today's price, that would be close to another 4% of the company.

Big buyers paid close to today's price

Meta priced the common stock less than 1% under the $630.56 last sale price on Oct. 26, after increasing the sale from the $22.5 billion it first announced. Nvidia said it would invest $3 billion in Meta's equity offering.

The preferred buyers gave up some upside. In return for the 6.5% dividend, they take the stock's losses under $625. But they don't share in any gains until Meta passes about $734, about 17.5% over the offering price. These terms suggest they see today's price as a sensible spot to own Meta.

Is Meta stock a buy near $625? I think so. True, giving up a little over 2% of the company costs existing holders something, and the planned $60 billion program might take more. But the cash comes to more than Meta spent on capital expenditures in the third quarter, while its ad sales are still rising more than 20%.

I'd consider buying shares at about the same price Meta's new investors just paid.

news.Title: SK Hynix Just Delivered Great News for Micron Investors
news.Content:
It would be odd to say that investors are too pessimistic about a stock that has tripled this year, but that appears to be the case for Micron (NASDAQ:MU).

Shares of the leading memory chipmaker are up 240% this year, but they're down more than 20% since peaking after Micron's fiscal third-quarter earnings report.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In the months since, investors have hotly debated the sustainability of the memory chip boom, driven by a shortage that has led to sky-high prices. Even as supply-and-demand conditions have tightened since June, investors seem to believe that Micron stock has peaked and that they're better off hedging their bets in anticipation of the cycle's downside.

However, one of the other big three chip companies just reported earnings, and the results and commentary continue to support an extended shortage of memory chips, as Hynix said it expected demand to outpace supply through 2030. Additionally, the company said it was virtually sold out through 2029.

Image source: The Motley Fool.

What the Hynix report showed

Like Micron before it, SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) reported blockbuster results in its third quarter, with revenue up 328% year-over-year and 32% sequentially, showing that the tailwinds in the industry remain strong even from the previous quarter.

Importantly, prices are still going up as the company reported a high 20% sequential increase in average selling prices (ASP) for DRAM chips, which includes the high bandwidth memory (HBM) deployed at AI data centers, and it had mid-20% sequential growth in NAND, which is typically used for data storage.

Hynix also reported 10% sequential DRAM bit growth, a solid increase in volume, while NAND was down slightly.

The company also made a number of predictions beyond demand exceeding supply through 2030, which Micron investors will want to hear.

Management predicted that the global AI data center infrastructure market will expand by 40% annually through 2030, indicating it would quadruple in four years. It also said that memory demand would exceed earlier expectations as AI takes on longer, more complex tasks, driving a surge in compute and data processing.

At the enterprise level, it said that personal AI would drive near-term growth, while physical AI would broaden the scope of demand over the mid- to long-term.

Story Continues

For next year, the company expects DRAM bit growth in the mid-20 % range and NAND growth in the high-teens range, indicating it will benefit from both volume and pricing growth. That's good news for Micron as well, and seems to indicate that analysts are likely underestimating its growth in fiscal 2028, which begins next September.

What it means for Micron

Micron's stock's weak performance in recent months suggests investors expect the memory shortage to be short-lived and that prices will crash as new capacity comes online.

SK Hynix's report should dispel that notion, and it also indicates that the shortages will continue until at least 2030, meaning they could endure beyond four years from now.

Predicting what happens to AI in that period is nearly impossible, as there is a wide range of factors to account for, but one thing that seems likely is that the technology will continue to advance, which implies greater demand for memory. Physical AI, including robots and self-driving cars, is likely to add to memory demand, as will the broader growth of compute demand, which currently exceeds supply.

Like SK Hynix, Micron is entering into long-term contracts with customers to protect itself against any downside in the memory cycle, which should ensure solid profits through next year.

The stock currently trades at a forward P/E of less than 6, and its EPS estimates could easily go up following Hynix's report.

If shortages endure through 2030, Micron will be able to pay back most of its market cap in profits, if not all of it, in that time period, making the stock look attractive at the current price, especially if it ramps up buybacks.

Based on that valuation and SK Hynix's latest comments, investors still seem overly pessimistic about the memory sector.

news.Title: Google stock plunges as Q3 sales fall short of expectations
news.Content:
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) reported its third quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, missing revenue projections on lower-than-anticipated advertising sales, despite Google Cloud growth of 103%.

Google saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 on revenue of 127.58 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS of $3.01 on revenue of $127.93 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs came in at $111.21 billion. Wall Street was anticipating $111.29 billion.

Google's advertising segment saw sales of $82.01 billion versus expectations of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit brought in $30.71 billion. Analysts were projecting revenue of $29.1 billion.

Google stock fell more than 8% on the news.

Google is also burning through its free cash flow, declining from $-5.85 billion in Q2 to -$9.06 billion in Q3.

The results come just hours after the company debuted its latest frontier AI model.

Google said the new model, Gemini 4 Carbon, outpaces even its Gemini 4 Argon, which it released just two weeks ago. The company claimed Carbon also beats out competing models, including OpenAI's ( OPAI.PVT ) GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) Claude Opus 5.5.

According to Google CEO Sundar Pichai, the Gemini app now has more than 1 billion users, making it the fastest-growing app in the company's history.

Investors on Wall Street, meanwhile, have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.

Those fears came into focus last week as traders dumped CoreWeave stock amid questions about the company's massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.

On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.

But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta, thanks to its new Muse AI agent . According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.

If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.
