news.Title: Nvidia faces DOJ antitrust scrutiny over $12.9B Hugging Face deal, Reuters says
news.Content:
Investing.com -- The U.S. Department of Justice is probing NVIDIA Corporation's (NASDAQ:NVDA) planned $12.93 billion acquisition of open-source artificial intelligence hub Hugging Face, folding questions about the transaction into a broader, multi-year antitrust investigation into the chipmaker's business practices, Reuters reported. Shares of Nvidia slipped 1.7% in Wednesday trading following the news, as market participants weighed the regulatory headwinds facing the world's premier computing firm.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Antitrust enforcers have zeroed in on whether absorbing Hugging Face would allow Nvidia to seize control of a crucial distribution channel for AI models and software, according to two people familiar with the matter. Nvidia, which anticipates closing the transaction in the first half of 2027, has maintained that the platform will preserve open support across a full spectrum of rival processors, cloud architectures, and software ecosystems.

Beyond the pending Hugging Face buyout, federal investigators are scrutinizing Nvidia's sales tactics, strategic investments, and historical acquisitions to evaluate whether the company has exerted undue commercial pressure on customers. Regulatory questions have targeted Nvidia's prior purchases of workload-orchestration developer Run:ai and supercomputing software firm SchedMD, alongside a 2025 licensing and talent arrangement with chip startup Groq.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Of particular interest to officials is whether Nvidia leveraged its dominant graphics processing units to compel buyers into taking adjacent products, exploring allegations that preferential chip allocations were tied to purchases of its networking equipment and Groq processors. Such practices would signal an effort to fortify a walled ecosystem at a time when rivals such as Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, and Alphabet are expanding their custom silicon initiatives.

The sweeping conduct inquiry originated under the Biden administration and has extended into the Trump presidency, reflecting a staff-led regulatory review that has spanned multiple political cycles. Although President Donald Trump has praised Nvidia's leadership and awarded Chief Executive Jensen Huang the National Medal of Science, there is no indication the White House has intervened, and inquiries do not inevitably lead to formal legal enforcement.

Story Continues

A Justice Department spokesperson declined to address specific matters before the agency, emphasizing that leadership prioritizes domestic superintelligence capabilities while noting that conduct investigations are distinct from routine merger reviews. For investors, the intensifying scrutiny underscores a critical friction point for Nvidia, testing its ability to deploy massive cash reserves toward vertical integration without triggering heightened regulatory resistance.

news.Content:
KLA (KLAC) came out with quarterly earnings of $1.22 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.18 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.88 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +3.39%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this maker of equipment for manufacturing semiconductors would post earnings of $1 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.05, delivering a surprise of +5%.

KLA, which belongs to the Zacks Electronics - Miscellaneous Products industry, posted revenues of $4.14 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 2.20%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $3.21 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

KLA shares have added about 26.5% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 12.8%.

What's Next for KLA?

While KLA has outperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for KLA was favorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to outperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $1.34 on $4.43 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $5.44 on $17.88 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. news.Title: Elon Musk Says Neoclouds Face a "Guppy Level" Death. IREN Is Down 64% From Its High. Is He Talking About This Stock?
news.Content:
SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Tesla CEO Elon Musk recently posted on X that over the past few weeks, debt markets have "almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers". Musk believes that tightening could cause more than 200 neocloud companies -- which mainly provide AI infrastructure services -- to face a "guppy-level death and consolidation" in the near future.

That statement caused many neocloud stocks to plummet. One of the hardest-hit stocks was IREN (NASDAQ: IREN), which trades 64% below its all-time high from last November. Let's see why a tightening debt market could spell trouble for this former market darling.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

What could happen to IREN?

IREN was once an Australian Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) miner called Iris Energy. In 2024, it rebranded as IREN and became a neocloud AI infrastructure company. As IREN, the company allocated all of its capital, logistics, and power infrastructure toward expanding its AI and high-performance computing (HPC) data centers rather than its Bitcoin mining operations.

Today, IREN has a fleet of six operational data centers across four countries. It plans to bring seven additional data centers online in the near future. It plans to increase its capacity from 810 MW today to 4.5 GW over the long term. Its 2026 capacity is already "largely" sold out, and it's in "late-stage discussions" with new customers for a "significant portion" of its 2027 capacity.

IREN has already secured multi-billion-dollar cloud services contracts with Microsoft , Nvidia , and other AI giants. It requires many of those customers to prepay roughly half of the GPU capex, reducing its upfront capital requirements.

From fiscal 2026 (which ended in June) to fiscal 2029, analysts expect its revenue and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) to grow at CAGRs of 177% and 243%, respectively, as it expands its capacity and converts its backlog into revenue.

With an enterprise value of $34.6 billion, IREN trades at just 12 times this year's sales and 19 times its adjusted EBITDA. However, its net losses -- which include interest payments, hardware depreciation, and stock-based compensation excluded from its adjusted EBITDA -- are expected to widen from $703 million in fiscal 2026 to $1.05 billion in fiscal 2029.

Story Continues

That's bad news for a company that ended its latest quarter with $11.6 billion in total liabilities and a high debt-to-equity ratio of 2.8. It's already increased its share count by 78% over the past two years -- and that dilution will worsen as it raises cash with more stock offerings. So while I wouldn't claim that IREN will face a "guppy-level" death, I think it's a risky stock to own if interest rates keep rising and the debt markets get even tighter.

news.Title: Google Q3 sales fall short of expectations, stock plunges
news.Content:
Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) reported its third quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, missing on revenue projections on lower than anticipated advertising sales.

Google saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.12 on revenue of 127.58 billion. Analysts were looking for EPS $3.01 on revenue of $127.93 billion. Revenue excluding traffic acquisition costs came in at $111.21 billion. Wall Street was anticipating $111.29 billion.

Google's advertising segment saw sales of $82.01 billion versus expectations of $83.5 billion, while its cloud unit brought in $30.71 billion. Analysts were projecting revenue of $29.1 billion.

The results come just hours after the company debuted its latest frontier AI model.

Google says the new model called Gemin 4 Carbon outpaces even its Gemini 4 Argon, which it released just two weeks ago. Carbon, the company claims, also beats out competing models including OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5.

Investors on Wall Street, meanwhile, have been vacillating between concern and exuberance about the future of AI and whether hyperscalers' vast investments in the technology will pay off.

Those fears came into focus last week, as traders dumped shares of CoreWeave over questions about its massive debt load, sending large swaths of the market lower.

On Tuesday, Oracle announced that it will be the first company to purchase Google's AI processors for use in its own data centers.

But Google is also facing increasing competition from Meta thanks to its new Muse AI agent . According to Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, 10 million people have set up Muse, with the majority of users accessing the app for shopping.

If Muse continues to expand its user base and gain ground in online sales, it could prove to be a long-term threat to Google.

"Search usage [and] growth is back in focus given Muse launch and challenges Google could face in migrating users to agentic while maintaining strong monetization," Post wrote.

news.Title: SpaceX’s Starlink Just Added 1.6 Million Customers. But That’s Not the Best News
news.Content:
Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX) announced its third-quarter results on Oct. 20, and Wall Street was impressed. The company's revenue of $14.6 billion was up 161% year over year, coming in well ahead of analyst estimates. The company also reported a net profit of $4.4 billion, significantly higher than the year-ago net loss of $1.1 billion. SpaceX's strong performance was partly due to its connectivity segment, and this unit is showing promising signs investors shouldn't ignore.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Starlink did something it rarely does

SpaceX's Starlink business provides satellite-based internet connectivity services through a network of Low Earth Orbit satellites . The company has especially targeted customers in underserved areas, at least so far.

In the third quarter, connectivity revenue increased 69.5% year over year to $5.2 billion. The segment's operating income came in at $2.4 billion, up almost 99% compared to the year-ago period.

Starlink added 1.6 million customers during the period -- compared to the previous quarter -- and ended the third quarter with a total of 13.6 million, up almost 89% compared to the year-ago period.

These are excellent results, but there is more. Starlink's average revenue per user (ARPU) for the quarter was $69. While that decreased from the $83 posted in the prior-year quarter, it increased 4.5% sequentially.

That's significant, since SpaceX itself has warned investors that ARPU would decrease as the space company expands and offers lower-priced plans. This metric does not grow sequentially very often for SpaceX.

Management attributed the recent sequential increase to a favorable customer mix, but this may not carry over to the fourth quarter. Still, it's worth noting that connectivity's operating income grew much faster than revenue. This is perhaps even more important than the sequential increase in ARPU. Starlink requires significant upfront investments to be up and running.

Launching thousands of satellites into space that are capable of serving millions of customers is expensive, but costs decline once the constellation is up and running. To illustrate the point, suppose 10,000 satellites can service 5,000 customers while maintaining decent internet speeds.

Story Continues

If SpaceX has 1,000 customers, the cost of adding 4,000 more customers is relatively small compared to the initial cost of setting up the satellite constellation. There are still expenses to consider, and SpaceX would also need to launch additional satellites to expand its capacity (and replace those that are no longer working).

But this dynamic partly explains why connectivity operating income grew faster than revenue in the third quarter.

The future of Starlink

SpaceX submitted a regulatory application to launch 100,000 of its Starlink V3 satellites into orbit. The company currently has a little over 11,100 mostly older satellites up there. SpaceX's Starlink ambitions could transform the business.

Here are two reasons why. First, Starlink V3 satellites are much more powerful than previous versions and could offer faster speeds to a larger pool of customers. Second, Starlink V3 satellites don't fit into the company's Falcon 9, its current workhorse rocket.

So, the plan to send 100,000 of them into orbit will depend on SpaceX's Starship, its next-gen rocket, the largest ever built, and designed to be fully reusable (Falcon 9 is only partially reusable).

Starship could significantly reduce launch costs for SpaceX. So, the costs of launching 100,000 Starlink V3 satellites may not be as high as it sounds at first. If SpaceX is successful, the company could substantially expand its number of Starlink subscribers and grow Starlink revenue at a good clip.

There is a vast opportunity here for SpaceX. However, the company will have to navigate several potential headwinds, including execution risks for Starship, the rocket central to its ambitions.

SpaceX will also have to overcome regulatory risks. The company could certainly achieve its goal, but there is significant uncertainty, and if several projects fail, the stock could fall significantly. Investors should keep that in mind before initiating a position.

Analysts were projecting EPS of $4.73 on revenue of $90.63 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company saw EPS of $4.13 and revenue of $77.6 billion in the same period last year. Q1 marks the first quarter of Microsoft's new segment structure . The Agents and Infra segment include the revenue from Microsoft's Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud services, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, and frontier and support services. The Devices and Consumer segment includes sales tied to Microsoft's search and advertising businesses, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices. Agents and Infra revenue climbed to $76.8 billion, ahead of expectations of $75.6 billion, with Azure sales climbing 48% to $33.17 billion Devices and Consumer sales came in at $15.5 billion. news.Title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise as Fed holds rates steady, Big Tech earnings loom
news.Content: US stocks edged higher on Wednesday as investors digested the Federal Reserve's 10-2 decision to hold interest rates steady and focus shifted to earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ). The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gained roughly 0.2% and 0.3%, respectively. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed roughly 0.3% Investor attention turned toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, where the Fed voted to keep its funds rate unchanged , despite elevated inflation readings. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook dissented, favoring a rate hike. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh also announced the central bank will have one less policy-setting meeting next year. Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks rose for a third day in a row after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported a 632% year-over-year profit increase. Peeres Micron ( MU ) and Samsung ( 005930.KS ), also gained. Oracle ( ORCL ) shares jumped after the software and cloud computing giant issued a fiscal 2030 revenue outlook of $225 billion, implying 35% annual growth. Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out. Oracle expects capital spending to peak in fiscal 2027 and 2028, in part to build the capacity needed for its cloud and AI businesses. It expects spending to decline in fiscal 2029. Oracle expects to reach positive free cash flow during the second half of its fiscal year 2028. The company set a free cash flow target of more than $30 billion for fiscal year 2029. Though the company is spending heavily now, its projections indicate those investments should translate into substantial cash generation later. Today at 7:05 PM UTC Jared Blikre Bond traders still see more Fed hikes ahead The Fed won't be sitting on its hands for long, says the market. Traders see about an 85% chance that the Fed raises its benchmark rate by a quarter point at its next meeting on Dec. 9, according to Bloomberg data. The data comes from futures contracts that let traders bet on where the Fed sets rates. Those odds are about where they stood Tuesday, before the decision. Further out, traders expect the Fed's rate to climb from about 3.9% now to nearly 4.7% by September 2027. That's about three more quarter-point hikes, slightly more than they expected Tuesday. The Dec. 9 meeting is next. A hike would match what traders already expect. Another hold would mean they've gotten ahead of the Fed. Today at 6:48 PM UTC Ines Ferré Warsh announces changes to FOMC meetings schedule starting next fall Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh announced a change to the FOMC meeting starting next fall. Warsh said eight meetings per year is the right number for the Federal Open Market Committee. But in 2027, one meeting will focus exclusively on broad monetary policy strategy with neither a vote on the Fed's funds rate nor a policy statement. The rest will be regular policy meetings. Warsh also expects that in 2028, policymakers will hold 2 meetings dedicated to strategy and 6 for setting policy. "Getting policy right involves assessing near-term developments at timely, regular, and information-rich intervals," said Warsh. "But it's equally important we reserve time and space as an intellectually diverse group for strategic deliberations for thinking anew about big questions, looking out over longer time horizons," he added. Buy stocks at the end of October, hold them through April, then step aside for the summer. Yale Hirsch found the pattern in 1986. news.Title: 台股大反攻！杜金龍強勢加碼到7成喊：抱緊「這3檔」賺到明年Q1
news.Content:
台股大反攻！加權指數28日狂漲939.35點，收在47,035.58點，不僅重返4萬7千點大關，也重新站回季線。有 「股市老先覺」之稱的資深分析師杜金龍 認為，台股歷經一波大幅修正後，4萬6千點附近已展現支撐力道，隨著護盤買盤進場、籌碼逐步沉澱，年底至明年初的跨年行情值得期待，並點名 台積電（2330）、欣興（3037）、南亞（1303） 3檔個股，成為後續觀察重點。

【46000點築底成功！杜金龍持股水位拉高至7成】

「只要大跌，就是最好的買點！」面對外資今年大舉拋售，許多散戶在震盪中感到恐慌，但資深分析師杜金龍卻展現冷靜思維。他觀察到大盤在 45,676 點附近獲得強烈支撐，且融資短線快速減肥，籌碼面趨於乾淨。眼見底部浮現，杜金龍已順勢將自己的持股水位由 6 成拉高至 7 成多，用實際行動力挺後市反攻。

【三大進場時機曝光 跨年行情上看60000點】

談到這波反攻行情的節奏，杜金龍揭露三大關鍵進場時間點：第一波是大盤大幅拉回時逢低撿便宜；第二波落於美國大選前後；第三波則在台灣選舉前後（約 11 月 27 至 29 日）。他預估自 11 月下旬起台股將全面啟動跨年反彈，行情可望一路熱絡至 2027 年 2 月初甚至 5 月，波浪理論目標價上看 53,000 至 60,000 點，外資甚至喊出 57,000 點高標，輔助驗證大盤多頭格局未變。

【抱緊這3檔潛力股！權王、ABF與塑化接棒攻頂】

要想在這波反攻浪潮中賺到明年第一季，選對核心個股至關重要。杜金龍點名三大值得長期抱緊的指標股：

1. 台積電（2330）： 作為護盤核心工具，杜金龍於 2,420 元與 2,390 元分批逢低抄底。分析 2,380 元附近具備極強支撐，且外資報告評估長線目標價看好至 5,000 元，勝率極高。28日台積電收在 2,425 元，上漲 25 元。後續仍須觀察先進製程需求、AI晶片成長動能及外資買賣超，才能判斷股價能否延續強勢。

2. 欣興（3037） ：ABF 載板族群龍頭，杜金龍於 1,090 元買進卡位。隨著法說會展現亮眼展望，法人目標價上看 1,500 至 1,800 元，產業主流地位可望延伸至 2028 年。

3. 南亞（1303）： 塑化族群爆出歷史天量換手成功，隨著轉投資南電與南亞科帶動每股淨值狂升，外資與本土法人目標價已調升至 400 元以上，為年底補漲重頭戲。

整體而言，台股28日大漲近千點，重新站回4萬7千點，為近期震盪行情注入反攻動能。杜金龍看好4萬6千點附近的支撐力道，也對跨年行情抱持期待；台積電、欣興、南亞則分別代表權值股、ABF載板與塑化族群，後續表現值得追蹤。

news.Title: Meta, Snap Face a Reckoning Over Teen Safety
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms ( NASDAQ:META ) and Snap ( NYSE:SNAP ) are heading into a fresh legal test over allegations that their social media platforms contributed to mental health problems among young users.

Jury selection began Wednesday in Los Angeles in a case involving two plaintiffs who allege that features including autoplay and endless scrolling encouraged compulsive use , contributing to depression, anxiety and eating disorders.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The trial is expected to last several weeks.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram head Adam Mosseri and Snap CEO Evan Spiegel are all expected to testify.

The case is particularly important because it is only the second individual-plaintiff trial involving claims that major social media companies deliberately designed their platforms in ways that encouraged addictive behavior.

In March, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and YouTube negligent and awarded $6 million in damages .

The current case covers claims against Snap from both plaintiffs and claims against Meta from one plaintiff in Mississippi.

The Illinois plaintiff has already settled her claims against Meta, while both plaintiffs reached settlements with TikTok and YouTube before trial.

Meta disputes the allegations and argues that other factors contributed to the plaintiffs' difficulties. The company also points to protections it has introduced for younger users.

Snap says Snapchat differs from traditional algorithmic social media feeds and argues that the allegations mischaracterize both its product design and existing safeguards.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest issue here is not this individual case by itself.

It is the precedent risk .

Thousands of similar lawsuits have been consolidated in Los Angeles Superior Court, meaning the outcomes of early trials could influence settlements, legal strategies and potential liabilities across the broader litigation.

Meta and Snap have argued that Section 230 protects them from liability for user-generated content, but the judge has allowed claims focused on platform design to proceed.

That distinction matters.

If plaintiffs continue finding success by targeting product features rather than content itself, social media companies could face a much broader legal exposure than traditional Section 230 defenses were designed to address.

For investors, the key things to watch are the jury verdict, testimony from senior executives, potential damages, settlement activity and whether additional courts allow similar design-based claims to move forward .

The financial impact remains uncertain.

The legal theory being tested could be much more consequential.

news.Content:

AMD ( NASDAQ:AMD ) is investing $1 billion in Meta Platforms' ( NASDAQ:META ) equity offering as the two companies deepen a partnership spanning CPUs, GPUs, networking, systems and software.

The deal strengthens AMD's relationship with one of the world's largest buyers of AI infrastructure at a time when hyperscalers are spending aggressively to expand compute capacity.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD said its Helios rack-scale systems are already running at Meta , while EPYC processors power Meta's Muse AI agent.

AMD technology also provides Day-0 support for Meta models including Muse Spark Open and Muse Glimmer .

The expanded partnership builds on years of collaboration across AMD EPYC CPUs, Instinct GPUs, Pensando networking and the ROCm software ecosystem.

The companies now plan to work more closely across silicon, software and systems to address the increasingly demanding requirements of operating large-scale AI infrastructure.

That is important because Meta is rapidly expanding its superintelligence infrastructure and needs enormous amounts of compute, networking and power-efficient hardware.

For AMD, deeper integration gives the company another opportunity to challenge Nvidia across more of the AI stack.

The market responded positively.

AMD shares rose more than 3% to $547.61 , while Meta traded down about 1.4% at $621.92.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of this announcement is that AMD is becoming more deeply embedded inside Meta's infrastructure rather than simply selling it individual chips.

The relationship now stretches across processors, accelerators, networking, rack-scale systems and software.

That gives AMD more ways to capture spending as Meta's AI infrastructure expands.

The $1 billion equity investment also strengthens the strategic alignment between the companies.

For investors, the key things to watch are Helios deployment volumes, Instinct GPU adoption, ROCm usage, EPYC penetration and whether Meta commits a larger share of future AI spending to AMD hardware .

AMD still has a long way to go before matching Nvidia's position in AI accelerators.

But winning deeper integration with a customer the size of Meta is exactly the kind of progress it needs.

news.Title: 2 AI Stocks to Buy if the Market Sells Off Before Year-End
news.Content:
The broader stock market has been resilient this year despite significant problems, including geopolitical tensions and a challenging macroeconomic landscape. However, it is still possible that equities will experience a sell-off by the end of the year. Long-term investors need not worry too much about that. Stock market downturns happen fairly regularly, and they typically offer astute investors the opportunity to pick up shares of great companies on the dip.

And with many people fearing that the market is overvalued right now due to pricey artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, a sell-off might make some AI companies much more attractive. With that said, let's consider two AI stocks to buy if there is a market downturn by year-end: Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ: SPCX) and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Space Exploration Technologies

According to management, SpaceX could generate $1 trillion in revenue by 2030, with AI accounting for 99% of the company's value by then. Those are ambitious goals, but they might be within SpaceX's reach after all. The company has added several AI compute deals to its portfolio in recent months, and its AI segment has been its fastest-growing.

In the third quarter, SpaceX's total revenue increased by 161% year over year to $14.6 billion. The company's AI segment, dubbed Super Intelligence (SI), recorded $7.6 billion in sales, up 830% compared to the year-ago period. That wasn't all organic growth, but even putting aside an acquisition that closed in August and contributed $608 million in revenue for SI, the segment's year-over-year sales growth was an impressive 755%.

What's more, SpaceX still sees significant demand ahead for its AI products. CEO Elon Musk said we may be moving toward a shortage of SI compute that could last a while. There is some evidence for that from SpaceX's own business. The company is seeing several times as much demand for AI compute as it is willing to rent out, and even older systems are renting at a premium compared to when they were new.

If this trend continues, SpaceX's SI business could maintain strong revenue growth over the medium term. However, the market seems to have already factored that into the share price. SpaceX's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 85.5, which is very high. And despite significant progress across all three of its segments since its debut on equity markets -- as well as excellent financial results -- the stock hasn't gained much, if at all. SpaceX is a great business and would be much more attractive at the right price. It could reach that price if a sell-off is imminent. But at current levels, the stock isn't a buy.

Story Continues

2. Tesla

Tesla shares several similarities with SpaceX. Notably, it is led by Elon Musk and is investing heavily in AI. Tesla does not offer AI services, but its future is heavily dependent on the technology. Consider, for instance, that the company's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software has been trained on data from real-world driving situations. AI allows Tesla's vehicles running on its FSD software to process data in real time and make decisions on the fly. This is critical for the company's business for several reasons.

The FSD software has grown in popularity and has helped boost Tesla's electric vehicle (EV) sales in recent quarters. The company generates decent sales from this business, since it charges $99 per month for FSD subscriptions. This business is generating close to $1 billion in annual recurring revenue. It could expand significantly over the next few years.

Further, Tesla is scaling its robotaxi fleet, a business where its FSD software will be even more central. If this becomes a successful unit, Tesla could generate revenue from its EVs through their entire useful lives. So, Tesla could be looking at massive opportunities ahead that AI will help it tap into, and we haven't even mentioned the company's humanoid robot project, which also depends heavily on AI. However, Tesla has the same problem as SpaceX: valuation. Tesla is trading at 133.3x forward earnings. The stock could be a great buy on the dip -- whether in a marketwide or company-specific sell-off -- but until then, I'd rather stay away.

news.Title: Vertiv Guides for 38% Growth, GE Vernova's Orders Jumped 96%. Which AI Power Stock Is the Better Buy After the Sell-off?
news.Content:
Vertiv (NYSE: VRT) and GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) have both benefited from the rapid growth of the cloud infrastructure and AI markets . Vertiv produces thermal management, liquid cooling, and uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems for those power-hungry data centers. GE Vernova, which was spun off from General Electric (NYSE: GE) in 2024, sells the turbines, transformers, and substations that deliver the power to those data centers.

Both companies recently posted third-quarter earnings reports that easily exceeded Wall Street's estimates. Vertiv's revenue surged 61% year over year, driven by 55% organic growth and 6% from acquisitions, and it expects its full-year revenue to increase 38% organically.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

GE Vernova's revenue rose 27% year over year, with 18% organic growth, as its total orders jumped 96% organically. It expects its full-year revenue to rise 22%-25%.

However, Vertiv and GE Vernova are still trading at 45% and 24% below their all-time highs from earlier this year, respectively. Let's see why they pulled back -- and which one is a better buy.

Why did Vertiv and GE Vernova pull back?

Vertiv and GE Vernova both struggled to maintain their high valuations after the Fed raised its benchmark rates for the first time in three years this September. That pressure could force utilities and data center operators to throttle their AI infrastructure spending, while higher yields on fixed income investments drew investors away from riskier growth stocks.

Vertiv and GE Vernova also faced other near-term challenges. Vertiv struggled with supply chain constraints and the uneven timing of its larger contracts, and its recent takeover of UtilityInnovation Group -- a developer of microgrid solutions, advanced power controls, and behind-the-meter power architecture designs for data centers -- could squeeze its margins.

GE Vernova's Power and Electrification businesses were firing on all cylinders, but its smaller Wind segment remained weak. It's also ramping up spending to increase capacity, and its planned acquisition of Trench Group could further compress its margins.

Why are they still solid investments?

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Vertiv's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 29% and 49%, respectively. During that same period, they expect GE Vernova's revenue and EPS to increase at CAGRs of 17% and 24%, respectively.

Story Continues

Vertiv trades at 25 times next year's earnings, while GE Vernova has a forward multiple of 37. Neither stock is a screaming bargain yet, but they look more attractive than they did a few months ago. I'd be willing to buy both stocks at these prices -- but if I had to pick one over the other, I'd start with Vertiv because it's growing faster and trades at a lower valuation.

news.Title: Oracle Makes Major Strong Move Ahead of Key Investor Day
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Oracle ( NYSE:ORCL ) shares climbed about 4% Tuesday after the company unveiled a wave of new semiconductor partnerships designed to expand the AI capabilities of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure ahead of its Investor Day.

The announcements span Cerebras, Intel, Nvidia and Google , giving OCI customers a broader mix of hardware for AI training, inference and agentic workloads.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with ORCL.

Is ORCL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

One of the more notable additions is Cerebras.

Oracle plans to offer Cerebras Inference on OCI beginning in 2027 , targeting AI labs, enterprises and developers that need faster inference for increasingly complex AI agents.

That matters because inference speed becomes more important as agents perform multiple steps, including reasoning, checking outputs and taking actions.

Oracle is also expanding its relationship with Intel through a multiyear agreement to deploy current and future Xeon processors across OCI.

The partnership will include planned OCI X14 offerings built around Intel's next-generation Diamond Rapids server processors.

Nvidia remains another major part of Oracle's strategy.

OCI plans to build multi-gigawatt Superclusters using Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 systems , expanding on infrastructure already powered by GB200 and GB300 systems.

Oracle will also offer Nvidia HGX Rubin NVL8 systems paired with Intel Xeon processors for AI training, fine-tuning and inference.

Perhaps the biggest strategic surprise comes from Google.

Oracle plans to deploy Google Tensor Processing Units through OCI , making it the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer them.

Customers will eventually get access to Google's TPU 8t for training and TPU 8i for inference, with availability expected to begin in 2027.

Investor takeaway

I think the bigger story is that Oracle is trying to make hardware choice itself a competitive advantage .

Instead of forcing customers into one AI architecture, OCI increasingly looks like a platform where enterprises can choose among Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs, Cerebras inference systems and Intel CPUs.

That could matter as AI workloads become more specialized.

Some customers may prioritize training performance, others inference speed, and others cost efficiency.

news.Title: Why Garmin Stock Dropped After Record Results
news.Content:
Garmin (NYSE:GRMN) reported another strong quarter today, with revenue jumping 12% and profit margins expanding. That initially led shares to jump more than 2% in early trading.

But management provided a dose of reality on the conference call, prompting investors to reverse those gains. Garmin shares sank on the word that expanding profit margins will soon reverse course. The stock was trading down 6.2% on the day, as of 3:18 p.m. ET.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

The initial jump came as investors celebrated yet another strong quarter for the maker of GPS devices. Overall revenue grew to a record $1.99 billion, with Garmin's fitness and outdoor device revenue growing 16% and 20%, respectively, year over year.

That continued a strong run of growth in its two largest business segments. Those sales flowed to the bottom line , too, with gross and operating margins jumping to 63.3% and 30.8%, respectively. That was a notable increase over last year, when gross margin was below 60% and operating margin was south of 26%. That profitable growth has helped the stock soar nearly 175% over the past three years.

But margins are set to contract soon, according to management. CEO Cliff Pemble said fourth-quarter gross margin is expected to slide to about 61% as memory component costs have soared under tight supply driven by AI infrastructure demand. Regarding next year, Pemble stated:

We expect our consolidated gross margin profile will return to a historical range primarily due to higher memory costs.

The good news for investors is that the historical range is still about 58.5%. And today's sharp drop in the stock has Garmin's price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio down to about 25 based on the raised earnings guidance provided. That's a reasonable multiple for the strong underlying business, and could make today's price look like a great entry point when the dust settles.

news.Title: Anthropic Flags Data Center Moratoriums as a Top Risk to Its Growth Plans
news.Content:
Anthropic, the company behind Claude, is finally set for an IPO next month after filing its official public S-1 with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Monday, Oct. 26.

The roughly 400-page prospectus lays out the company's ambitious growth plans and vision for the future.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Running a frontier lab with cutting-edge tech development and massive infrastructure costs also brings a litany of risks spanning more than 90 pages in the S-1 filing. There are some pretty exotic, and frankly, concerning, risks cited that range from AI's potential to "destabilize the geopolitical order" to its being used to create novel bioweapons.

But the company also presented some more pressing concerns, credible threats to its business in the here and now. One that caught my eye: "moratoriums on new data center construction."

Data center moratoriums threaten Anthropic's growth

Claude may be software, but hardware plays an equal role in Anthropic's future success -- or failure. Compute capacity -- access to the GPUs and other chips that line AI data centers -- is the lifeblood of Anthropic's business. Without it, the company can't deliver the services it sells.

And therefore, Anthropic's growth is dependent on new data centers continuing to be built. That makes any restrictions on such a real threat, and one that is already showing up in the real world.

Some communities are hitting the pause button on new data centers because locals worry about strained power grids, skyrocketing utility bills, and environmental impacts. Several states, including New York, have already passed temporary moratoriums on new data center construction. Anthropic says opposition to data center development is increasing across the U.S.

Right now, this isn't widespread enough to materially threaten Anthropic's growth. But I think the trend is moving in the wrong direction for the company, and many investors don't fully appreciate how much impact this could have if it really takes off. It's an issue that companies across the industry have to face, from Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA)to Amazon .

Anthropic's revenue surges as operating losses narrow

Threats aside, the company's growth has been nothing short of incredible. Sales hit $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, about 14 times what they were in the first half of 2025.

Story Continues

On an operating basis, its first-half loss narrowed from $2.1 billion to $693 million, and the company recorded a $974 million operating profit in Q2. That's big, but it remains to be seen if this profitability holds up over time.

Does Anthropic have a lasting moat?

The moratorium issue adds uncertainty to a business that still has to prove it can consistently turn incredible revenue growth into profits. But in reality, it's not the most pressing issue in my mind.

My bigger concern is whether Anthropic has a lasting moat -- something that keeps customers choosing Claude even when competitors offer a more cost-effective alternative.

In my view, AI is evolving toward commodity status. And that means Anthropic will be forced to compete on price with companies that have a fraction of the expenses of a frontier lab.

news.Title: DOJ Inquires About Nvidia’s Hugging Face Deal, Reuters Says
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- The US Justice Department is making inquiries about Nvidia Corp.'s agreement to acquire AI model company Hugging Face for about $13 billion, part of broader regulatory scrutiny of the chip giant, Reuters reported.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Netanyahu Leads Eisenkot in Race to Form Israeli Government

Anthropic Files for IPO in Global Race to Raise Cash for AI

Finland and Norway Hold 'Frank' Call With Putin on Ukraine

The department is exploring how the transaction may affect competition in the artificial intelligence market, the news agency said, citing unidentified people familiar with the situation. At the same time, the DOJ is continuing a yearslong probe into the chipmaker's conduct, Reuters said.

Nvidia announced the Hugging Face deal in September, touting the purchase as a way to protect the open-source software community. Developers rely on the Hugging Face platform to share models and data that can be freely used by anyone. As part of the deal, Nvidia has vowed to keep the platform open.

The Justice Department has inquired whether the acquisition will let Nvidia control a key distribution point for AI, according to Reuters.

A representative for Nvidia declined to comment. Hugging Face didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The Justice Department said it doesn't typically comment on matters before it under longstanding policy. "We can affirm that this DOJ under President Trump's leadership will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence for the betterment of the American people," the department said in a statement, using the administration's preferred term for AI.

Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has parlayed its dominance in AI chips into a role in other markets, including software, AI models and networking equipment.

Bloomberg News reported last month that the DOJ was investigating whether Nvidia structured a $20 billion licensing agreement with AI chip startup Groq Inc. to avoid antitrust review. Though Groq remained an independent company after that deal, the startup's chief executive officer and operating chief moved to Nvidia as part of the transaction. Some US lawmakers later said the agreement was a takeover that stifled competition.

More recently, Nvidia has been discussing a deal with startup Reflection AI, Bloomberg has reported. That startup, which is already backed by Nvidia, debuted an open-weight model earlier this month. With such software, developers release the model's parameters, or weights, allowing others to freely use and modify the technology.

news.Title: Why Wendy's Rallied Big on Wednesday
news.Content:
Shares of fast-food stalwart Wendy's (NASDAQ:WEN) rallied on Wednesday, rising 14.7% as of 1: 51 p.m. EDT.

Wendy's entered the day down about 25% for the year, and down massively from its all-time highs.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Today, however, a major investor offered to buy out the entire company for $1.4 billion, or roughly a 20% premium to yesterday's closing price.

Peltz's Trian offers to take Wendy's out of the spotlight

Today, major Wendy's investor Trian Fund Management, a hedge fund run by Nelson Peltz, along with other investors, including other hedge funds and one of Wendy's largest franchisee groups, offered to purchase Wendy's outright for $1.4 billion, or $7.35 per share. Of note, Trian and its affiliated parties already own about 16.25% of the company, according to regulatory filings.

The buyout offer marked roughly a 20% premium to yesterday's closing price, but is also far, far below Wendy's all-time highs and the price at which the stock began the year.

Wendy's is in a tough competitive spot, as it has long billed itself as the "higher quality" fast-food option compared with budget-conscious fast-food chains like McDonald's (NYSE:MCD). But in recent years, more premium burger chains, such as Shake Shack (NYSE:SHAK), and myriad other private burger chains have sprung up. That leaves Wendy's in a strange "middle" that appeals to neither the most budget-conscious nor the quality-first crowd.

In other words, Wendy's may need extensive work on its turnaround , and that may be easier if executed outside of the prying eyes of the public markets.

Image source: Getty Images.

Investors should probably take profits

It's an open question whether the rest of Wendy's shareholders will agree to be bought out at this valuation. On the other hand, if they refuse, it's unclear whether Wendy's stock can go higher in the near term.

While Wendy's is still profitable, things are trending in the wrong direction. Same-store sales were down 6.3% last quarter, including a 7.0% decline in the U.S., resulting in a significant profit decline. Operating income plunged 23.1%, and net income fell an even greater 41.4%, as Wendy's struggled under the weight of about $2.4 billion in net debt.

So, there doesn't seem to be much residual upside if the buyout goes through, while a "no-buyout" scenario could cause a pullback, with no clear turnaround in sight.

news.Title: Google previews new security system built for banks
news.Content:
Google is pushing its technology deeper into the infrastructure that financial institutions use to move money and digital assets.

In March 2025, CME Group and Google Cloud announced a pilot using Google Cloud Universal Ledger, or GCUL, for wholesale payments and tokenized assets. CME said the technology could make collateral, margin and settlement payments more efficient as markets move toward round-the-clock trading.

But moving tokenized money is only part of the challenge.

Banks also need tight control over who can authorize a transaction.

Google is now previewing Google Multi-Party Compute, a security service designed to help banks and other institutions safeguard and transfer cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets.

The product is in private preview, with commercial availability planned for early 2027.

The timing addresses a recognized banking risk. In July 2025, the Federal Reserve, FDIC and OCC said the loss or compromise of cryptographic keys is one of the primary risks of crypto safekeeping.

A private key essentially acts as the credential needed to authorize a digital-asset transfer.

How Google's system would work

Instead of storing a complete private key in one place, Google's system splits control between separate key shares. Those shares work together to sign a transaction, Google told CoinDesk .

Related: Cathie Wood sells Bitcoin, buys $5.2 million of sinking stock

For example, a bank could keep one share on its own hardware and another in Google Cloud. Before a transfer is signed, rules can check where the funds are going, enforce transaction limits or require additional approvals.

Google says this reduces the risk of a single compromised system gaining control of the assets.

The idea itself is not new to Google.

In 2023, Google Cloud published a reference architecture showing institutions how to build MPC-based signing systems using Confidential Space.

The new service packages signing, transaction policies and recovery into a dedicated product instead of requiring customers to assemble those components themselves.

Google's financial infrastructure push has also expanded elsewhere. In March 2026, BMO, CME and Google Cloud announced plans for tokenized cash that could be used for margin, collateral and settlement. BMO targeted the second half of 2026 for that separate project, subject to regulatory approval.

Popular on TheStreet Roundtable:

Goldman Sachs revises rating and target on beaten-down AI stock

Nobel Prize winners blast Netanyahu's plan as markets favor Gadi

Mark Cuban puts Bitcoin and Apple in the same bucket

Story Continues

Wells Fargo has separately advertised for an engineer to work on MPC technology for its own digital-asset platform, another sign of institutional interest in this type of security infrastructure.

Still, much remains unproven. Google has not named the banks testing its new service or disclosed pricing . Post-quantum protection is also a future goal rather than a current feature.

And while rule-based signing can make stolen credentials harder to exploit, it cannot eliminate every risk, including an authorized employee being tricked into approving a bad transaction.

For banks, Google's system would therefore add another security layer, not replace their existing risk controls.

news.Content:
Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) stock is on the rise, up 5.5% as of 2:24 P.M. ET on Wednesday, Oct. 28, after a rival memory maker reported a strong quarter.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite were up 0.1% and down 0.2%, respectively.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

SK Hynix expects shortages through 2030

news.Title: Is AMD Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold Right Now? Here's What I'm Doing.
news.Content:
Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) has had an incredible year as a stock. It's up around 140% so far in 2026, good enough to be in the top 10 best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 . It's also crushing rival Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), which is only up around 13%.

However, what's in the past is in the past. It's time for investors to look to the future and see what to do with AMD stock. I'm currently not an AMD shareholder (to my error), but if I were, would it be time to hold or sell the stock? Or should I take a look at opening up a position?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

AMD's growth case is looking up

At the start of the AI race, AMD's technology was lagging behind Nvidia's. As a result, it lost a ton of early market share to its rival, Nvidia. However, AMD has started to catch up and has made several deals with AI hyperscalers, like OpenAI, to supply them with computing power. This has led to strong growth, with data center revenue rising 107% year over year in the second quarter to $6.7 billion.

AMD also has significant consumer and embedded processor segments, so its overall growth rate in Q2 was 52%, but the biggest improvement in AMD has come from its profit margin.

AMD Profit Margin (Quarterly) data by YCharts.

AMD's profit margin has improved steadily and continues to get stronger. If AMD can keep this trend up, the future looks very bright for the company.

Wall Street analysts expect AMD's growth rate to take a step back next quarter, and only rise to 41%. However, they expect 57% growth in the fourth quarter, and in 2027, they expect 75% growth. That's spectacular, and makes investors wonder if AMD stock could repeat in 2027 .

That's the bull case, but the bear case is much more rooted in reality.

AMD's stock has already priced in future growth

I am not denying that AMD has great growth prospects. I think that it will have a phenomenal year as a company in 2027. The issue is that all this growth is already priced into AMD's stock. If you value the stock using this year's and next year's earnings estimates, it reveals that AMD is a very expensive stock.

AMD PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts.

AMD trades for a very pricey 68 times forward earnings and 33 times next year's earnings. For reference, rival Nvidia trades at 27 times trailing earnings right now. That means that there is about a year and a half worth of growth priced into AMD's stock, which could affect future returns.

Story Continues

While I think AMD's great year has been fun for its investors, they're about to get a reality check unless AMD can absolutely blow away analyst expectations. Is there a case to just hold on to the stock? I don't think so.

When you get to extreme valuation levels like this, odds are far higher that the stock will underperform or lose value, rather than gaining. As a result, I think investors are likely better off selling and rotating into an industry peer like Nvidia. AMD has had a great year, but it has likely been too great a year, as the valuation of the stock doesn't match the business performance it's delivering.

There are far better options out there than AMD right now. If you were smart enough to get into AMD stock before it took off earlier this year, it's time to exercise some self-control, take gains, and move on to the next candidate.
