news.Title: Exclusive-US DOJ is inquiring about Nvidia's purchase of Hugging Face, sources say
news.Content:
By Max A. Cherney, Jeffrey Dastin and Jody Godoy

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 28 (Reuters) - The US Department of Justice has made inquiries about how Nvidia 's $12.93 billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face would affect competition in artificial intelligence, at the same time as antitrust enforcers pursue their years-long investigation into the chip designer's conduct, two people ‌familiar with the matter said.

The Justice Department's recent questioning covers Nvidia's acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether the chip designer has exerted pressure on its customers, the two people said. On ‌Hugging Face, Justice Department officials have asked whether the deal would let Nvidia capture a fundamental distribution point for AI , the people said. The acquisition is expected to close in the first half of 2027, Nvidia has said, adding that Hugging Face ​would continue to support work with a range of chip, cloud and AI providers.

The department's questions around the Hugging Face deal and details of its continued pursuit of Nvidia's conduct more broadly are reported for the first time here. Nvidia has become a cornerstone of the tech economy and AI boom, backing major players such as Anthropic and OpenAI while spurring data center development globally so its chips can power AI's voracious computing needs.

Any action by the DOJ could ripple through the chip industry and challenge Nvidia's investing and acquisition strategy that has extended its influence in AI. Government investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and do not necessarily ‌result in lawsuits.

A DOJ spokesperson declined to comment on any matters ⁠before the department, citing longstanding policy. The spokesperson added, "This DOJ under President Trump's leadership will continue to prioritize advancement of Super Intelligence for the betterment of the American people."

Nvidia declined to comment, and Hugging Face representatives did not respond to a request for comment.

The broad Nvidia examination started under former Democratic President Joe Biden and ⁠has continued under the administration of Republican President Donald Trump, during which time Nvidia has been the most valuable company in the world and a singular force in AI. There is no indication that Trump has any involvement, and the probe may not result in any Justice Department action.

As part of the probe, the DOJ has examined Nvidia's acquisition of SchedMD, one of the people said. The December 2025 purchase sparked worries among AI specialists ​about ​their access to SchedMD's open-source software, which helps run supercomputers relevant to national security. Nvidia has vowed to continue ​open access and support.

Story Continues

NVIDIA AND TRUMP

Nvidia has the biggest share of the market for ‌AI chips, which power the likes of ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude and similar tools. A host of startups and chip-design companies have challenged its dominance.

Competitors Broadcom and Alphabet's Google design processors together, seeking to beat Nvidia hardware with chips purpose-built for specific tasks and AI software. Advanced Micro Devices has said it can produce technically superior hardware and has struck billion-dollar deals with several AI labs and cloud computing operators.

Nvidia's market position has nonetheless made it an industry force and helped CEO Jensen Huang develop a relationship with Trump, who has touted American AI. Huang and Trump have made frequent appearances together, with the CEO joining the president's diplomatic trip to China. Trump, who has disclosed owning Nvidia stock, separately awarded Huang the National Medal of Science for advancing AI hardware.

Trump critics have previously accused the administration ‌of political intervention at the DOJ, which the administration has disputed. Such intervention is traditionally out of the ordinary.

Staff-led ​investigations at the DOJ often take years and can stretch from one administration to the next. In addition, the DOJ ​routinely seeks input from companies when evaluating proposed mergers. "It would be inappropriate for the Department ​to conduct a merger investigation under the guise of a conduct investigation," the DOJ spokesperson said.

SCRUTINY OF OTHER NVIDIA DEALS

The DOJ has scrutinized Nvidia's conduct following other ‌transactions, including its 2025 deal to license technology from chip startup Groq and ​hire its engineers, the people said. Officials have explored ​whether Nvidia unfairly offered larger allocations of AI chips if customers purchased its networking equipment and Groq processors, raising questions about whether Nvidia used its dominant product to push into a newer market, the people said.

Nvidia declined to comment, and Groq did not respond to a request for comment.

The DOJ has also looked at Nvidia's acquisition of Run:ai, which makes software ​that helps AI chips run more efficiently, the people said.

The department's questions ‌about the proposed Hugging Face acquisition include identifying how Nvidia might use the AI platform to harm rivals in the AI market, and whether Nvidia could use the ​newly acquired business to gain leverage, the people said.

Officials are also asking questions about Hugging Face's competitors, said the people.

(Reporting by Max A. Cherney and Jeffrey Dastin in ​San Francisco and Jody Godoy in New York; Editing by Peter Henderson, David Gaffen and Matthew Lewis)

news.Title: 3 Reasons Micron Stock Could Keep Climbing From Here
news.Content:
It can be hard to please the market, as Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is finding out. True, the stock has gained 218% this year, but it has declined 27% since hitting a new all-time high in June, despite the semiconductor specialist's fantastic financial results. However, my view is that this recent dip represents a wonderful opportunity for long-term investors to purchase the company's shares, as there are good reasons to believe that there is plenty more upside ahead. Let's discuss three of those reasons.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Micron's results are excellent

Micron is firing on all cylinders. In the fourth quarter of its fiscal year 2026, which ended Sept. 3, the company's revenue of $54.23 billion increased by 379% year over year and by almost 31% sequentially. The company's data storage chips are flying off the proverbial shelves like hotcakes, and the significant demand for its products is giving it stronger pricing power. That's showing up in the company's margins.

Consider that Micron's gross profit for the period grew significantly faster than revenue, reaching $47 billion, up almost 831% compared to the year-ago period. Micron's GAAP gross margin was 86.8%, almost twice the 44.7% reported in the prior year-quarter. Micron's net income increased even faster, reaching $37.7 billion, up 1077.8%. Micron's core data center business unit accounted for 33% of revenue during the period, compared to just 14% in the fourth quarter of its previous fiscal year.

This helps highlight the massive impact of the artificial intelligence (AI) tailwind on the company. What's more, Micron's guidance implies that the party isn't about to stop. The company expects revenue of $61.5 billion (at the midpoint) for the first quarter of its fiscal year 2027, representing an increase of about 351% year over year. Other important metrics, including gross margins and earnings per share, should also grow at a good clip, based on Micron's projections.

2. The memory bottleneck could persist several more years

One of the most important reasons Micron is generating outstanding financial results is the shortage of memory chips. Since these chips are indispensable to AI infrastructure, hyperscalers have no choice but to pay a premium to secure them if they want to continue scaling their data centers. But how much longer will this shortage last? It's hard to say, but according to some estimates, it may not ease until 2029. Here is why. As demand surges, Micron and other companies in this niche are prioritizing AI-focused products, as they are the most profitable right now.

Story Continues

However, this is causing shortages elsewhere in the memory chip market. Micron and other leaders in the field will have to increase their capacity to meet demand across the industry, but doing so could take several years; until then, the shortage may persist. At worst, it could continue beyond 2030. Of course, these predictions may not be accurate. But the evidence at least suggests that Micron has a couple more years of incredible demand for its products and significant pricing power.

3. Micron's valuation looks reasonable

Even if the shortage persists, Micron's revenue and earnings growth rates will eventually decrease. They always do. But in my view, that's already somewhat baked into the company's share price. Consider that Micron's current forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio is 5.05. Let's assume Micron's forward P/E stays essentially unchanged over the next five years, while the company's earnings per share (EPS) compounds at an average of 12% through this period -- then the company will register a cumulative return of about 76% over this period, or 12% annually, which is pretty strong.

There are certain risks that are reflected in Micron's low forward P/E, notably the cyclicality of the semiconductor industry. However, Micron is also likely to maintain EPS growth that's much stronger than our assumption, at least over the next few years. Even if it decreases significantly after that, the assumed average through 2031 looks fairly reasonable, in my view. So, the stock could deliver attractive returns over the medium term, making it a buy today.

news.Title: Should You Buy AMD Stock Before Nov. 3?
news.Content:
As artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers race to build data centers, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) is swiftly emerging as a formidable competitor to GPU powerhouse Nvidia .

As of this writing (Oct. 28), AMD stock has skyrocketed 164% in 2026, handily outpacing both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite , which have gained 12.9% and 13.8%, respectively. The company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Nov. 3.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Considering shares have already enjoyed a sizable rally, should investors buy AMD stock before the upcoming announcement, or has Wall Street gotten ahead of itself? Let's take a closer look.

What does Wall Street expect for AMD earnings?

AMD's second-quarter financial results illustrated how the company is expanding. Total revenue increased 50% year over year to $11.5 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) reached $1.66. More importantly, AMD's data center business generated $6.7 billion in revenue, representing 107% growth year over year.

Naturally, this momentum raised expectations for the upcoming third-quarter report. According to Wall Street's consensus estimates, analysts anticipate AMD to generate $13.1 billion in revenue and EPS of $1.93.

Here's the challenge: Strong earnings don't automatically translate into a higher stock price. When a stock has already appreciated substantially, investors tend to expect more than simply meeting consensus estimates. AMD will need to deliver an impressive earnings beat and raise its fourth-quarter outlook to justify another rally.

What tailwinds does AMD have?

AMD's Instinct AI accelerators are gaining traction among cloud computing companies seeking alternatives to Nvidia's chips. The company recently introduced its MI400-series accelerators, including the MI455X, designed to handle increasingly demanding AI training and inference workloads.

Meanwhile, its Helios rack-scale platform combines advanced GPUs, processors, networking, and software into one integrated AI computing system. Customers and partners include Microsoft , Meta Platforms , OpenAI, and Anthropic .

Beyond GPUs, AMD's Epyc server processors are another growth opportunity. These chips power data centers and compete with Intel 's server CPUs, allowing AMD to benefit from broader AI infrastructure demand beyond accelerators.

Story Continues

Is it too late to buy AMD stock?

While AMD's growth prospects are compelling, its valuation deserves attention. The stock trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 35 times. For perspective, this is roughly double the long-term forward earnings multiple for the S&P 500. Against this backdrop, it's clear investors are pricing in considerable future profit growth for AMD already. While this isn't necessarily unreasonable for a semiconductor company experiencing unprecedented demand, it leaves virtually no room for disappointment.

Investors who bought AMD stock earlier this year have already enjoyed unusually high returns. It's important to realize that buying the stock today involves a much different risk-reward profile.

At this point, investors aren't simply betting that AMD will grow. Rather, they are anticipating that the company will sustain rapid growth, execute its product road map, capture additional data center market share, and generate enough earnings to justify its elevated valuation.

In reality, this is a much higher bar. This brings me to an important observation: AMD can be an excellent business without being an attractive investment at the same time.

Personally, I wouldn't rush to build a large position immediately before Nov. 3. Instead, I would prefer to see whether AMD's results support its premium valuation and provide greater visibility into its 2027 growth trajectory.

For investors with a long-term time horizon, purchasing shares gradually might be more sensible than making a large investment ahead of a potentially volatile event such as an earnings report. Ultimately, attempting to predict short-term stock movements is a fool's errand, especially when dealing with momentum-driven companies. AMD's AI opportunity is real, but much of the easy money has already been made.

news.Title: Where Will Marvell Technology Stock Be in 2030?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) has emerged as a key player in the artificial intelligence (AI) hardware ecosystem, and that explains why shares of this semiconductor company have jumped by an incredible 189% over the past year.

Marvell designs custom AI chips, networking and optical connectivity components, and storage controllers. The company sees incredible demand for these products over the next five years. We will closely examine Marvell's key catalysts in this article and find out how much upside investors can expect from this semiconductor stock by 2030.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Marvell Technology's revenue and earnings growth are poised to accelerate impressively

Marvell's revenue in the first six months of fiscal 2027 (which ended on Aug. 1) jumped 32% year over year to $5.16 billion. However, the company sees a significant improvement in its growth rate by the end of the decade.

Marvell recently noted during its Investor Day presentation that its revenue will increase at a compound annual growth rate ( CAGR ) of 55% to 60% between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2031. This outstanding growth will be fueled by solid growth in the company's AI-related products. Revenue from custom AI chips, for instance, is anticipated to grow at an 80% CAGR through fiscal 2031. Meanwhile, interconnect revenue could increase by a 65% CAGR over the same period.

Importantly, Marvell expects that its earnings per share (EPS) growth will exceed its revenue CAGR during this period. That's because Marvell anticipates its operating expenses to increase at approximately half the rate of its revenue growth. This explains why analysts have substantially increased their long-term EPS growth estimates.

YCharts

Marvell stock can easily double by 2030

Marvell's adjusted EPS in fiscal 2026 (which ended on Jan. 31, 2026) was $2.84. The company's revenue growth estimate for the next five fiscal years indicates that its EPS could increase at a CAGR of more than 55%.

Even analysts are expecting its long-term EPS to grow at an annual rate of 56%. Assuming Marvell's earnings indeed increase at a 56% CAGR through fiscal 2031 (which will end in Jan. 2031), its EPS could reach $26.24 by the end of the decade.

If Marvell trades at 21 times earnings at that time, in line with the tech-focused Nasdaq-100 index's forward earnings multiple, its stock price could jump to $551 in 2030. That's 125% higher than Marvell's current stock price. However, Marvell's strong growth prospects suggest that it should ideally trade at a premium to the broader index.

Story Continues

That's why I won't be surprised to see Marvell stock jumping by a bigger margin by 2030, which is why investors looking to buy the next big semiconductor play should consider buying it before it surges higher.

news.Title: Stock market today:  Nasdaq wavers, S&P 500 and Dow climb as Fed votes to hold rates steady
news.Content: US stocks diverged on a critical day for markets, as investors digested a 10-2 Federal Reserve decision to hold interest rates steady and earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) loomed. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) edged roughly 0.1% higher. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) fell below the flatline. Investor attention turned toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision, where the Fed voted to keep its funds rate unchanged, despite elevated inflation readings. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook dissented, favoring a rate hike. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference will be closely watched for any signs of a hawkish bias. ( Follow live updates from the meeting .) Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks drove the rally on Tuesday after Broadcom's CEO negotiated with a consortium of banks to announce a $63 billion financing structure to build AI compute capacity. They continued to gain on Wednesday after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported a 632% year-over-year profit increase. Micron ( MU ), Samsung ( 005930.KS ), and other chipmaker stocks also rose. Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out. Rounding out the earnings picture are Ford ( F ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), eBay ( EBAY ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), and ServiceNow ( NOW ). LIVE 14 updates 7 mins ago Ines Ferré Federal Reserve votes to hold rates steady in 10-2 decision The Federal Reserve voted 10-2 on Wednesday to hold interest rates steady in the 3.75% to 4% range following its two-day policy meeting. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack and Fed Governor Lisa Cook dissented, favoring a rate hike. Markets had widely anticipated the Fed would leave rates unchanged at this meeting, with a potential rate increase at its December meeting. Investors now await remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, scheduled for 2:30 p.m. ET. 59 mins ago Jared Blikre SpaceX stock is testing a key floor level after surviving its biggest share lockup expiration Last Thursday, SpaceX took its worst one-day hit since early August, when its biggest share unlock yet freed up to 1.3 billion shares to trade. Roughly a week later, it's back at the same floor, and the rest of the space trade has left it behind. SpaceX ( SPCX ) shares were sliding again on Wednesday, along with nearly every space stock. $140 has been SpaceX's floor since the summer. It marked the top of the stock's August trading range before a breakout, and it sits about halfway between the August low near $108 and the $172 ceiling that capped rallies in June and October. That makes $140 support , a price where buyers have repeatedly stepped in. They did it twice this month, and the stock is back there again. Today at 4:15 PM UTC Ines Ferré US consumers look resilient despite higher prices for gas, Halloween candy, and more Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports: There's an old adage in investing that goes something like this: Don't bet against the US consumer's propensity to spend. After all the excitement over the Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus dropping this week, I think the Federal Reserve decision today will bring some focus back to the state of the economy and, by extension, some focus on how the US consumer is faring amid higher prices for gas, Halloween candy , medical expenses, and winter clothing, among other inflationary categories. I would sum up what I am seeing from consumers right now as remarkable resilience. Coca-Cola ( KO ) has pushed through commodity-based price increases , yet Coke Zero sales increased 16% in the third quarter. Though new Coke CEO Henrique Braun did sound a touch measured about the consumer in an interview on Yahoo Finance. Today at 3:30 PM UTC David Hollerith Ford Q3 earnings preview: Guidance boost in doubt Ford ( F ) is scheduled to report third quarter results after the bell on Wednesday, Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports: Investors will be watching whether the automaker will hold or raise its full-year outlook again. For the quarter, Ford is expected to report automotive revenue of $46.2 billion per Bloomberg consensus, with adjusted EPS of $0.41 on adjusted EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) of $2.38 billion. Last quarter, Ford raised its full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10 billion to $11 billion (prior guidance was $8.5 billion to $10.5 billion). It also lifted its adjusted free cash flow outlook to $6 billion to $7 billion. Analysts see full-year adjusted EBIT of $10.52 billion, in the upper half of that range. Capital expenditures are expected at $9.9 billion, within Ford's unchanged $9.5 billion to $10.5 billion range. Last week, rival GM narrowed its 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance to $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion while raising its EPS outlook, and shares slid despite an earnings beat, with investors hoping for more. Today at 3:00 PM UTC Ines Ferré This Nvidia chart shows why the AI compute shortage remains acute This week has shown that the appetite to build out AI infrastructure and put it to use isn't slowing down, contrary to market jitters. Rental rates for older-generation Nvidia ( NVDA ) GPUs, known as Blackwell and Hopper, continue to rise, suggesting that the shortage of compute remains acute, BCA Research chief economist Peter Berezin pointed out (see chart below). An acute shortage occurs when demand outstrips supply. "I think we are heading for an AI capex bust but probably not until 2028," Berezin said. Today at 2:15 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Natural gas emerges as key AI bottleneck, Anthropic S-1 filing shows Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports: Access to power has emerged as one of the greatest bottlenecks for the AI build-out, with a particular focus on natural gas, which is cheap and abundant in the US. Anthropic's S-1 filing proves natural gas is "an AI vertical," Melius Research managing director James West said. "We know power is a constraint to AI and Anthropic's S-1 filing did nothing to assuage that view," West wrote to clients on Tuesday. "AI compute is a natural gas demand story." Power-intensive data centers are the backbone of the AI build-out. US electricity demand from data centers is expected to double from 2025 to 2027, per research from Goldman Sachs, after 20 years of roughly stagnant energy grid expansion in the US. Today at 1:38 PM UTC David Hollerith US stocks edge into the green at Wednesday's open US stocks were mixed at Wednesday's open as investors looked ahead to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and earnings from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ). The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) was little changed, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed 0.4%. Wendy's shares rose 15% in premarket trading on the news. After nearly two years of struggles competing with the likes of behemoths McDonald's ( MCD ) and Yum! Brands' ( YUM ) Taco Bell, plus upstarts such as Shake Shack ( SHAK ), Wendy's is on the cusp of a large number of restaurant closures. "With one of its largest franchisees filing bankruptcy in September (although contested by WEN given prior termination of franchise agreement), we think investors likely expect closures to tick higher than expected, but we admit visibility on our side remains somewhat limited and there could still be a range of outcomes," veteran restaurant analyst Andy Barish warned in a recent note. "That said, given our view that there are likely additional franchise operators in the system facing challenges with leveraged balance sheets, higher interest rates and profitability pressures from higher beef, labor & build costs (like many others in QSR), we think it is prudent to moderate our development estimates and bake in more potential closures over the next 6-12 months, as the company works to strengthen its system." Today at 11:58 AM UTC David Hollerith Robinhood warns its AI agents could make unauthorized trades, sparking legal disputes Robinhood ( HOOD ) warned Wednesday that its new artificial intelligence agents could execute unintended trades and expose the online trading platform to new regulatory and legal risks. Robinhood opened its platform to AI agents brought by customers in May, and began rolling out an in-app version last month . The company warned in its third-quarter regulatory filing that the expansion creates "greater reputational risk" as the technology reaches more investors. In an interview last month, Robinhood said customers are responsible for trades executed by their agents. But the company now acknowledges that courts or regulators might not uphold its customer agreements that assign responsibility to its customers. news.Title: Here's How Much You'd Need to Invest in Coca-Cola to Generate $1,000 in Yearly Dividends
news.Content:
Coca-Cola (NYSE: KO) has raised its dividend for 64 consecutive years. That's the kind of consistency you want to look for to earn a reliable annual income. For investors who want $1,000 a year, the math is simple.

Coca-Cola raised its quarterly dividend by 4% earlier this year to $0.53 per share each quarter, or $2.12 a year. At the share price of $92, as of midday trading on Oct. 27, 2026, that works out to a yield of 2.3%. Earning $1,000 annually would require about 472 shares, or about $43,500.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Investors can rely on that dividend every year thanks to Coca-Cola's brand power and profitable business model. It owns 32 brands, each generating $1 billion in annual sales, and it mainly sells concentrate syrup to bottlers to make the finished product, resulting in above-average margins.

Concentrate operations made up 85% of the company's unit case volume in 2025. With bottlers picking up the tab for factory maintenance and other capital-heavy expenditures, Coca-Cola can generate higher margins. Its profit margin was 28% over the past year, and it paid out 62% of trailing earnings as dividends.

It continues to work on improving margins. During a September 2026 Barclays conference, CEO Henrique Braun said Coca-Cola has scaled back from 500 brands to less than 200 since the pandemic. With margins higher than five years ago, it is apparent that management prioritized keeping the most profitable brands.

The main near-term risk is a squeezed shopper due to elevated interest rates and inflation . Coca-Cola's answer has been to focus on keeping its products affordable, which led to another strong quarter of volume growth in the third quarter, with unit case volume up 5% year over year for the second straight quarter.

With 64 straight years of dividend raises, Coca-Cola more than qualifies as a Dividend King. That's a company where the payouts have increased annually for at least 50 years without interruption. It is also focused on delivering affordable, strong brands that generate high margins.

Altogether, Coca-Cola is one of the best blue chip dividend stocks to build toward $1,000 in annual passive income.

news.Title: What Generac (GNRC) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Generac Holdings Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Generac's sales rose 16% year over year to $1.29 billion, while adjusted EBITDA increased 33% to $256 million. Growth came from accelerating commercial and industrial data-center demand and a recovery in residential generator sales.

Data-center backlog surged: A long-term Amazon agreement includes $2.4 billion of expected deliveries in 2027–2028, helping drive Generac's data-center backlog to approximately $4.5 billion. Management expects 2027 data-center revenue to well exceed $2 billion.

Outlook improved: Generac maintained its full-year sales-growth forecast but raised its adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 20.5%–21% and free-cash-flow expectation to approximately $450 million for 2026. The company is also expanding large-megawatt generator capacity to support anticipated demand.

MarketBeat Week in Review – 09/21 - 09/25

Generac (NYSE:GNRC) said third-quarter net sales rose 16% year over year to a record $1.29 billion, driven by accelerating data center demand in its commercial and industrial business and a return to growth in residential generator sales.

Adjusted EBITDA increased 33% to $256 million, or 19.8% of sales, compared with $193 million, or 17.3% of sales, in the prior-year quarter. GAAP net income rose to $109 million, or $1.83 per diluted share, from $66 million, or $1.12 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted net income was $151 million, or $2.54 per share, compared with $108 million, or $1.83 per share.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

Can Bloom Energy Pop the Top Off AI's Massive Energy Bottleneck?

President and Chief Executive Officer Aaron Jagdfeld said the quarter reflected "continued momentum" in commercial and industrial markets, as well as improving residential demand. The company generated $132 million of free cash flow during the quarter, up from $96 million a year earlier.

Amazon agreement expands data center backlog

The company highlighted a long-term supply agreement with Amazon for data center backup-power generators. Generac expects initial deliveries under the agreement to total $2.4 billion across 2027 and 2028.

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

Generac Plugs Into Amazon for an $8B AI-Powered Deal

The agreement includes up to approximately 1.7 million common warrant shares, with future vesting linked to $8 billion of backup-generator purchases over the deal's seven-year term. Jagdfeld said the arrangement creates strategic alignment between the companies and provides an incentive for Amazon to continue using Generac beyond the initially anticipated deliveries.

Story Continues

Generac said its data center-related backlog increased to about $4.5 billion, nearly tripling from 90 days earlier. The backlog includes demand from hyperscale customers as well as new and existing non-hyperscale customers across multiple continents.

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

Jagdfeld said Generac now expects 2027 revenue from products sold into the data center market to "well exceed" $2 billion. He also said the company sees a path to doubling its commercial and industrial reporting segment in 2027, supported by data center demand, rental equipment customers, industrial distributors and international markets.

Third-quarter data center revenue exceeded $100 million.

Full-year 2026 data center revenue is now expected to approach $500 million, compared with prior expectations of about $450 million.

More than half of the company's $4.5 billion data center backlog is expected to be delivered in 2027, according to management.

Capacity expansion and supply chain plans

Generac began initial production at its new large-megawatt generator facility in Sussex, Wisconsin, at the end of the third quarter. The company expects production rates to ramp significantly during the fourth quarter, supporting sequential sales growth.

Management said it is working to triple global production capacity for large-megawatt generators, targeting roughly $4 billion in annual data center-related capacity by the second half of 2027. The planned expansion includes additional production lines, staffing increases, international facility expansions and a packaging facility in Belvidere, Illinois, expected to begin operations in early 2027.

Jagdfeld characterized the expansion as relatively capital-light, saying the company can increase output largely through added lines, labor and shifts within its existing manufacturing footprint. He said the company is also evaluating what an additional expansion beyond the planned capacity could require.

On supply chain readiness, Jagdfeld said Generac is dual- and triple-sourcing major components where possible, though high-horsepower diesel engines remain an exception because of limited global supply. He said the company's hyperscale customers have also conducted due diligence on Generac's supply chain and its capacity.

Commercial and industrial sales rise 28%

Commercial and industrial segment sales increased approximately 28% to $553 million. Segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $69.3 million, or 12.5% of sales, from $43.8 million, or 10.1% of sales, in the prior-year quarter.

Beyond data centers, Generac said mobile-product sales to rental equipment customers grew year over year. The Allmand mobile-products business, acquired in January, exceeded Generac's prior sales and profitability expectations, according to Jagdfeld.

Domestic industrial distributor shipments rose sequentially but declined from the prior-year quarter, which included a stronger comparison related to backlog drawdown. Generac said lead times lengthened as it completed the final phase of moving production to its Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, facility. The company expects lead times to normalize in the first quarter of 2027.

International commercial and industrial sales, excluding data center shipments, also increased, led by growth in Europe, Latin America and the Middle East. Telecom shipments declined as certain customers reduced site-deployment backlogs.

Residential sales return to growth

Residential segment sales increased 9% to $744 million, led by mid-teens growth in home standby generator sales and strong portable-generator demand. Lower residential energy-storage shipments partially offset those gains following the completion of a Department of Energy program in Puerto Rico at the end of 2025.

Residential adjusted EBITDA rose to $200.8 million, or 27% of sales, from $160.2 million, or 23.4% of sales. Generac cited favorable price-cost dynamics, higher shipment volumes, operating leverage and lower energy technology investment.

Jagdfeld said more normalized outage activity, particularly in the Midwest and Northeast, supported stronger demand. Home standby activations returned to growth in September for the first time since the second quarter of 2025, while the company's dealer network expanded to nearly 9,900 dealers.

Portable generator sales benefited from stronger outage activity and additional retail shelf space. Jagdfeld said Generac believes it has regained the No. 1 U.S. market-share position in portable generators. Meanwhile, Ecobee sales increased, and its connected-home count reached approximately 5.5 million homes.

2026 outlook maintained; EBITDA margin outlook raised

Generac maintained its forecast for full-year net sales growth in the mid- to high-teens percentage range, including an approximate 2% favorable impact from foreign currency, acquisitions and divestitures. The company continues to expect commercial and industrial sales growth in the low-30% range and residential sales growth in the high single digits.

Chief Financial Officer York Ragen said the company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin outlook to 20.5% to 21%, from a prior range of 20% to 21%, following third-quarter outperformance. Generac expects fourth-quarter gross margin of 37% to 38%, reflecting sales mix from projected data center growth and inflationary pressures.

The company also raised its free-cash-flow expectation to approximately $450 million for 2026 despite elevated capital expenditures for capacity expansion. At quarter-end, Generac had approximately $1.33 billion in debt and a gross debt leverage ratio of 1.4 times adjusted EBITDA.

About Generac (NYSE:GNRC)

Generac Holdings Inc is a technology and energy solutions company that designs and manufactures power generation equipment and other energy-related products. Its offerings include standby and portable generators, commercial and industrial power systems, energy storage solutions, and products that help customers manage and monitor energy use.

The company serves residential, commercial, industrial, and utility customers. Its products are used for backup power, prime power, and distributed energy applications across homes, businesses, data centers, healthcare facilities, construction sites, and other critical operations.

news.Title: NBT Bancorp Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in NBT Bancorp Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

NBT Bancorp reported record third-quarter earnings , with net income of $58 million, or $1.11 per diluted share. Net interest income reached $143 million, while net interest margin expanded to 3.78% on stronger loan growth and higher asset yields.

Loans grew to $11.9 billion, with commercial and consumer lending driving gains, while fee-based businesses also reached record revenue levels. The company raised its quarterly dividend 8.1% year over year to $0.40 per share.

Management cited strong capital levels and improving credit trends, alongside long-term growth opportunities from semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing investments across NBT's markets, including Micron and GlobalFoundries projects.

NBT Bancorp (NASDAQ:NBTB) reported record third-quarter earnings as loan growth, a higher net interest margin and fee-based business contributions lifted results. The company posted net income of $58 million, or $1.11 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026.

President and CEO Scott Kingsley said the company generated stronger earnings than in both the prior-year quarter and the second quarter of 2026. Operating return on assets was 1.41%, while operating return on tangible equity was 16.53%. Tangible book value per share reached $27.75, up 8.8% from a year earlier.

→ Comfort Systems Earnings: AI Slowdown or More Growth Ahead?

NBT raised its quarterly dividend to $0.40 per share, an 8.1% increase from the prior year. Kingsley said capital deployment priorities remain centered on supporting organic growth and maintaining annual dividend increases, while the company also evaluates strategic opportunities and measured share repurchases.

Record Net Interest Income and Loan Growth

Chief Financial Officer Annette Burns said net interest income rose to a record $143 million, increasing $5 million from the second quarter and more than 5% from the third quarter of 2025. Net interest margin expanded five basis points sequentially to 3.78%.

→ A 70% Rally Isn't Chord Energy's Only Selling Point

The sequential improvement reflected organic loan growth, higher earning-asset yields, increased purchase-accounting accretion and one additional calendar day during the quarter, Burns said.

Total loans were $11.9 billion at quarter-end. Excluding consumer runoff portfolios, loans increased $427 million, or 4%, from Dec. 31, 2025. Commercial loans grew $234 million during the first nine months of the year, while consumer loans increased $116 million. Commercial and consumer loans represented 56% and 44%, respectively, of the total portfolio.

Story Continues

→ Not All Tech Is Getting Crushed: 5 Names Holding Up Through the AI Sell-Off

New commercial loan originations during the quarter carried a 6.41% yield. Kingsley said the company expects fourth-quarter loan growth to be broadly consistent with its year-to-date pace, noting that construction projects typically do not generate substantial draws during the winter months.

For 2027, Kingsley identified a 3% to 5% loan-growth range as a "good starting point," taking into account expected early payoffs and continued runoff in certain consumer portfolios. He added that semiconductor-related investment across NBT's markets could create an opportunity for stronger growth over time.

Deposits, Expenses and Fee Revenue

Total deposits stood at $13.6 billion at the end of the quarter, up modestly from year-end. Core deposits increased 2.6% during the first nine months of 2026. Nearly 60% of deposits were in no- and low-cost checking and savings accounts, with a blended cost of 38 basis points.

Total deposit costs declined by one basis point from the prior quarter to 1.32%, while total funding costs increased one basis point to 1.42%. Burns said the company has shifted deposit mix away from higher-cost time deposits and toward checking, savings and money-market products. During the year, $99 million of brokered certificates of deposit matured and NBT redeemed $25 million of subordinated debt.

Fee income excluding securities gains totaled $52.9 million, up $3.3 million from the prior quarter and 2.9% from a year earlier. Retirement plan administration revenue increased 8.7% year over year. Combined quarterly revenue from retirement plan services, wealth management and insurance services reached approximately $34 million, a new high, according to Burns.

Non-interest income accounted for approximately 27% of total revenue. Burns cautioned that the fourth quarter is typically the lowest-revenue period for the company's fee businesses because activity-based fees decline seasonally.

Total operating expenses increased 3% sequentially, primarily due to an additional payroll day, incentive compensation, activity-based costs and a higher reserve for unfunded loan commitments. Burns said NBT expects fourth-quarter operating expenses to remain near third-quarter levels of roughly $114 million to $115 million.

Credit Trends and Capital Position

Provision expense was $3.8 million in the third quarter, down from $6.1 million in the second quarter. Burns attributed the decline primarily to slower loan growth, a modest improvement in the economic forecast and portfolio-mix changes.

The allowance for loan losses represented 1.17% of total loans and covered nonperforming loans by two times. Burns said nonperforming loans rose modestly during the quarter but did not reflect broad industry or regional trends, instead stemming from borrower-specific situations. Criticized and classified loans declined from the prior quarter and were significantly below year-earlier levels, she said.

Kingsley said the company ended the quarter with capital levels of nearly 10% on a leverage basis, 12.5% for common equity tier 1 capital and more than 14% for risk-based capital. He said the capital position gives NBT flexibility to invest in its markets, pursue organic initiatives and consider acquisition opportunities.

Semiconductor Investment Across NBT Markets

NBT Bank President Joe Stagliano said the company's markets are benefiting from semiconductor and advanced-manufacturing investment across upstate New York and other parts of its footprint. NBT operates about 70 branches across the affected New York corridor.

Stagliano pointed to progress on Micron's development in Clay, New York, where construction has advanced beyond site preparation and crews began driving pilings for the first fabrication facility. Although chip production is not expected until about 2030, he said the project is already driving attention toward workforce housing, infrastructure and support services. NBT expects to open a branch about one mile from the Micron campus in the first half of 2027.

He also cited activity in the Mohawk Valley, semiconductor research led by NY Creates in the capital region, and GlobalFoundries' plans to add two fabrication facilities in Saratoga County. GlobalFoundries also has a facility in Burlington, Vermont, where CHIPS Act-supported investments are advancing semiconductor technologies.

Kingsley said NBT believes it has strong teams in Central New York, the Mohawk Valley and the capital region to serve potential construction, contractor, housing and business-development needs tied to these projects. He said the company's long-term growth outlook is supported by both these regional opportunities and its diversified operating model.

About NBT Bancorp (NASDAQ:NBTB)

NBT Bancorp Inc is the bank holding company for NBT Bank, a community banking institution headquartered in Norwich, New York. Through NBT Bank and its subsidiaries, the company provides banking, lending, investment, insurance and financial services to consumers, businesses, nonprofit organizations and municipalities.

NBT Bank offers checking and savings accounts, certificates of deposit, residential and commercial mortgages, consumer loans, business lending, cash-management services and agricultural financing.

news.Title: Prediction: This Will Be Nvidia's Stock Price by the End of 2027
news.Content:
With a market cap of about $5.3 trillion, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the largest company in the world -- and it's easy to see how it reached that size. The tech giant's advanced processors are the dominant compute hardware in the data centers that underpin the entire generative artificial intelligence (AI) industry , and as soaring demand for its chips continues to outstrip supply, it enjoys booming sales at sky-high margins.

That said, all investors know that past performance doesn't guarantee future results. And the larger a company becomes, the harder it is for additional growth to move the needle on its finances. So what might this leading tech stock be worth by the end of 2027?

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Generative AI has taken the world by storm

It's been roughly four years since OpenAI's ChatGPT introduced the world to the power of generative AI, and the revolution that it triggered shows no signs of slowing down. According to analysts at Goldman Sachs , tech companies' AI-related capital expenditures will total more than $1 trillion in 2026. And much of that spending will go toward graphics processing units (GPUs) and other data center compute hardware created by companies like Nvidia.

The supply of advanced semiconductor equipment remains tight relative to demand, and Nvidia's GPUs remain the most popular data center AI accelerators, a situation that allows it to charge high prices. These persistent tailwinds were reflected in the company's second-quarter earnings.

Revenue jumped 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, driven mostly by strength in the company's data center segment, which grew 117%. This business involves designing and selling advanced AI infrastructure. And management plans to keep the momentum going with new releases, such as its Vera Rubin platform, which is designed specifically to handle agentic AI workloads. Nvidia's bottom line is also looking good; the company's net income jumped 32% year over year to $59.7 billion in the period.

What are the risks?

On the surface, Nvidia looks like the perfect stock to own. But investors should be aware that it faces some big challenges. Perhaps the biggest is its lack of diversification. In the past, Nvidia boasted a broader business model as it sold GPUs for consumer video games, machine learning, cryptocurrency mining, virtual reality devices, and data centers, among other uses. However, the mix of end-uses has condensed dramatically: Data centers now account for over 90% of its revenue.

Story Continues

This situation leaves Nvidia exceptionally exposed to a potential downturn in the AI market. And even the bulls should be willing to accept that the current levels of data center spending probably won't last forever.

A recent paper by Columbia University finance professor Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh (first presented at the nonpartisan Brookings Institution) concludes that U.S. businesses and consumers will eventually have to spend the equivalent of 9% of the country's GDP on AI-related services to justify the current levels of capital investment going toward the technology. That's as much as we spend on food, and far more than we spend on essentials like energy and construction.

While large language models (LLMs) are useful, they are notoriously difficult to monetize due to their huge energy consumption and the intense level of competition in the space, especially from lower-cost Chinese alternatives. In fact, industry leader Anthropic reported an eye-popping net loss of $80 billion in the first half of 2026. If the consumer-facing side of the AI market struggles to turn a profit, that could eventually lead to a smaller market for hardware providers like Nvidia.

What will Nvidia stock be worth by the end of 2027?

Trading today at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 23.5, Nvidia stock is still relatively cheap relative to its growth potential. And investors who believe the AI boom will maintain its momentum can comfortably expect the stock to offer additional multibagger returns from here. That said, this represents the best-case scenario. And there are several reasons to be less optimistic.

The AI industry shows many of the signs that it's in an unsustainable bubble. And Nvidia's business model isn't diversified enough to be cushioned against the painful impact of a spending slowdown. With these risks in mind, it looks more likely to me that when we get to the end of 2027, Nvidia shares will be trading close to flat compared to their price today.

After all the excitement over the Anthropic ( ANTH.PVT ) IPO prospectus dropping this week, I think the Federal Reserve decision today will bring some focus back to the state of the economy and, by extension, some focus on how the US consumer is faring amid higher prices for gas, Halloween candy , medical expenses, and winter clothing, among other inflationary categories. news.Title: Microsoft earnings live: Microsoft to report Q1 earnings with Wall Street looking for further Azure growth
news.Content:
Microsoft ( MSFT ) will report its first quarter earnings after the bell on Wednesday, providing the market with a better view of demand for AI apps and services.

This is the first time Microsoft will report earnings under its new segment structure . The company announced the change in Q4, saying that rather than Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing, it will switch to two segments: Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.

Microsoft's Agents and Infra segment will garner the most attention and include the company's Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud services, productivity and server licensing, industry solutions, and frontier and support services.

Devices and Consumer will include Microsoft's search and advertising businesses, Xbox, and Windows OEM and devices.

Investors following the company's Q1 report will be on the lookout for more information about Azure and Copilot growth as Microsoft continues to push its AI services.

For the quarter, Wall Street is anticipating earnings per share of $4.27 on revenue of $90.6 billion, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus estimates. That would be an improvement from the EPS of $4.13 and revenue of $77.6 billion the company saw in the same period last year.

Agents and Infra revenue is expected to climb 22.5% to $75.6 billion, with Azure and Microsoft 365 bringing in $32.2 billion and $27.4 billion, respectively.

Devices and Consumer sales are projected to decline 6% to $15 billion.

Capital expenditures, including leases, are anticipated to top $45.9 billion in the quarter, up from the $19.3 billion Microsoft spent in Q1 last year.

news.Title: Beyond NVIDIA: Why TSMC Stock Looks Attractive After Q3 Earnings
news.Content:
NVIDIA NVDA may dominate the AI chip headlines, but investors looking for another way to capitalize on the artificial intelligence boom should not overlook Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company TSM or TSMC. The world's leading contract chipmaker is benefiting from surging demand for advanced semiconductors, with third-quarter 2026 revenues rising 41.2% year over year. The company expects full-year revenue growth of approximately 44% in U.S. dollars, supported by robust AI demand and the ramp-up of next-generation 2-nanometer technology. With demand spanning AI accelerators, agentic AI and networking chips, TSMC offers investors a promising opportunity to participate in AI growth beyond NVIDIA.

TSMC's Q3 Results Show Strong Growth Momentum

TSMC's third-quarter 2026 revenues were up 16.2% sequentially. Net income increased 68.7% year over year while earnings per American depositary receipt (ADR) reached $4.60.

Profitability remained robust, with gross margin of 66.4%, which expanded 690 basis points (bps) from the year-ago quarter. Operating margin of 58.7% expanded 810 bps year over year. Net profit margin was 51.1%. Advanced technologies, defined as 7-nanometer and more advanced processes, accounted for 79% of wafer revenues.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

High-performance computing (HPC), which includes processors used in AI and other demanding computing applications, remained TSMC's largest platform. HPC revenues rose 22% sequentially and accounted for 68% of third-quarter revenues.

AI Demand and 2-Nanometer Production Drive the Outlook

TSMC expects fourth-quarter 2026 revenues of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, representing approximately 14% sequential growth at the midpoint from third-quarter revenues.

Management raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth outlook to approximately 44% year over year in U.S. dollar terms. CEO C.C. Wei said demand for leading-edge technologies remained extremely robust, supported by technology differentiation and a broad customer base.

TSM expects gross margin of 65%-67% and operating margin of 56.5%-58.5% in the fourth quarter. It also indicated that overseas expansion could increase margin dilution over the next few years.

The company also noted growing adoption of agentic AI, open-source AI models, AI accelerators and networking chips. The company expects these developments to support demand for advanced silicon.

The 2-nanometer manufacturing ramp is another important growth driver. The technology contributed 8% of wafer revenues in the third quarter and management expects its ramp-up to support fourth-quarter performance. TSMC also expects annual capacity for its N2 family of technologies to more than double in 2027, supported by demand from smartphones and HPC applications.

Story Continues

TSMC is also working with ASML Holding ASML to advance next-generation chipmaking technology. In September 2026, the companies announced an industry initiative to transition to 12-inch photomasks for high-numerical-aperture (High-NA) extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography. The initiative targets a pilot line by 2031, with advanced-node production readiness targeted for 2033. The larger photomasks are expected to improve manufacturing productivity and reduce chipmaking costs, supporting the industry's longer-term push toward more advanced semiconductors.

TSMC Earnings Estimate Revisions Chart

Heavy Capital Spending Supports Expansion but Creates Risks

TSMC plans to spend $60 billion to $64 billion on capital expenditures in 2026. Management expects investment during 2026-2028 to be significantly higher than in the preceding three years as the company expands capacity to meet customer demand.

The increasingly negative values in the chart below reflect rising capital outflows, showing the company's substantial investment commitments as it prepares to meet growing demand for AI chips.

TSMC vs. NVIDIA: Two Different AI Growth Opportunities

NVIDIA reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 revenues of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year. Data Center revenues increased 117% to $89 billion. The company forecast third-quarter revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.

These figures demonstrate that NVIDIA remains a powerful AI growth story. Its GPU architecture, CUDA software ecosystem and integrated computing platform differentiate its business from TSMC's.

TSMC, by contrast, manufactures advanced chips for NVIDIA and other customers. Its investment case rests on semiconductor production demand across multiple designers and end markets, rather than the success of a single chip platform.

Is TSMC Stock Worth Buying Now?

TSMC's strong third-quarter performance, upgraded outlook and expanding 2-nanometer business strengthen its growth prospects. Moreover, its Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) reflects positive earnings estimate revisions, making the stock a candidate for investors seeking exposure to the AI semiconductor boom. However, buying TSMC as an alternative way to participate in AI growth is different from expecting it to replace NVIDIA in a portfolio.

NVIDIA remains a dominant AI computing platform provider, while TSMC benefits from manufacturing advanced chips for multiple customers. Rather than viewing the two stocks as substitutes, investors should evaluate their distinct growth drivers and risk profiles. TSMC's strong outlook makes it worth considering now, although its capital intensity and geopolitical exposure remain important risks. news.Title: History Says AGNC Can Keep Paying Through a Rate Shock: Its Dividend Held as Book Value Fell 38% in 2022
news.Content:
AGNC (NASDAQ: AGNC), the world's second-largest mortgage real estate investment trust ( mREIT ), pays a forward dividend yield of 16.2%. That massive dividend might seem like a bright red flag, especially as rising interest rates and Treasury yields rattle the market. Still, it's actually paid continuous dividends ever since its IPO in May 2008.

During those 16 years, the U.S. economy experienced three major "rate shocks" in 2013, 2018, and 2022. Let's see how AGNC kept paying dividends through those downturns that significantly reduced its book value, and whether that resilience makes it a worthwhile investment.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Why does AGNC's book value support its dividend?

Unlike equity real estate investment trusts ( REITs ), which buy physical properties to collect rent, mREITs buy mortgage-backed securities (MBS). AGNC generates most of its profits by borrowing at short-term rates (via "repo" transactions that enable it to sell its MBS and buy them back at a set price plus interest at a future date) to buy longer-term MBS.

This strategy is highly exposed to interest rate hikes, which increase its short-term borrowing costs and reduce the book value of its existing MBS (as older, lower-yielding bonds decline in value relative to higher-yielding new issues). Higher rates also discourage homeowners from refinancing their mortgages, extending the lifespan of their lower-yielding MBS.

When interest rates hold steady, AGNC's book value rises as it accumulates more leveraged mortgage assets, which generates more net interest income to support its dividends. But when interest rates spike, its book value drops and its dividends become more difficult to sustain.

Why is AGNC's book value per share declining?

Over the past five years, AGNC's book value per share declined significantly. The steepest drop occurred in 2022, when the Federal Reserve executed its fastest rate hikes in 40 years. Its net spread and dollar roll income per share -- which mREITs use to gauge their profitability and dividend coverage -- also shrank but continued to cover its dividends.

AGNC's book value recovered in 2024 and 2025 as the Fed cut its benchmark rates again, but its net spread and dollar roll income per share -- which lags behind its book value (because it's still tied up in its repo borrowing) -- continued to decline.

At the end of 2025, many investors were bullish on AGNC because it seemed the Fed would continue cutting rates in 2026. However, the Iran war and inflation forced the Fed to hold rates steady throughout most of the year before raising them again in September.

By the end of the third quarter of 2026, its book value had dropped to $7.13 per share. For the first nine months of 2026, its net spread and dollar roll income per share rose two cents to $1.19, but it could barely cover its $1.44 per share in dividends by the end of the year.

What shouldn't AGNC investors overlook?

AGNC's ability to continue paying dividends even after its book value plunged 38% in 2022 is impressive, but it's also reduced that payout nine times since its IPO. At its peak in 2010-2011, AGNC paid $5.60 per share in annual dividends -- compared to $1.44 per share today.

AGNC's stock price has also declined from its IPO price of $20 to around $9. Reinvesting its dividends would have offset that pressure and given you a total return of about 520% -- but you would still have underperformed the S&P 500 's (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) total return of 671%.

AGNC is designed to generate steady income rather than market-beating gains, but another interest rate hike could force it to cut its massive dividend. So while AGNC's stock might look tempting at these levels, I'd rather stick with more reliable dividend plays instead.

news.Title: Apple announces $2,899 MacBook Pro — its first touchscreen laptop
news.Content:
Apple ( AAPL ) has done something company observers never thought it would: launched a MacBook with a touchscreen display.

Called the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, the laptop gets, you guessed it, an XDR OLED touchscreen, with better colors and brightness than standard LCD displays.

Available in 14-inch and 16-inch options, the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display also gets the iPhone's Dynamic Island, which houses the laptop's Center Stage webcam. It's also where you'll find Siri AI and Live Activities.

Inside, the notebooks can be outfitted with either Apple's M5 Pro or M5 Max processors.

All of that, however, will cost you: The 14-inch model starts at a wallet-draining $2,899, while the 16-inch will set you back $3,199.

The base MacBook Pro 14-inch with Apple's new M6 processor starts at $1,999. The standard MacBook Pro 16-inch with Apple's M5 Pro processor starts at $2,999.

Those prices represent a $300 increase that Apple implemented in June due to the global memory and storage shortage.

Apple's move to include a touchscreen display with its MacBook comes years after rivals Microsoft ( MSFT ), HP ( HPQ ), Dell ( DELL ), and others implemented the technology in their own laptops.

Apple previously dabbled with touch on its Macs with its Touch Bar, a thin touch-sensitive OLED strip that sat above the keyboard. But the company discarded the feature after it failed to gain traction among users.

The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display — man, that's a lot of words for a laptop — comes a day after Apple debuted upgraded versions of its MacBook Pro and iMac . The company kicked off the week with a refresh to its iPad mini , which received a larger, improved display and a new processor.

Apple's Mac line of devices accounted for $33.7 billion of the company's $416.1 billion in 2025, making it the tech giant's fourth-largest segment by sales. Apple's iPhone brought in $209.5 billion, while services made up $109.1 billion.

The company has stepped up the cadence of product launches in the second half of the year, bringing out everything from new chips to updated AirPods and more.

The most ambitious device is the iPhone Duo , which is currently sold out in stores, with delivery times extending into late January.

news.Title: Oracle has a spending question its new chip deals can’t answer
news.Content: If you asked ChatGPT a question this week, the reply probably landed in seconds. Behind it sat racks of chips, cooling systems, and power lines someone paid for long before you typed. Oracle Corporation (ORCL) is one of the companies that pays first and collects later. On Oct. 27, Oracle lined up more chips for that business. Its cloud will offer processors from Alphabet's (GOOGL) Google, Nvidia Corporation (NVDA), Intel Corporation (INTC), and Cerebras Systems (CBRS). It also pulled OpenAI deeper into its business software. Yet none of these deals answers the question investors bring to Oracle's Investor Day on Oct. 28: how Oracle pays for everything it has promised to build. Also read: Oracle CEO admits its software can take years to get running Evercore ISI estimates that Oracle needs $50 billion to $60 billion in additional funding, according to Seeking Alpha . The firm sees that need lasting until free cash flow turns positive in fiscal 2029. Oracle's building plans are running ahead of the cash its business brings in. The new chips come with new bills The Google deal shows the tradeoff. Oracle said its cloud will be the first large provider outside Google to offer Google's custom chips, called TPUs, starting in 2027. The same press release says Oracle will supply the power, cooling, and data center networking to run them. The release does not say who pays for the chips themselves. Either way, Oracle must house and power several kinds of hardware. Oracle also plans clusters measured in gigawatts on Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems, plus a multiyear Intel Xeon deal, according to Seeking Alpha . Nvidia's Ian Buck said the aim is to help customers "put more of their infrastructure to work today and sustain its value as AI evolves." Meanwhile, CNBC reported that Oracle's cloud will also host OpenAI's Jalapeño chip. Mahesh Thiagarajan, president of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, told the network that chips remain scarce and customers like OpenAI benefit from having options. I read that as Oracle protecting its supply, which is sensible. Yet Thiagarajan also called Nvidia's chips "the best, most fungible," meaning the easiest to shift between models and workloads. Hardware must stay useful long enough to pay for itself. By his own measure, the other accelerators joining Oracle's cloud are less flexible bets. The market already values the AI cloud below zero Those bets come while investors already doubt Oracle's AI cloud. Evercore valued Oracle's software and non-AI cloud businesses at about $197 per share after accounting for debt. By Evercore's math, the market assigns Oracle's AI cloud a negative value. Story Continues If investors see the AI cloud as a drag, more of it cannot fix that. Evercore said investors need "a clearer picture of the remaining funding needs." Oracle has already leaned on equity investors. The company sold $20 billion of common stock during its fiscal first quarter, according to its earnings release . New shares spread future profits across more owners. Oracle has forecast $90 billion to $95 billion in capital spending for fiscal 2027, according to Seeking Alpha. The spending plan roughly equals the $90 billion or more in revenue Oracle expects this fiscal year, according to its earnings release. In other words, Oracle plans to spend about as much on building as it collects. Oracle says it is structuring new deals to ease that strain. Its earnings release said more than $30 billion in AI contracts booked last quarter added nothing to its capital-raising plans. That covers new contracts, not those already driving the bill. OpenAI moves into Oracle's safer business The OpenAI announcement matters most to me because it reaches the businesses Evercore says carry Oracle's value. OpenAI said Oracle's applications and data are coming into ChatGPT, and OpenAI models will power new Oracle products. Oracle's own recruiting team now prepares some market research in 15 to 20 minutes instead of two to four days, OpenAI said. Results like that become Oracle's sales pitch. Thiagarajan told CNBC that using ChatGPT "allows anybody to build an application, deploy it, manage it." Software sales do not need a new data center for each customer, making this the cheapest growth Oracle announced on Oct. 27. However, the catch is concentration. OpenAI is now Oracle's compute customer, the designer of a chip headed to its cloud, a partner in its apps, and a vendor to its staff. Evercore said investors want clarity on Oracle's contracted backlog excluding OpenAI, a sign the market treats that link as a risk. Reports in April that OpenAI fell short of several sales targets showed how quickly that link can turn. Tying Oracle's steadier software business to the same partner raises the cost of any OpenAI stumble. More Oracle: CoreWeave, Oracle have an interest rate problem Oracle boss Larry Ellison just suffered a historic wealth collapse Oracle's 'force majeure' warning lands as AI power gets scarce Investors want a funding plan, not more chips The recent deals also hint at who will carry the AI buildout's cost. Google placing its chips in a rival hyperscaler's cloud for the first time suggests chip designers want reach without building every data center. Someone still owns the power, the cooling, and the debt. Oracle has volunteered for that role. It works if customers keep paying and help fund the build. Evercore listed customer funding, alternative financing, and possible data center delays as details investors will watch. The Oct. 28 test is simple. Oracle needs to put its own number on the funding gap and show who fills it. The next phase of the AI boom may reward companies that finance data centers more than those that fill them with the most chips. news.Title: Arista Networks Stocks Move Lower With Prometheus Networking Deployment in Focus
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Arista Networks ( NYSE:ANET ) has a concrete place in Meta's AI buildoutand it reaches beyond the GPU rack. Shares fell 0.97% to $185.19 at 11:00 a.m. ET on October 28, even as reporting on Prometheus highlighted the networking supplier's role in connecting the supercluster's buildings. For investors, the hook is straightforward: bigger AI systems need more than computing power. They also need networks that keep widely dispersed processors working together.

Meta's engineering breakdown names Arista's 7800-series chassis, powered by Broadcom's Jericho3 chips, in the aggregation network linking building-level systems across distances of two kilometers to more than 100 kilometers. Capacity runs into multiple petabits per second between regional pairs. That puts Arista inside a demanding deployment and could strengthen its pitch as AI infrastructure spreads across larger campuses. news.Title: Applied Digital Insiders Just Bought More Shares. Should You Join Them?
news.Content:
Applied Digital (NASDAQ: APLD) insiders have been buying the dip as the artificial intelligence (AI) stock continues to slide. The company's CEO and president bought a combined $6.7 million worth of shares on Oct. 16. Despite the insider buying, Applied Digital is down by more than 30% over the past month.

No doubt, sentiment around AI stocks has soured lately, but that doesn't mean fundamentals have weakened. These are some details to consider when deciding whether Applied Digital is a buy.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Applied Digital is realizing AI revenue

Applied Digital makes money by building AI data centers . The company creates the facilities, and then it's up to customers to bring their own hardware. CoreWeave is one of Applied Digital's largest customers with 15-year leases valued at up to $11 billion in revenue over that stretch.

The total deal covers 400 megawatts, putting the value of each megawatt at $1.83 million per year. While some AI data center companies are multiple years away from building facilities and generating revenue, Applied Digital is already seeing big gains on its balance sheet. Revenue surged by 322% year over year to reach $341.9 million in its fiscal 2027's first quarter.

Costs have also been surging, leaving the company still unprofitable, though that's common in the AI data center industry. Even Nebius remains deeply unprofitable despite high revenue growth. This is normal because it costs a lot of money to build data centers. As Applied Digital completes more of its facilities and attracts more customers, revenue will start to outpace costs.

AI demand isn't going anywhere

Every quarter seems to feature a news cycle of waning demand for AI and concerns about a popping bubble. However, the tech executives who know the most about the industry regularly speak about substantial growth and demand, and their fundamentals back up their talk.

Elon Musk told investors when discussing Space Exploration Technologies ' quarterly results that the company is "hounded" by hyperscalers and dozens of smaller companies that are seeking compute. Demand is still accelerating, prompting higher contract values.

It's a good environment for Applied Digital as it brings more of its facilities online. Not only will it start to realize more revenue from its backlog, but Applied Digital is also gaining the flexibility to charge higher prices to future customers.

Story Continues

Musk told investors to expect $100 billion in annual recurring revenue by December. Applied Digital benefits from the same tailwinds as SpaceX's AI business. That should eventually show up in the stock price even though doom and gloom has been the common narrative in recent weeks.

Applied Digital's Achilles' heel

Although Applied Digital is in the right industry and is building high-demand infrastructure that can command lofty contract values, there are some problems. The two big flaws are that Applied Digital uses a colocation model and locks in long-term contracts. Colocation involves building a facility and letting the hyperscaler bring their own chips and other resources. It's a less capital-intensive effort, which lets Applied Digital build more data centers with less overhead.

However, there's a big catch. Remember the $1.83 million annual megawatt value Applied Digital secured with CoreWeave? That's not much when compared to Nebius landing $40 million to $50 million per megawatt each year on short-term deals.

Nebius puts more capital into its data centers and also operates a cloud platform. Neoclouds are more complex to set up than colocation facilities. However, the revenue ceiling is much higher. Nebius was only receiving annual contract values of $12 million per megawatt. The value of a megawatt has more than quadrupled in less than one year for short-term deals, and that type of momentum suggests more lucrative deals in the future.

Applied Digital hasn't put itself in a good position to capitalize on rising megawatt prices since it isn't a neocloud and it signs 15-year leases with its tenants. Meanwhile, capital expenditures can climb at these sites where Applied Digital has locked in relatively low annual contract values per megawatt. Applied Digital is in the right industry and looks oversold at current levels, but pure neoclouds are a better way to approach the opportunity.
