news.Title: AAOI's CATV Business Gains Momentum: Can It Beat LITE and COHR?
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI is benefiting from robust demand for its cable television (CATV) products, driven by accelerating network upgrades and increasing adoption of DOCSIS 4.0 technology. Strong shipments of next-generation amplifiers, expanding customer relationships, and growing demand for software solutions are strengthening the company's growth prospects and competitive positioning against Lumentum LITE and Coherent COHR in the optical networking market.

In the second quarter of 2026, CATV revenues surged 43.8% year over year and 20.6% sequentially to a record $80.6 million, which accounted for approximately 42% of total revenues. Results benefited from significant shipments of 1.8 GHz amplifiers to its largest CATV customer and growing engagement with newer multiple-system operator customers.

AAOI's selection by Mediacom as its primary vendor for DOCSIS 4.0 network upgrades represents another significant growth opportunity. The deployment of QuantumLink software and next-generation 1.8 GHz Quantum bandwidth smart amplifiers is expected to improve network reliability while reducing operational costs.

Further expanding its portfolio, in September, AAOI announced plans to showcase its first live Quantum30 3.0 GHz proof-of-concept demonstration at SCTE TechExpo in Atlanta. The demo will feature live downstream operation at 3.0 GHz over a coaxial network using a concept amplifier, SC-QAMs, OFDM channels and a 3.0 GHz DOCSIS signal generator. Building on its Quantum18 platform, AAOI aims to help cable operators evaluate network requirements beyond DOCSIS 4.0's 1.8 GHz capacity. The company also released a white paper examining engineering, operational, and economic considerations associated with expanding hybrid fiber-coaxial networks toward 3.0 GHz.

AAOI's expanding CATV portfolio, growing customer adoption and continued investments in next-generation broadband technologies are expected to sustain growth momentum and strengthen its competitive position against Lumentum and Coherent. The company expects third-quarter 2026 CATV revenues between $100 million and $110 million, reflecting strong sequential growth. It also anticipates annual CATV revenues exceeding $325 million, supported primarily by amplifier shipments and initial software contributions.

How Competitors Fare Against AAOI

Applied Optoelectronics is facing stiff competition from Lumentum and Coherent in the AI space.

Lumentum is benefiting from strong demand for its optical components and systems, driven by the industry shift to AI workloads and increased data center connectivity. Key growth drivers include record shipments of 800G and next-generation 1.6T cloud transceivers, strong momentum in pump and EML laser sales and successful ramp-up of new technologies like near-packaged optics and co-packaged optics.

Coherent is benefiting from the strong demand in AI data center and communications markets, leading to record revenues and accelerated growth. Key drivers included strong customer bookings, expansion of production capacity, especially in 6-inch indium phosphide output and the ramp-up of new products like advanced transceivers and optical circuit switching systems.

news.Title: Why Arm’s Q2 Earnings Could Spur a Recovery in Its Stock
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) will release its fiscal 2027 second-quarter earnings on Nov. 4. While profit booking following a significant rally has led to a correction in its stock price, its solid Q2 performance and strong Arm AGI CPU demand could spur a recovery.

Arm continues to see strong customer demand across its business, which indicates solid growth ahead. Moreover, it has signed multiple high-value agreements that will support long-term growth.

More News from Barchart

PLTR Stock Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Palantir's Q3 Report

'U.S Has the Best Healthcare in the World. It's Not Even Close' Says Mark Cuban — But the Problem Is Most Americans Can't Afford It

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

Arm's Q2 Outlook

Arm entered fiscal 2027 on a strong footing, led by solid momentum across its business. Strong demand for ARM-based computing architectures across cloud infrastructure, consumer electronics, automotive systems, and emerging AI applications positions it well to deliver solid growth in Q2 and beyond.

Arm reported first-quarter revenue of $1.29 billion, up 22% year-over-year (YoY). The top line benefited from solid performance in the royalty business. Its royalty revenue increased 22% YoY to $715 million, with cloud AI and data center infrastructure emerging as the primary growth engines. Data center royalty revenue more than doubled from the previous year, supported by the expanding adoption of ARM-based server processors among major hyperscalers.

In addition, the growing deployment of data processing units (DPUs) and SmartNICs is providing another growth source, as Arm technology is incorporated into a broad range of leading data center networking products.

In the consumer segment, Edge AI royalties continued to expand despite weakness in the smartphone market. Higher royalty rates, driven by growing adoption of Armv9 architectures and compute subsystems, helped offset softer smartphone sales and the pressure from elevated memory prices. Physical AI also contributed positively, with continued adoption of ARM-based technologies in advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and autonomous applications supporting demand across the automotive ecosystem.

Licensing revenue is another key growth driver. License and other revenue reached $574 million, up 23% YoY, reflecting strong customer demand for next-generation architectures and deeper strategic relationships with major technology companies. Arm also secured multiple high-value agreements as existing customers renewed long-term licenses. These arrangements, involving hyperscalers, automotive and robotics companies, and handset manufacturers, strengthen Arm's competitive position.

Story Continues

Demand for Arm's AGI CPU offering is also gaining traction, with reported demand exceeding $2 billion. The addition of customers across the U.S. and China, alongside an expanding overall pipeline, points to strong growth ahead.

Looking ahead, management expects the growth trajectory to remain strong in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Arm forecasts revenue of $1.38 billion, representing approximately 22% YoY growth. Licensing and other revenue are projected to rise about 30%, while royalty revenue is expected to grow at a low-teens rate.

The earnings outlook is also solid, with management projecting adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.47 for Q2, up 21% YoY.

Why ARM Stock Appears Compelling Ahead of Q2

Arm's upcoming Q2 earnings could be a key catalyst for a stock-price recovery, supported by strong customer demand, expanding data center adoption, and growing traction for its AGI CPU offering.

Arm is expected to deliver solid revenue and earnings growth, driven by strength in royalty revenue. Higher licensing revenue and long-term agreements with major technology companies also highlight its solid growth prospects. Moreover, rising adoption of ARM-based architectures across AI infrastructure, automotive systems, and consumer electronics provides multiple avenues for sustained growth.

Although ARM stock still trades at a high valuation, the 49% decline from its 52-week high has eased some of these concerns ahead of the earnings announcement.

Analysts currently have a "Moderate Buy" consensus rating on ARM stock and a mean price target of $292.72.

news.Title: PepsiCo Hasn't Been This Cheap Relative to Earnings in 6 Years. Here's Why That's the Signal to Buy.
news.Content:
Snack and beverage giant PepsiCo (NASDAQ: PEP) has struggled over the past few years. The stock began diverging from arch-rival Coca-Cola in early 2024. It has fallen by about 20% since then, while Coca-Cola has risen by 57%. Additionally, PepsiCo is now 30% off its all-time high, a rare drop for the legendary dividend stock.

Trading at just 17 times trailing-12-month earnings, PepsiCo hasn't been this cheap in about six years and, to that point, seldom falls to such low valuations. But PepsiCo has made mistakes that justify the stock's decline -- enough that an activist investor took a $4 billion stake in the company to help get the train back on its tracks.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Here's why the signal to buy shares now is glaringly strong.

Working to right the ship

Most of PepsiCo's struggles lie in its core North America business. The company has raised prices over the years, and consumers started to push back. The rising popularity of obesity drugs, such as Wegovy and Zepbound, has only dialed up the pressure. Sales volumes have slumped, and growth has slowed.

Management has worked to course-correct its pricing, but North American beverage volume still fell 2% year over year in the third quarter of 2026, while food volumes were flat. Activist investor Elliott Management has been a proponent of cutting prices to boost volume and paring its U.S. product line to reduce costs.

Wall Street analysts currently estimate that PepsiCo will grow earnings by roughly 4% annually over the next three to five years. That's notably below Coca-Cola's 8% growth estimates, a sign that the current slump is weighing on the company's near-term upside. It goes a long way in explaining the stock's lackluster performance.

Cheap stocks aren't always strong buys. Here's why PepsiCo is.

An important part of being a long-term investor is assessing whether a business's model is broken or just a bump in the road that the company can overcome.

In PepsiCo's case, there's still so much to like . It dominates your local grocery store with a unique breadth of snack and beverage brands that consumers love. On top of that, management still plans to return $8.9 billion to shareholders through dividends and stock buybacks in 2026. That's a solid signal that management is confident in PepsiCo's stability and prospects going forward.

Story Continues

As I said above, the stock's valuation is uncharacteristically low right now. That gives investors a solid margin of safety in case PepsiCo doesn't get back on track as quickly as it hopes.

Shares yield a whopping 4.3% today and are backed by a huge balance sheet, making it unlikely that this Dividend King 's streak of 54 consecutive annual dividend increases will face a cut. The dividend could drive that 4% growth rate to an annualized total investment return of 8%, and there's double-digit upside if the company can get earnings growth closer to Coca-Cola's 8% over the long term.

Cheap stocks aren't always smart buys. But here, there seems to be a lot more room for upside than downside in this beaten-down dividend stalwart.

news.Title: Celestica sees 2027 sales nearly doubling to $40 billion
news.Content: Celestica expects revenue to nearly double to $40 billion in 2027 , a 90% increase from its outlook for this year, as major cloud and artificial intelligence customers ramp up demand for networking equipment and custom computing systems. The Canadian technology company designs and manufactures hardware used in large data centers, including high-speed network switches and systems built around specialized AI processors. The forecast follows a strong third quarter. Celestica's revenue jumped 83% from a year earlier to $5.83 billion , and adjusted earnings more than doubled to $3.30 per share, exceeding the company's previous guidance. Celestica ( CLS ) also raised its 2026 revenue forecast to $21 billion from $20.5 billion in its third-quarter earnings announcement on Oct. 26. Celestica shares jumped 12.62% to $277.76 in afternoon trading on Oct. 27. Google and OpenAI programs fuel Celestica's growth Celestica's Connectivity & Cloud Solutions business, which supplies data-center networking and computing equipment, generated $4.87 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 102% from a year earlier. Revenue from its Compute & Storage business grew 242%, driven by higher volumes of AI computing systems and demand for storage products, according to the company's quarterly filing . Also read: Broadcom gets major OpenAI boost in AI chip race Google is one of the customers behind Celestica's expansion plans. Celestica is increasing its U.S. manufacturing capacity to support systems built around Google's Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs, specialized chips designed to handle AI tasks. The company, which describes itself as a preferred manufacturing partner for Google's data-center hardware, expects its U.S. expansion to be completed in 2027. Celestica is also preparing to ramp production of hardware systems built around OpenAI's Jalapeño AI accelerator. OpenAI designed the processor with help from Broadcom, which provides chip implementation and networking technology. Celestica contributes circuit board, server rack, and system engineering expertise to help bring the platform into large-scale production. The companies announced the Jalapeño project in June , with plans to expand the custom AI computing platform over multiple generations. Beyond custom AI systems, Celestica supplies networking equipment that connects large numbers of processors inside data centers. Its 800-gigabit and 1.6-terabit Ethernet switches help move data between AI chips at high speeds. As cloud operators build larger AI clusters, they need faster connections to prevent data transfers from slowing down computing workloads. Story Continues Earlier this month, Celestica introduced the DS6005 , a liquid-cooled network switch designed to support dense AI clusters and reduce power consumption. At its Oct. 27 investor and Analyst Day, Celestica said customer demand forecasts for 2028 are already meaningfully higher than its $40 billion revenue outlook for 2027 . Management said those projections are based on programs Celestica has already won. However, the forecasts still depend on customer deployment schedules and do not represent guaranteed future revenue. Meeting the expected demand will require Celestica to expand its manufacturing capacity before many of the planned AI systems are ready for delivery. Celestica plans up to $2 billion to expand production Celestica expects to spend $1.5 billion to $2 billion on capital investments in 2027 , up from roughly $1 billion planned for 2026. The company is adding production capacity at its U.S. facilities in Texas, upgrading operations in Mexico and expanding its manufacturing campus in Thailand. Some of the investment will also go toward additional electrical capacity and automated production lines to assemble and test complex AI systems. More Artificial Intelligence: AI's biggest business opportunity may not look like AI AI racks are outgrowing old power: 2 chipmakers have a strategy BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive Celestica must pay for much of that expansion before the new equipment generates revenue. The company lowered its 2026 non-GAAP free-cash-flow forecast to $460 million from $600 million , citing additional working capital needed to prepare for next year's growth. Working capital includes money tied up in inventory and other operating needs. Celestica may need to buy components and increase production before customers pay for the completed hardware. Management said during its Oct. 27 earnings call that it expects a net use of cash in 2027 as capital spending and working capital requirements increase. Celestica has already raised additional funds to support its expansion. The company completed a $3.45 billion stock offering in August and ended September with approximately $4 billion in cash and cash equivalents . The expansion also leaves Celestica exposed to changes in the plans of its largest customers. Its latest quarterly filing shows that one customer accounted for 35% of third-quarter revenue , while its 10 largest customers generated 85%. If a major customer delays an AI project, changes its hardware requirements, or cuts planned spending, Celestica could be left with production capacity built for orders that arrive later than expected. The next test will be whether Celestica can bring its new factories and production lines online fast enough to deliver the nearly $19 billion in additional annual revenue it expects in 2027. news.Title: Why F5 Stock Is Getting Crushed Today
news.Content:
By most measures, shares of AI cybersecurity outfit F5 (NASDAQ:FFIV) should be up today. Its fiscal fourth-quarter revenue improved 13% year over year to $917 million, topping consensus estimates of $884 million. Adjusted per-share earnings of $4.42 also beat expectations of only around $4.30, up slightly from the year-ago comparison of $4.39.

Yet, FFIV stock is well down today. As of 12:51 p.m. ET, in fact, shares are more than 19% lower. What gives?

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Investors are panicking over what the company's guidance implies, although there's important context to add to the market's extreme bearish response.

Guidance suggests a slowdown

F5's guidance for the quarter and the year ahead isn't horrifying. Its top line for fiscal 2027 should grow between 8% and 9%, in line with consensus estimates. And, while the midpoints of earnings guidance ranges for the quarter and the year now underway are a tad shy of analysts' consensus figures, they still suggest respectable profit growth is in store from last year's $17.49 per share.

Image source: Getty Images.

The stumbling block is what the guidance numbers suggest. That's slowing growth and shrinking gross profit margins, ultimately suggesting that a major cyclical refresh of key product lines has already peaked. This prompted Piper Sandler to downgrade FFIV stock from overweight to neutral.

The market took that ball and ran with it, so to speak.

Perspective

The sheer scope of today's setback, however, is exaggerated given the company's past and projected results. And fanning today's bearish flames is the fact that, as of yesterday's close, shares were up nearly 80% since the beginning of the year, leaving them vulnerable to profit-taking regardless of F5's fourth-quarter results or forward-looking guidance. Investors just appear to be interpreting guidance in the worst possible light.

But, the sellers may have overshot their target.

Even before today's tumble and downgrade from Piper Sandler, the analyst community's consensus price target was $457.44, versus the ticker's current price near $370. Moreover, while Piper may have downgraded FFIV, Evercore ISI raised its price target in response to F5's fourth-quarter report, as did Barclays and Morgan Stanley . If you can stomach the volatility that likely awaits, today's sell-off is arguably a buying opportunity for risk-tolerant investors.

news.Title: Lumentum Shares Jump 135% YTD: Can AI Momentum Sustain the Rally?
news.Content:
Lumentum LITE shares have surged 135% year to date (YTD), outperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's return of 16.5%. The outperformance reflects investor optimism about the company's expanding role in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, accelerating demand for optical connectivity and improving profitability. These factors have helped LITE shares outperform peers, including Cisco Systems CSCO, Broadcom AVGO, and Coherent COHR YTD. Shares of Coherent and Cisco have returned 27.8% and 45.3%, respectively, while Broadcom shares have dropped 1.1%. Despite robust demand, LITE faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Apart from stiff competition, LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. So, what should investors do with the LITE stock? Let's find out.

LITE's Valuation

Lumentum faces challenges in expanding manufacturing capacity sufficiently to meet customer requirements. Tight availability of laser components and other materials could restrict shipments and delay revenue realization. The company is expanding ultra-high-power laser production across its San Jose, U.K. and Greensboro facilities.

The company suffers from customer concentration. LITE's dependence on a limited number of major customers exposes its business to changes in purchasing patterns and capital spending priorities. Lumentum is benefiting from increasing investments in AI data centers, which require high-bandwidth, low-latency optical connectivity. The transition from copper-based connections to optical technologies is creating opportunities across scale-out, scale-across and scale-up networking architectures. Increasing adoption of AI accelerators and larger computing clusters is driving demand for Lumentum's lasers, optical components and transceivers.

The company is benefiting from accelerating adoption of next-generation 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers as hyperscalers upgrade their AI networking infrastructure. Lumentum achieved record 800G shipments and initiated production shipments of 1.6T transceivers during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Lumentum expects the adoption of 1.6T transceivers to accelerate through calendar 2027, supported by deployments of custom AI clusters among leading hyperscale customers.

Lumentum's OCS business represents a significant growth opportunity as hyperscalers seek energy-efficient networking solutions. OCS technology enables dynamic traffic routing while reducing power consumption and optical signal losses compared with conventional electrical switching. news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Rallied Today
news.Content:
Shares of Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) charged sharply higher on Wednesday, jumping as much as 6.4%. As of 12:27 p.m. ET, the stock was still up 5.9%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist higher was a competitor's bullish financial report.

Image source: Getty Images.

Show me the money

Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) -- one of Sandisk's key rivals in the artificial intelligence (AI) chip space -- reported the results of its fiscal 2026 third quarter, and the results wowed investors. It reported record revenue that surged 328% year over year and 32% quarter over quarter to 104.6 trillion South Korean Won (roughly $78.9 billion). Operating profits were equally robust, soaring 632% year over year and 38% sequentially to 83.3 trillion won (roughly $61.7 billion).

To give the results perspective, analysts' consensus estimates were for revenue of 98.34 trillion won and operating profit of about 76.7 trillion won, so the results cleared both bars with ease.

Sandisk is one of the Big Three computer memory manufacturers, so it will profit from the supply and demand imbalance for memory chips -- which are critical to the ongoing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI).

Despite stock price gains of more than 650% over the past year, Sandisk is selling for just 19 times earnings, a valuation that is all the more meaningful since the company continues to grow at a triple-digit rate. Moreover, SK Hynix's commentary suggests the ongoing AI-related demand will continue through the end of the decade, which will benefit Sandisk shareholders.

That's why Sandisk stock is still a buy.

news.Title: Mark Zuckerberg's Meta Platforms Reported Negative Free Cash Flow for the First Time Since 2012. Here's Why That Milestone Matters for Shareholders.
news.Content:
Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META) just gave investors a fresh update on its financial results. During the third quarter, the social media empire reported revenue of $64.6 billion, which soared 26% year over year. This marked the third straight quarter that the top line grew by more than 25%, an impressive feat given how massive the business is.

But the story continues to be how much money Meta Platforms is spending on artificial intelligence (AI) investments. Operating income fell 37%, compressing the operating margin from 40% in Q3 2025 to 20% in the latest quarter.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

And in what was probably an unsurprising development, the company posted negative free cash flow (FCF) of $2.1 billion in Q3. This hasn't happened since 2012, the year that Meta Platforms, then called Facebook, went public. Here's what the FCF milestone means for shareholders.

Management is spending at a breakneck pace

During the third quarter, Meta Platforms' capital expenditures (capex) totaled $34.9 billion, up 80% year over year. This pushed FCF into negative territory, as the business burned $2.1 billion. It's been well over a decade since this has occurred. But given that fellow internet giant Alphabet reported negative FCF in the second quarter, investors must have seen this coming.

Meta Platforms is a hyperscaler . It's sparing no expense to build out AI-related compute capacity, primarily data centers and supporting technical infrastructure. Its capex figures have ballooned. And they are now expected to be $140 billion (at the midpoint) in 2026.

That spending is showing no signs of slowing. As of Sept. 30, Meta Platforms had $825 billion in future commitments, up from $643 billion as of June 30. That huge sum is equal to half of the company's total market capitalization. It's easy to believe this will continue to expand in future quarters.

This is no longer a capital-light enterprise that was printing cash. Meta Platforms has become a capital-intensive business. It's also borrowing to fund the AI build-out. Long-term debt is at $80.9 billion. Exactly four years ago, just before OpenAI launched ChatGPT, there was $9.9 billion in long-term debt on the balance sheet.

The consensus view among sell-side analysts is that Meta Platforms will report negative FCF of $10.6 billion in 2026. Next year, FCF will be in the red by almost $35 billion. Then in 2028, it will turn positive again. Take this forecast with a grain of salt, however, as nobody knows how the AI boom will evolve in the coming years.

Story Continues

For what it's worth, top-line gains have been robust. And during the third quarter, ad pricing rose 14%, while ad impressions grew 10%. Daily active users of its Family of Apps climbed to 3.64 billion. And Meta's Muse agent is a hit, with more than 10 million sign-ups in the U.S. and Canada so far. "About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on any given day," founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on the Q3 2026 earnings call.

Meet the new Meta

For investors, I think there are two parts to the story. This will shape your view of Meta Platforms as a portfolio candidate. The first development is that the business is probably riskier financially than it has ever been. Negative FCF and sizable debt show that this is the case. And there is uncertainty regarding the long-term payoff on the heightened capex.

Meta Platforms even paused stock buybacks. It repurchased $26.2 billion worth of shares in the first three quarters of 2025. But through the first nine months of this year, that figure was zero. A significant capital returns program is on hold.

The second takeaway is that assessing valuation is no longer a straightforward exercise. The stock looks compelling based on its price-to-earnings ratio of 22. But this doesn't paint the full picture. Shares trade at an expensive 65 times trailing FCF.

These are variables to consider before you buy this Magnificent Seven stock.

news.Title: Amazon Warns Employees Against Costly AI Habit
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) is telling its software engineers to use artificial intelligence aggressively, but not blindly.

In an updated internal engineering guideline, the company cautioned employees against tokenmaxxing, or maximizing AI-token usage simply to hit activity metrics, warning that doing so can raise costs without improving outcomes.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMZN.

Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Amazon said AI will be central to software engineering going forward and encouraged developers to incorporate the technology into their daily work. But management stressed that engineers should ultimately be measured by customer, business and team outcomes rather than by how many tokens they consume or how many AI tools they use.

The company said token usage, code changes and AI-adoption rates can still be useful indicators, but become dangerous when treated as targets.

Amazon explicitly warned that such metrics can create negative incentives, including higher costs and unnecessary complexity.

The guidance reflects a more mature stage of enterprise AI adoption.

Amazon said teams that embrace AI heavily are often seeing stronger productivity and delivery, but it also wants leaders to examine whether that usage is actually producing better output.

The company recommended paying close attention to both the lowest and highest ends of AI adoption, including teams that are not using AI effectively and teams that are using it heavily without matching delivery gains.

Amazon also stressed that engineers should understand when AI does not help.

An employee who can explain why a task is not improved by current AI tools is demonstrating judgment, not failure, the company said.

Investor Takeaway

I think the bigger story is that Amazon is moving from AI adoption to AI efficiency .

The company still wants engineers using AI, but it is clearly trying to avoid a culture where more tokens automatically means more productivity.

That matters because enterprise AI costs can scale quickly when thousands of employees use coding assistants and agentic tools every day.

For investors, the key things to watch are developer productivity, internal AI costs, adoption of Amazon's own AI tools and whether the company can translate heavier AI usage into faster software delivery without letting expenses run out of control .

The message is not use less AI.

It is prove that the AI you use is actually worth the cost.

According to data from Synergy Research Group, Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet held second-quarter 2026 worldwide cloud market shares of 28%, 20% and 15%, respectively. Microsoft and Alphabet are steadily narrowing the gap, applying sustained competitive pressure on AWS.

Strategic Partnerships of AWS in Q3

The third quarter brought several high-profile agreements that are likely to have shaped AWS' near-term positioning. Most notably, AWS and NVIDIA expanded their partnership in August to deploy two million additional NVIDIA GPUs during 2027-2028. AWS also signed a multi-year strategic collaboration agreement with Cognition, expanded its partnership with Salesforce, and agreed to acquire DuckLabs. Additionally, AWS became the first cloud provider approved for NATO RESTRICTED workloads across all member nations, while Agentic Grid Planning, built with Duke Energy, broadened the customer base across defense and utilities.

Story Continues

Infrastructure, Silicon and AI Innovation in Q3

AWS' third-quarter infrastructure investments are expected to have meaningfully shaped the operating cost base during the to-be-reported quarter. The planned investment of more than $5.3 billion in Saudi Arabia, where the first AWS region is slated to open in December 2026, is likely to have increased deployment-related expenses. Trainium adoption, backed by multi-year, multi-gigawatt commitments from Anthropic and OpenAI, supported AI workload absorption, while Annapurna Labs' collaboration with NVIDIA on custom high-bandwidth memory is expected to strengthen future Trainium generations.

Investment Perspective

Heading into the third-quarter print, AWS demonstrates promising indicators across accelerating revenues, a $496 billion backlog and broadening AI-silicon adoption among frontier labs and large enterprises. Customer wins announced in the to-be-reported quarter add further diversification across regulated industries.

However, investors should note that approximately $220 billion in planned 2026 capital expenditures, raised from $200 billion partly due to higher memory costs, are likely to have pressured third-quarter margins and free cash flow, which had already turned to a trailing 12-month outflow of $7.6 billion. AWS operating margin, reported at 39.4% in the second quarter, benefited from a one-time energy-derivative gain that is excluded from third-quarter guidance and might have moderated sequentially. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for earnings per share has moved 3.1% higher over the past 30 days to $2.01, but investors might consider awaiting clarity on AI-capacity returns and capital efficiency before adding to positions ahead of this Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) company's results. news.Title: Oklo Is Still Pre-Revenue. Here's What Actually Has to Happen Before That Changes.
news.Content:
After a spectacular surge in value, Oklo (NYSE: OKLO) stock has had a meltdown of its own. That's not an exaggeration: The stock has lost about 80% of its value since last October. As it turns out, the half-life of Wall Street's enthusiasm ("nuclear renaissance!") was pretty short.

Wall Street has cooled on artificial intelligence stocks, and it has grown especially wary of speculative stocks like Oklo. For its part, Oklo, which once carried a $30 billion market value at its peak and remains at roughly $5 billion even after its drop, trades at a hefty price relative to the little revenue it generated last quarter (about $1.2 million).

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

All that leaves plenty of room for the stock to fall further if investors continue losing patience. Oklo likely won't regain investor confidence until it's selling nuclear power . And that likely won't happen until it overcomes a few major hurdles.

What needs to happen before Oklo generates revenue

For starters, Oklo is designing a small nuclear reactor, which it calls an Aurora powerhouse. These powerhouses will be assembled in factories -- potentially cutting costs and time to deployment -- and deployed to industrial sites and data centers to generate power on-site. These reactors, in turn, could help fill a gap in power generation, which is expected to widen as electricity demand outpaces utilities' ability to keep up.

Oklo has interested customers lined up, but it doesn't have a certified reactor. This is the first major hurdle: Oklo needs regulatory approval before it can commercialize its Aurora powerhouse. Although it is working through the process -- and has made impressive progress this year -- it does not have permission to switch on reactors and start selling power.

The company doesn't have a firm date for when it will turn on its first powerhouse. In the meantime, annual revenue will likely be insignificant, as the chart below illustrates.

OKLO Revenue (TTM) data by YCharts

We could stop at regulation, but let's go a step further -- for Oklo to generate significant revenue, it also has to build the powerhouse. Indeed, building a nuclear power plant isn't like rolling out a new running shoe. Nuclear power is notoriously expensive, and even if Oklo's reactors are small, high construction costs could force it to charge electricity prices that customers aren't willing to pay. That could turn away potential buyers, especially if cheaper solutions are available at that time.

Story Continues

Until it deploys its first reactor, Oklo's revenue will likely be small. Add to that the fact that Oklo will likely move at the pace of nuclear energy, which is to say slow, sometimes frustratingly slow, and this stock could struggle to regain its footing. If that pace doesn't agree with your time horizon, investing in Oklo might not be right for you.

news.Title: Is UPS a Buy After Its Latest Earnings Report?
news.Content:
Shares of United Parcel Service (NYSE:UPS) rose nearly 5.8% on Oct. 27, the day of the company's third-quarter earnings report, after UPS delivered a beat-and-raise quarter.

The shipping giant reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.69, beating Wall Street consensus estimates by $0.06. Revenue of $22.9 billion topped expectations by over $600 million.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Additionally, UPS raised its full-year outlook, now expecting $92.6 billion in total revenue and an adjusted operating profit of roughly $8.75 billion. Previously, management had guided for $91.2 billion in total revenue and an adjusted operating profit of roughly $8.65 billion.

Is the stock a buy after its latest earnings report?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Executing on the turnaround plan

In late 2024, UPS launched a turnaround plan called "Efficiency Reimagined," which focused on cutting costs, leaning into automation, and exiting low-margin businesses and entering higher-performing ones.

The company cut 48,000 jobs in 2025 and another 30,000 earlier this year, while also closing many of its facilities as well. UPS has also significantly reduced the amount of shipping it does for Amazon due to the many lower-margin packages it ships for the e-commerce giant.

Now, UPS is focusing on shipping for businesses that provide better margins, such as healthcare, small- to medium-sized businesses willing to pay higher rates, business-to-business, and complex industrial sectors like data centers.

UPS also recently announced a new global operating model in which the company will have a core standardized model across all its markets, while still providing teams with the flexibility to adapt to their local market needs.

"... These results show that our strategy is working," UPS CEO Carol Tomé said on the company's third-quarter earnings call. "We're driving more premium growth, improving revenue quality and mix, and creating greater operating leverage through a more efficient network. All of this is strengthening the underlying performance of our business."

In the quarter, UPS' U.S. domestic business grew revenue 4.5% year over year, while generating an operating margin of 6.1%. The international segment grew revenue 7.1% and had an operating margin of 14.9%. The company's smallest segment, supply chain logistics, grew revenue by over 18% and achieved an operating margin of 3.1% (9% on an adjusted basis).

Story Continues

UPS has benefited from the data center boom by shipping critical software, such as chips, that are often time-sensitive and, in some cases, require special care.

On the earnings call, Tomé sized UPS' logistics opportunities of data centers at $15 billion alone.

Is the stock a buy?

As seen in the market's reaction to the earnings report, Wall Street analysts are optimistic about UPS' prospects.

Truist analyst Lucas Servera raised his price target on the stock by $5 to $120 per share and maintained a buy rating on the stock, noting that the recent results, as well as management's comments, give him confidence that the company can improve revenue, continue to make productivity gains, and improve margins next year.

With management having executed much of the turnaround so far, UPS's valuation has improved. But if the company continues to boost margins, the stock can continue to move higher over the long term.

UPS PE Ratio data by YCharts

Additionally, the stock has a very compelling trailing dividend yield of 6.25%. Projected dividends this year of $5.4 billion are covered by expected adjusted free cash flow of $6.1 billion.

UPS also hasn't cut its dividend since it went public in 1999, so management is likely to make every possible effort to maintain the dividend. For all of these reasons, I think investors can buy the stock right now.

news.Title: Can UiPath's Rising ARR Drive Sustained Growth for PATH Stock?
news.Content:
UiPath PATH continues to strengthen its position in enterprise automation, supported by growing demand for AI-driven workflow solutions and recurring subscription revenues. The company's expanding annualized renewal run-rate (ARR) highlights its ability to retain customers, deepen enterprise relationships and generate predictable revenues.

With businesses increasingly prioritizing operational efficiency and AI adoption, UiPath's recurring revenue growth could provide a foundation for long-term expansion.

PATH's ARR Growth Strengthens Revenue Visibility

UiPath's ARR reached $1.94 billion in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, increasing 12.5% year over year from $1.72 billion. This compares with $1.04 billion in the corresponding quarter of fiscal 2024, reflecting the company's expanding enterprise automation footprint.

The sustained increase indicates growing adoption of UiPath's automation solutions as enterprises seek to streamline operations and reduce manual workloads.

UiPath's focus on agentic automation, which combines artificial intelligence agents, robots and human decision-making, offers additional opportunities to expand its presence within existing customer accounts.

Moreover, its expanding automation capabilities could help enterprises integrate AI into complex business processes, supporting customer retention and subscription growth.

Will ARR Momentum Support PATH's Future?

UiPath's recurring revenue model provides greater business visibility and opportunities for cross-selling advanced automation solutions. Growing enterprise interest in AI-powered productivity tools could further strengthen demand.

However, competitive pressure, prolonged enterprise purchasing decisions and challenges in monetizing newer AI offerings could limit growth.

Sustaining double-digit ARR expansion while improving profitability will remain important for UiPath's long-term investment appeal.

How Do MSFT and CRM Compare With PATH?

Microsoft MSFT and Salesforce CRM are two U.S.-listed technology companies expanding their enterprise AI and automation capabilities. Microsoft integrates automation through Power Automate and AI-driven Copilot solutions, benefiting from its extensive enterprise software ecosystem. Microsoft also leverages cloud infrastructure and existing customer relationships to accelerate adoption.

Salesforce offers workflow automation and AI capabilities through its Agentforce platform, targeting improved customer engagement and productivity. Salesforce benefits from its established CRM ecosystem and expanding enterprise AI offerings. While Microsoft enjoys broad technological diversification, Salesforce maintains a strong position in customer relationship management, creating competitive challenges for UiPath's specialized automation platform.

Story Continues

PATH's Price Performance, Estimates

The stock has declined 13% over the past year compared with the industry's 11% decrease.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

From a valuation standpoint, PATH trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.05, well below the industry's 28.52. It carries a Value Score of C.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for PATH's fiscal 2027 earnings has declined over the past 30 days.

PATH currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: 2 Fintech Stocks to Buy While Their Customer Numbers Keep Climbing
news.Content:
SoFi (NASDAQ: SOFI) and Robinhood (NASDAQ: HOOD) both disrupted older financial companies with their fintech platforms . SoFi, which initially offered only student loans, evolved into a "one-stop shop" for personal loans, auto loans, mortgages, credit cards, insurance plans, estate planning services, and stock and crypto trading tools. Robinhood challenged traditional brokerages with commission-free trading, and expanded its ecosystem to include cryptocurrencies, tokenized assets, prediction market trading, and digital banking services.

Both companies are still gaining new customers in this challenging market, but their stocks have stumbled as rising Treasury yields have compressed their valuations. Over the past 12 months, SoFi's stock has declined 46%, while Robinhood's stock has dropped 38%. However, those pullbacks could be great buying opportunities for investors who can stomach a little volatility.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

How fast is SoFi growing?

SoFi's digital-native approach made it a popular choice for younger people who didn't want to deal with traditional banks. It also acquired the digital payment processing company Galileo in 2020, launched its own digital bank after receiving a U.S. bank charter in 2022, and acquired the cloud-native banking platform Technisys that same year.

In the third quarter of 2026, SoFi's members grew 35% year over year to 17.1 million, while its total products in use rose 44% to 26.7 million. That's up from just 2.5 million members and 1.9 million products in use at the end of 2021. Galileo, which operates separately from its core business, hosts another 140 million accounts.

From 2021 to 2025, SoFi's adjusted net revenue grew at a 37% CAGR, as its adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) rose at a 227% CAGR. It also turned profitable under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) in 2024 and 2025.

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect SoFi's adjusted net revenue and adjusted EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 29% and 38%, respectively. That growth should be fueled by its loan platform business (which originates loans for third parties to earn high-margin referral fees), new blockchain-based services (tokenized assets and stablecoins), and more direct deposits. It also plans to further expand and monetize Galileo and Technisys.

Story Continues

With an enterprise value of $20.6 billion, SoFi trades at just three times next year's sales and 10 times next year's adjusted EBITDA. Even though it's a high-growth fintech company, it's still valued like a conventional bank -- so it could have a lot more upside potential.

How fast is Robinhood growing?

Robinhood ended the third quarter of 2026 with 28.7 million funded customers. That's up 7% from a year earlier. At the end of 2021, it had only 22.7 million funded accounts.

From 2021 to 2025, Robinhood's revenue and adjusted EBITDA grew at CAGRs of 25% and 193%, respectively. Like SoFi, it also turned profitable on a GAAP basis in 2024 and 2025.

Robinhood's growth was initially driven by the buying frenzy in meme stocks, riskier options, and cryptocurrencies in 2020 and 2021. Its commission-free trades and streamlined app made it a popular option among younger retail investors. Its growth cooled off in 2022 as rising interest rates drove many investors to park their cash in more conservative investments, but heated up again over the following years as the AI boom pulled them back toward higher-growth stocks.

Robinhood also expanded its subscription platform, Robinhood Gold, to lock in its customers with higher interest rates, more margin, and other perks. Its number of Gold subscribers grew 34% year over year to a record 5.2 million in the third quarter of 2026. Its growth in subscription revenue is gradually reducing its dependence on cyclical transaction-based revenues -- which it mainly generates by selling its "free" trades to high-frequency trading firms.

From 2025 to 2028, analysts expect Robinhood's revenue and adjusted EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 21% and 24%, respectively. That growth should be driven by new features (especially prediction markets and tokenized real-world assets), the expansion of its digital banking ecosystem (including its new cards and Trump accounts), and Gold subscriptions.

With an enterprise value of $79.4 billion, Robinhood trades at just 12 times and 20 times next year's revenue and adjusted EBITDA, respectively. It's cheap because investors are pricing in another cyclical slowdown in trading as the macro headwinds intensify -- but its growth, scale, and shrewd diversification should help it bounce back and soar higher over the long term.

news.Title: Prediction: This Dividend Growth ETF Will Outperform the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF Over the Next 20 Years. Here's Why.
news.Content:
The S&P 500 's (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) 10 largest holdings currently comprise 40% of its value. This broad market index hasn't been this concentrated since the 1960s. The next 20 years were a weak period for the S&P 500. That doesn't bode well for the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO), which tracks the S&P 500.

That's one factor driving my view that the iShares Core Dividend Growth ETF (NYSEMKT: DGRO) will outperform the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF over the next 20 years.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The current concentration problem

Like the S&P 500 index that it tracks, the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF currently has a high concentration in the largest technology stocks. Its 10 largest holdings currently comprise nearly 40% of the fund, and technology companies also make up around 40% of its holdings. That's due to the robust returns of large tech stocks, including the " Magnificent Seven ," over the past decade. They've delivered strong earnings growth and stock returns by capitalizing on megatrends like cloud computing, AI, and increased digitalization.

The concern is that the last time the S&P 500 was this concentrated, its returns suffered over the subsequent two decades. According to data from S&P Global , the S&P 500's annualized returns from 1965 to 1975 were just over 1%. While the S&P 500's annualized returns were stronger over the next decade at almost 11%, that still works out to around 6% annualized over those 20 years. While that historical performance doesn't guarantee the next 20 years will see a repeat, the current concentration increases the risk of lower future returns for VOO.

A proven winning strategy with lower tech concentration

Whereas VOO tracks an index of the 500 largest publicly traded companies in the U.S., iShares Core Dividend Growth ETF tracks an index of U.S. companies with a history of dividend growth. It screens for stocks that have delivered at least five years of dividend growth. It also screens for positive earnings growth forecasts and a payout ratio below 75%, and excludes the top 10% by yield. That puts DGRO's holdings in a solid position to continue growing their dividends.

That focus on dividend growers is noteworthy. Data from Ned Davis Research and Hartford Funds found that over the last 50 years, dividend growers have delivered a 10.2% annualized total return. That outperformed dividend non-payers (4.2%) and an equal-weighted S&P 500 index (7.7%). DGRO's focus on dividend growers has paid off, with the fund delivering a 12% annualized return since its inception in 2014.

Story Continues

Meanwhile, DGRO has much less concentration. Its top 10 holdings account for 27% of its value, while tech companies account for only 18%. Its largest holding is oil giant ExxonMobil (3.3% weighting). Contrast that with VOO's top holding, Nvidia, at 8.4%.

The potential to deliver market-beating returns

The S&P 500's heavy concentration in top tech stocks could affect its returns over the coming decades as the economy evolves. Meanwhile, DGRO's lower concentration and focus on dividend growers potentially position it to deliver strong returns over the next 10 years. That drives my view that DGRO will beat VOO over the next 20 years.

news.Title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. Dell Technologies: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
news.Content:
As the artificial intelligence era moves from experimentation to massive infrastructure deployment, investors are comparing Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL) to find the best way to profit.

While both companies are central to modern computing, they serve different functions. One designs the advanced chips that power complex calculations, while the other assembles the servers and storage systems that businesses rely on. Understanding their distinct business models is key to choosing the right stock.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

Advanced Micro Devices designs high-performance, adaptive computing products for a wide range of customers across the cloud, embedded systems, and gaming markets.

The company is a key player in the semiconductor sector, providing essential processors for data centers and personal computers. Its semi-custom chips power the Sony (NYSE:SONY) PlayStation 5 and the Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) Xbox Series consoles, according to its latest annual report.

In October 2025, the company also entered into a multiyear agreement with OpenAI to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, and in February 2026, it signed a similar 6-gigawatt agreement with Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META).

Both customers received warrants to buy up to 160 million AMD shares each at $0.01 per share, with vesting contingent on purchases and stock price milestones being met.

AMD's annual report says it depends on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its business, and one customer accounted for 11% of its receivables at the end of 2025. This level of customer concentration adds risk to the business.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, revenue reached nearly $34.6 billion, up about 34.3% from the prior fiscal year. Strong demand for its AI infrastructure and data center products drove this increase.

The company reported net income of roughly $4.3 billion for the same period. This marks a substantial improvement in profitability as the company scales its newest chip architectures.

Growth has accelerated since. In the second quarter of 2026, ended June 27, revenue rose 50% year over year to $11.5 billion and net income reached $2.3 billion, with data center revenue up 107% to $6.7 billion.

Management guided third-quarter revenue to approximately $13 billion, plus or minus $300 million. On Sept. 28, 2026, AMD announced an agreement to acquire World Labs, the spatial-intelligence lab led by Fei-Fei Li, for approximately $8.2 billion in AMD stock, with closing expected by the end of 2026.

Story Continues

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company maintains a very healthy financial position with a debt-to-equity ratio of about 0.05x, based on total debt of $3.2 billion against $63 billion of stockholders' equity. This ratio, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, indicates that the company carries very little debt relative to its equity base.

The current ratio is approximately 2.9x, indicating the company has $2.90 in short-term assets for every $1.00 in short-term liabilities. Free cash flow from continuing operations for the fiscal year ended Dec. 27, 2025, was about $5.5 billion, or operating cash flow of $6.5 billion less $974 million of capital expenditures.

Operating cash flow including the divested ZT Systems manufacturing business was $7.7 billion. Note that stock-based compensation of $1.6 billion represented roughly 25% of operating cash flow from continuing operations, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement. The debt picture has also changed.

In August 2026, AMD issued $4.75 billion of senior notes for general corporate purposes, more than doubling the $3.25 billion of note principal on its June balance sheet.

The case for Dell Technologies

Dell Technologies provides a broad range of hardware and software solutions, from personal laptops to complex data center infrastructure.

The company serves a diverse global customer base, including large enterprises, public institutions, and small businesses. Its infrastructure segment is currently seeing high demand for AI-optimized servers and storage solutions that help organizations manage massive datasets.

Although the company no longer serves as a primary distributor for stand-alone VMware products, it continues to integrate those solutions into its specialized hardware offerings. Dell uses both a direct sales force and a global partner network to reach international markets.

According to its latest annual report for the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $113.5 billion. This was an increase of nearly 18.8% year over year, reflecting a recovery in the PC market and growth in AI-related hardware.

Net income for the period was about $5.9 billion, for a net margin of roughly 5.2%. This net margin, which measures the percentage of revenue remaining as profit after all expenses, shows the company operates with thinner margins than specialized chip designers but makes up for it with massive volume.

The newest quarter showed a step change. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended July 31, 2026, revenue rose 58% year over year to a record $47.0 billion and net income reached $4.1 billion.

The AI server business booked a record $60.9 billion in orders, recognized $16.4 billion in revenue, and exited the quarter with a record $95 billion backlog. Management raised its full-year fiscal 2027 revenue outlook by $25 billion to $192 billion.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the company reported negative stockholders' equity of $2.5 billion and total debt of $31.5 billion, so a meaningful debt-to-equity ratio cannot be calculated. Years of share repurchases, including $6 billion in fiscal 2026 alone, have left total liabilities above total assets.

The current ratio is roughly 0.9x, which measures the ability to cover short-term liabilities with short-term assets. Despite these balance sheet figures, the company generates significant cash, reporting free cash flow of nearly $8.6 billion for the fiscal year ended Jan. 30, 2026, measured as operating cash flow of $11.2 billion less $2.6 billion of capital expenditures and capitalized software costs.

This cash flow provides the company with the flexibility to fund operations and return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Dell said it returned a record $4.3 billion to shareholders in the July quarter, and its board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.63 per share.

Risk profile comparison

Advanced Micro Devices faces intense competition in the data center and PC markets from Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) and Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA).

The company also faces significant geopolitical risks, particularly U.S. export controls on AI chips for the China market. Restrictions on its MI308 data center GPUs led to approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025, though AMD released about $360 million of that reserve in the fourth quarter.

Furthermore, the company relies heavily on third-party manufacturers like Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM) and GlobalFoundries (NASDAQ:GFS) for wafer fabrication.

Disruptions in these manufacturing relationships or capacity constraints could significantly affect product supply. Shareholders also face dilution. The OpenAI and Meta warrants cover up to 320 million shares combined, nearly a fifth of the 1.63 billion shares outstanding in July 2026, and the World Labs purchase will be paid in stock.

Dell Technologies operates in the highly competitive IT infrastructure and PC markets, where it faces pressure from both traditional hardware brands and large infrastructure-as-a-service providers.

The company also faces cybersecurity risks, as any compromise of sensitive data could trigger regulatory investigations or reputational damage. Its supply chain depends on a few contract manufacturers, primarily located in Asia, and on single-source or limited-source suppliers for some components, making it vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions and price volatility.

Additionally, the company's negative equity and $34.5 billion of total debt as of July 31, 2026, leave less cushion than AMD's balance sheet if AI server demand slows, and its recurring-revenue contracts allow customers to reduce usage or terminate early.

Valuation comparison

Dell Technologies appears to be the more value-oriented investment given its lower revenue and earnings multiples, whereas Advanced Micro Devices trades at a premium.

Metric

Advanced Micro Devices

Dell Technologies

Forward P/E

70.4x

17.6x

P/S ratio

21.3x

1.9x

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Dell is the better buy today, but its stock has already roughly tripled over the past year, so the case from here rests on a record backlog converting into profit.

That backlog stood at $95 billion after the quarter ended July 31, 2026, when revenue grew by more than half and management sharply raised its full-year revenue outlook. For a company trading at a fraction of AMD's earnings multiple, that's an unusual mix of hypergrowth and a value price.

The balance sheet is the catch. Dell carries a heavy debt load against negative equity, and its margins are thin enough that a pause in AI spending could quickly show up in results.

AMD looks like the stronger business over the next decade, and the latest quarter showed why. Data center revenue more than doubled, and both OpenAI and Meta have signed agreements covering up to 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs apiece. The price already reflects that. Shares trade at a forward earnings multiple several times that of Dell, and dilution is coming.

Each of those two customers holds penny warrants that could vest into nearly a tenth of the share count, and the all-stock World Labs purchase adds more shares on top. I'd want a better entry price before owning the chipmaker's long-term story.

Dell wins this comparison on price, while AMD remains the one to watch on the next pullback.

news.Title: Wall St treads water as chips rise, megacaps fall ahead of Fed, Big Tech earnings
news.Content:
By Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi

Oct 28 (Reuters) - US stocks were choppy on Wednesday as weakness in megacaps such as Tesla and Apple offset chipmaker gains sparked by SK Hynix's bumper results, while investors awaited hyperscaler earnings and the Federal ‌Reserve's interest-rate decision later in the day.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology jumped 4.8% to its highest in over two weeks after South ‌Korean rival SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold jump in quarterly profit, boosted by AI infrastructure demand. SK Hynix's US-listed shares gained 12.2%.

The Philadelphia chips index was ​up 0.9%, on track to gain for the fourth straight session.

Limiting gains in main benchmarks, most megacap and growth stocks traded lower. Tesla dipped 1.3% after surging more than 9% in the last two sessions. Apple eased 0.5%, while SpaceX dropped 2.4%.

At 11:39 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 155.89 points, or 0.30%, to 52,533.46. The S&P 500 gained 16.89 points, or 0.22%, to 7,739.58, while the Nasdaq Composite added 4.35 points, or ‌0.02%, to 26,482.16.

Six of the 11 major S&P ⁠500 sectors advanced, with energy leading gains, tracking higher crude oil prices.

The Nasdaq has risen about 2% so far this week, following a bruising first half of the month, as sentiment toward AI improved after Anthropic ⁠revealed its US IPO filing on Monday.

The focus now shifts to quarterly results from hyperscalers Microsoft and Alphabet, due after markets close on Wednesday, with both companies expected to report accelerating cloud growth.

Investors will closely scrutinize their capital expenditure plans for signs that massive AI investments are generating returns, as concerns over ​the ​viability of debt-funded spending amid rising borrowing costs continue to weigh on the ​sector.

"We can still see that the AI demand has ‌not paused... the number one worry for investors is not AI valuations anymore, but it's the financing through debt as debt goes through the roof in the US," said Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group.

Alphabet shares advanced 1% following a media report that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips.

Also on the day, Vertiv jumped 13.2% after the digital infrastructure provider raised full-year profit and revenue forecasts, while also topping third-quarter estimates.

Boston Scientific shed 6.6% after the medical device maker trimmed annual profit forecast.

Third-quarter earnings growth for S&P 500 companies is ‌seen at 31.8%, revised from 31% estimated last week, according to LSEG data.

Story Continues

Looking ahead, ​the US Fed's policy announcement is due at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday. The ​market consensus is widely tilted toward a pause following last ​month's hike, with investors more focused on remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and the policy outlook.

Market expectations, ‌however, remain hawkish as traders see at least three 25-basis-point ​increases by late 2027, according to ​LSEG data, as persistently high inflation due to rising energy costs tied to the Middle East conflict bolster the case for tighter monetary policy.

September's Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, could test those bets on Thursday. Third-quarter GDP, expected to ​show 3.2% growth, is also due this week.

Declining ‌issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.38-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by 1.05-to-1 on the Nasdaq.

news.Title: The Energy Transition in 5 Numbers: Where Solar, Nuclear, and Gas Stand Heading Into 2027
news.Content:
Energy is having a moment. As countries decarbonize, artificial intelligence (AI) data centers consume more power, manufacturing returns home, and the grid electrifies, demand for reliable energy is surging. This has put energy and utility stocks , traditionally viewed as boring, slow-growth dividend plays, at the center of a critical bottleneck for hyperscalers and the broader economy.

With the energy transition underway, here are five numbers that reveal where solar, nuclear, and natural gas stand heading into 2027.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. Global energy demand is set to grow 3.8% in 2027

According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), electricity demand is projected to grow 3.8% globally next year, above the 10-year average growth rate of 2.7%.

Rising demand from AI data centers, which require significantly more power per server rack than before, is driving this strong growth. Additionally, increasing industrial activity and rising EV adoption are placing greater strain on the grid.

2. Solar power will add 600 TWh of output next year

The IEA says low-emissions energy sources are growing so quickly that they can meet global demand growth through 2027. Solar power is driving this growth, projected to add 600 TWh (terawatt-hours) of output annually through 2027.

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), solar power will lead U.S. electricity generation growth, thanks to strong growth in ERCOT (Texas), CAISO (California), and MISO (which covers 15 states across the Midwest and South). EIA projects ERCOT will add 13 TWh and MISO will add 11 TWh of solar production by 2027.

For investors seeking exposure to the growing use of solar energy, NextEra Energy (NYSE: NEE) is a massive regulated utility company that has aggressively expanded its solar capacity and boasts the largest fleet of renewable assets in North America.

3. Nuclear capacity is coming online with two plant restarts in the U.S.

While many investors are intrigued by advanced nuclear reactors, such as small modular reactors (SMRs) and microreactors, new nuclear capacity coming online in 2027 will largely come from fleet restarts and uprates.

Next year, two decommissioned nuclear reactors will come back online: the Palisades Nuclear Plant in Michigan and the Crane Clean Energy Center (formerly Three Mile Island Unit 1) in Pennsylvania.

Story Continues

Privately held Holtec owns and operates Palisades, while Constellation Energy (NASDAQ: CEG) owns and operates the Crane Clean Energy Center, which is backed by a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft .

Constellation Energy, the largest nuclear fleet operator in the U.S., also has projects to increase nuclear capacity at plants in Illinois and Pennsylvania. Southern Company (NYSE: SO) is another utility with uprate plans at its Hatch and Vogtle plants in Georgia.

4. Slow grid interconnection times could require 48 GW of natural gas capacity by 2035

While not as clean-burning as nuclear or solar power, natural gas is another vital fuel driving the energy transition. Many view natural gas as a "bridge fuel" because it is an efficient power source with lower emissions than fossil fuels like coal, helping meet energy needs while renewable and nuclear infrastructure scales up.

According to BloombergNEF, grid delays and slow connection times could mean 48 GW of natural gas generation must come online by 2035 to meet growing data center power demand. Power equipment manufacturers like GE Vernova (NYSE: GEV) and Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) are seeing historic demand for their natural-gas-fired equipment.

5. Data center energy demand will roughly double by 2030

Power demand is expected to keep growing well into the future. According to the IEA, global data center energy consumption could roughly double to 945 TWh by 2030, and grow to 1,200 TWh by 2035. On top of this, reshoring manufacturing to the U.S. and Europe is expected to further increase energy demand.

Energy is the lifeblood of the economy and has become increasingly central to the global financial system for several reasons. As countries lower emissions and meet growing demand, investors should expect more solar power, natural gas turbines, and nuclear uprates and plant restarts in 2027 and beyond.

news.Title: Microsoft names the hackers who slipped in through a backup app
news.Content:
Every business owner keeps a mental list of the keys that matter. The bank login, the payroll account, the alarm code for the front door.

What rarely makes that list are the apps your IT provider plugged into your company email years ago. They don't log in like a person or get a text code. They just run in the background.

Most small companies outsource IT to managed service providers, or MSPs, which wire backup and security tools straight into each client's Microsoft 365 account.

Each tool holds standing permission to read and write your data with no person signing in, according to Help Net Security . For you, that's convenience. For a hacker, it's a skeleton key.

Last week, one of those keys was stolen. Attackers took a credential for ConnectWise Cloud Backup, a tool many MSPs use to back up clients' email and files, and used it to walk into company accounts one after another.

If your IT is outsourced, this story deserves ten minutes of your week.

What happened in the ConnectWise breach

On Oct. 15, someone using the backup app's identity started requesting access to customer accounts from a hosting-provider address, according to BleepingComputer . ConnectWise, which bought SkyKick in September 2024, disclosed the problem the next day, Techzine reported.

Huntress, a security firm that watches over small businesses, saw sign-in attempts from the attackers' address on about 1,000 Microsoft accounts, and around 300 of them succeeded, according to Security Affairs .

ConnectWise disabled seven application identities on Oct. 17 and took Cloud Backup offline. It later suspended its SaaS Security and Cloud Management services too, Dark Reading reported.

Related: Polymarket customer struggles to claw back funds lost to fraud

On Oct. 21, Microsoft named a culprit. It said Storm-0940, a China-state-aligned group active since 2021, used an AI-driven hacking tool called ARTEX to hit more than 2,250 accounts at a pace of 2,900 sign-in attempts per minute, according to CSO Online .

In several cases, the group went from picking a target to privileged access in under three hours, Microsoft wrote in its report, as quoted by Security Affairs . Most attempts failed. The ones that landed moved fast.

Why a stolen key can cost you real money

A backup tool has to see everything it protects. The compromised app could reach mailboxes, OneDrive and SharePoint files, Teams chats and the company directory, according to Cybernews .

Email is where small business money usually disappears. Business email compromise cost U.S. victims just over $3 billion in 2025, according to an analysis of FBI data cited by Insurance Business .

Story Continues

More Cyber Threats :

Bernie Sanders sounds alarm on AI agents in your bank account

Amazon caught hackers probing a PHP flaw 4 days before the fix

Meta Muse closes dangerous privacy loophole after researchers exploit it

The FBI logged 24,768 of those complaints [VERIFY vs IC3 2025 report]. By my math, that's roughly $123,000 lost per reported case.

The scheme is simple. A crook sitting in your mailbox studies how you bill, then emails a customer a real-looking invoice with new bank details, or asks your bookkeeper to update a vendor's account. With a hijacked account, the email really does come from you.

For a company with 20 employees, one diverted payment of that size can mean a missed payroll or a drained credit line. That's the dollar stake behind a story that sounds technical.

Here's what researchers found inside affected accounts:

In about 50 accounts Huntress monitors, ConnectWise management apps gave themselves directory roles, mostly Exchange Administrator, according to BleepingComputer .

In at least one, a ConnectWise Teams app made itself a global administrator and, within about five minutes, added new credentials to two other trusted apps, Help Net Security reported.

After getting in, the attackers changed app credentials and tried to alter privileged roles, Microsoft said, according to The Hacker News .

Switching off the app doesn't lock every door

ConnectWise says its stored backup archives remain encrypted and isolated, with no sign they were touched, according to Dark Reading . The company has also said it can't see inside customer accounts, so it can't tell whether any one business was hit, a separate Dark Reading report noted.

That leaves the cleanup to you and your provider. Microsoft warned that the attackers' changes "can remain active as a backdoor" even after the original app is fixed, according to CSO Online .

Here's the detail I'd flag for every owner: you may be exposed even if you stopped using SkyKick years ago. ConnectWise told partners to check accounts with dormant SkyKick connections, according to Techzine , because the permission stays in place until someone removes it.

Huntress also told administrators to disable the ConnectWise apps rather than delete them, and to check every app for credentials added since Oct. 13, iTnews reported.

Three questions to ask your IT provider this week

I asked Elli Shlomo, head of security research at Guardz, a cybersecurity company that sells to MSPs, what an owner with no security staff should actually do. He boiled it down to three questions.

"First: 'Was the ConnectWise Cloud Backup app connected to our Microsoft 365, is it disabled now, and did you check the sign-in logs for activity that didn't come from the vendor?'" Shlomo said.

"Second: 'What changed while it was connected?'" he said. "In some tenants the app gave itself administrator rights and added new credentials to other apps, so you want a check for new admin roles, new app secrets and new mailbox forwarding rules, not just a password reset."

His third question looks past this one vendor. "Third: 'Which other vendor apps hold this kind of access to our email and files, and when were they last reviewed?' A good provider has already done all three and can show you the evidence," Shlomo said.

That last line is the real test. If your provider can't hand you a written answer, you've learned something about who's guarding your accounts.

Ransomware crews now hunt for company backups

On Oct. 20, the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and international partners warned that SafePay, one of 2026's most active ransomware crews, has hit about 600 victims since August 2024, according to HSToday .

SafePay operators shut off a built-in Windows snapshot service and reset network storage drives holding backups to factory settings. In some cases they deleted every network-attached backup before negotiations began, GBHackers reported.

The agencies' fix is familiar advice with new urgency. Keep backups that are offline, encrypted and impossible to alter, and regularly test that you can restore from them, according to HSToday .

There's a practical gap to close, too. ConnectWise Cloud Backup has been paused since Oct. 17, so ask your provider whether your email has been backed up since then and when restores return].

This breach will fade from the headlines. The permissions it exposed won't, unless someone goes looking for them.

Ten minutes and three questions this week could spare you a six-figure invoice scam later. For the business you've spent years building, that's cheap insurance.

Related: When AI attacks, who fights back?
