news.Title: Why Micron Technology Stock Rallied Today
news.Content:
Shares of Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) popped on Wednesday, jumping as much as 5.5%. As of 11:31 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 4.8%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The catalyst that sent the semiconductor specialist higher was a rival's robust financial report.

Image source: Getty Images.

Show me the money

Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) reported its fiscal 2026 third-quarter results, and investors were clearly impressed. The company reported record revenue of 104.6 trillion South Korean Won (roughly $78.9 billion), up 328% year over year and 32% quarter over quarter. At the same time, operating profit of 83.3 trillion won (roughly $61.7 billion) soared 632% year over year and 38% sequentially.

For context, analysts' consensus estimates called for revenue of 98.34 trillion won and operating profit of about 76.7 trillion won, so the results easily surpassed investor expectations.

However, what really turned heads was management commentary about the state of the industry. SK Hynix's outlook speaks volumes: "Demand [is] expected to outpace supply through 2030." The company also noted that its supply is essentially sold out for the next three years. There have been fears that demand for memory chips would begin to decline starting in 2028, so this pronouncement was cheered by investors.

The company also announced that it would return 100 trillion won to shareholders, including at least 30 trillion won in cash dividends and 60 trillion won via share buybacks.

As one of the Big Three computer memory manufacturers, Micron will benefit from the ongoing demand for High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM), Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM), and NAND flash memory chips -- all critical to the ongoing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI).

Despite stock price gains of more than 340% over the past year (as of this writing), Micron stock is selling for just 13 times earnings, a valuation that is all the more attractive given that the company continues to deliver revenue and profit growth in the triple digits. Moreover, SK Hynix seemed to confirm that the current demand cycle will continue for several more years, and Micron has adopted measures to lock its major customers into multi-year, non-cancelable contracts, thus ensuring the boon continues.

Story Continues

That's why Micron stock is still a buy.

news.Title: Astera Labs Stock Climbs as Investors Look Beyond Nvidia
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Astera Labs ( NASDAQ:ALAB ) shares jumped more than 10% Tuesday , joining a broad rebound across AI infrastructure stocks as investors regained confidence in continued spending on data centers and advanced computing.

The rally came after a difficult stretch for the stock, which had fallen about 21% over the prior month .

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with CRWV.

Is CRWV fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Astera is different from the better-known AI chip names because it focuses on the connectivity layer inside AI systems , helping move data between GPUs, CPUs, memory and networking equipment.

That role is becoming more important as AI clusters grow larger and data movement increasingly becomes a bottleneck.

The broader AI trade also received a boost from Anthropic's IPO filing and a $63 billion financing package tied to Broadcom hardware , which helped ease fears that capital for AI infrastructure was drying up. CoreWeave ( NASDAQ:CRWV ), Nebius ( NASDAQ:NBIS ), Dell and other AI-linked names rallied alongside Astera.

Astera's underlying growth has also been strong.

Second-quarter revenue reached a record $392.4 million , up 104% year over year and 27% sequentially. Management said growth was broad-based across AI fabrics and signal-conditioning products.

The company expects its Scorpio fabric switches to become its largest product family, while it is also expanding into optical interconnects, memory controllers and newer rack-scale architectures.

Earlier this month, Astera introduced Orion , a compute-agnostic rack-scale architecture designed to help customers deploy AI inference systems using multiple GPU and CPU platforms.

Investor Takeaway

I think the bigger story is that the AI rally is starting to spread beyond the obvious GPU winners.

As clusters scale, the ability to move data efficiently between processors and memory becomes increasingly important.

That gives Astera exposure to a second-order bottleneck in the AI buildout.

The opportunity is meaningful, but expectations are already high.

For investors, the key things to watch are Scorpio adoption, customer concentration, optical connectivity growth, gross margins and whether Astera can keep expanding beyond its original retimer business .

The 10% rally reflects renewed enthusiasm around AI spending.

Astera still has to prove that its connectivity platform can capture a growing share of it.

news.Title: Nvidia Faces Fresh Challenge as OpenAI Expands AI Bets
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

OpenAI is reportedly planning to buy artificial intelligence chips from Alphabet's (GOOG) Google, a potentially significant shift as the ChatGPT maker looks to diversify the enormous amount of computing infrastructure needed to train and deploy its models.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with CRWV.

Is GOOGL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Final terms of any potential agreement have not yet been determined, according to multiple media reports.

OpenAI is already one of the world's largest buyers of Nvidia ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) GPUs, which remain central to both AI model training and inference.

A deal with Google would therefore be notable because it could give OpenAI another major source of AI computing capacity while reducing its reliance on a single chip supplier.

For Google, the implications could be equally important.

The company has spent years developing its own AI accelerators to support internal workloads. Selling more of those chips to outside AI developers could turn that investment into a much larger commercial business.

The reported talks also highlight how rapidly the AI infrastructure market is evolving.

Leading AI companies increasingly need massive quantities of specialized processors, power and data-center capacity, making supply diversification strategically important.

That does not necessarily mean Nvidia is being displaced.

OpenAI's compute requirements are large enough that the company could continue purchasing substantial quantities of Nvidia GPUs even while adding Google chips to its infrastructure.

Instead, the move would suggest that AI developers increasingly want access to multiple hardware platforms rather than depending on one architecture.

Investor Takeaway

I think the biggest potential read-through is for Google's AI infrastructure ambitions .

If OpenAI becomes a meaningful buyer of Google-designed chips, Alphabet would not simply be competing with OpenAI at the model level. It would also be supplying infrastructure to one of its biggest AI rivals.

For Nvidia, the development is worth watching but does not automatically imply lost demand.

OpenAI's compute needs continue to expand, and adding another supplier could simply reflect how difficult it is to secure enough capacity.

For investors, the key things to watch are the size of any agreement, which Google chips OpenAI ultimately adopts, deployment timing and whether other major AI developers follow with similar multi-supplier strategies .

The AI chip race may be becoming less about choosing one winner.

It is increasingly about securing as much compute as possible from several of them.

news.Title: Stock market today:  Nasdaq wavers, S&P 500 and Dow climb ahead of Fed decision, Big Tech earnings
news.Content: US stocks diverged on a critical day for markets, with a Fed decision and earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) on deck. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) and S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) edged roughly 0.2% higher, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) held steady at the flatline. Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks drove the rally on Tuesday after Broadcom's CEO negotiated with a consortium of banks to announce a $63 billion financing structure to build AI compute capacity. They continued to gain on Wednesday after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported that profits grew 632% year over year. Micron ( MU ), Samsung ( 005930.KS ), and other chipmaker stocks also rose. Attention now turns toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET, where the Fed is expected to hold rates steady despite elevated inflation readings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference will be closely watched for any signs of a hawkish bias. ( Follow live updates from the meeting .) Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out. Rounding out the earnings picture are Ford ( F ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), eBay ( EBAY ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), and ServiceNow ( NOW ). LIVE 11 updates 42 mins ago David Hollerith Ford Q3 earnings preview: Guidance boost in doubt Ford ( F ) is scheduled to report third quarter results after the bell on Wednesday, Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian reports: Investors will be watching whether the automaker will hold or raise its full-year outlook again. For the quarter, Ford is expected to report automotive revenue of $46.2 billion per Bloomberg consensus, with adjusted EPS of $0.41 on adjusted EBIT (earnings before interest and taxes) of $2.38 billion. Last quarter, Ford raised its full-year adjusted EBIT guidance to $10 billion to $11 billion (prior guidance was $8.5 billion to $10.5 billion). It also lifted its adjusted free cash flow outlook to $6 billion to $7 billion. Analysts see full-year adjusted EBIT of $10.52 billion, in the upper half of that range. Capital expenditures are expected at $9.9 billion, within Ford's unchanged $9.5 billion to $10.5 billion range. Last week, rival GM narrowed its 2026 EBIT-adjusted guidance to $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion while raising its EPS outlook, and shares slid despite an earnings beat, with investors hoping for more. Today at 3:00 PM UTC Ines Ferré This Nvidia chart shows why the AI compute shortage remains acute Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi reports: This week has shown that the appetite to build out AI infrastructure and put it to use isn't slowing down, contrary to market jitters. Rental rates for older-generation Nvidia ( NVDA ) GPUs, known as Blackwell and Hopper, continue to rise, suggesting that the shortage of compute remains acute, BCA Research chief economist Peter Berezin pointed out (see chart below). An acute shortage occurs when demand outstrips supply. "I think we are heading for an AI capex bust but probably not until 2028," Berezin said. Today at 2:15 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Natural gas emerges as key AI bottleneck, Anthropic S-1 filing shows Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley reports: Access to power has emerged as one of the greatest bottlenecks for the AI build-out, with a particular focus on natural gas, which is cheap and abundant in the US. Anthropic's S-1 filing proves natural gas is "an AI vertical," Melius Research managing director James West said. "We know power is a constraint to AI and Anthropic's S-1 filing did nothing to assuage that view," West wrote to clients on Tuesday. "AI compute is a natural gas demand story." Power-intensive data centers are the backbone of the AI build-out. US electricity demand from data centers is expected to double from 2025 to 2027, per research from Goldman Sachs, after 20 years of roughly stagnant energy grid expansion in the US. Today at 1:38 PM UTC David Hollerith US stocks edge into the green at Wednesday's open US stocks were mixed at Wednesday's open as investors looked ahead to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision and earnings from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOGL ). The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) was little changed, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.3%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) climbed 0.4%. Tech stocks entered the session with renewed momentum after back-to-back gains for the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, while investors awaited fresh signals on AI demand from Microsoft and Alphabet after the bell. The Fed is widely expected to leave rates unchanged at 2 p.m. ET, with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference closely watched for signs of how willing policymakers are to raise rates again. Today at 12:44 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Billionaire investor Nelson Peltz makes move to buy struggling Wendy's Nelson Peltz's Trian Partners has reportedly offered $1.4 billion to buy the struggling fast food giant, according to the Wall Street Journal. Wendy's shares rose 15% in premarket trading on the news. After nearly two years of struggles competing with the likes of behemoths McDonald's ( MCD ) and Yum! Brands' ( YUM ) Taco Bell, plus upstarts such as Shake Shack ( SHAK ), Wendy's is on the cusp of a large number of restaurant closures. "With one of its largest franchisees filing bankruptcy in September (although contested by WEN given prior termination of franchise agreement), we think investors likely expect closures to tick higher than expected, but we admit visibility on our side remains somewhat limited and there could still be a range of outcomes," veteran restaurant analyst Andy Barish warned in a recent note. "That said, given our view that there are likely additional franchise operators in the system facing challenges with leveraged balance sheets, higher interest rates and profitability pressures from higher beef, labor & build costs (like many others in QSR), we think it is prudent to moderate our development estimates and bake in more potential closures over the next 6-12 months, as the company works to strengthen its system." Today at 11:58 AM UTC David Hollerith Robinhood warns its AI agents could make unauthorized trades, sparking legal disputes Robinhood ( HOOD ) warned Wednesday that its new artificial intelligence agents could execute unintended trades and expose the online trading platform to new regulatory and legal risks. Robinhood opened its platform to AI agents brought by customers in May, and began rolling out an in-app version last month . The company warned in its third-quarter regulatory filing that the expansion creates "greater reputational risk" as the technology reaches more investors. In an interview last month, Robinhood said customers are responsible for trades executed by their agents. But the company now acknowledges that courts or regulators might not uphold its customer agreements that assign responsibility to its customers. The new warnings were added in the risk factor section of the company's 10-Q filing. Robinhood shares fell nearly 8% in Wednesday premarket trading after it reported weaker-than-expected third quarter profits Tuesday. Today at 11:36 AM UTC Ines Ferré SK Hynix profit jumps 632%, memory chipmaker sees shortage lasting to 2030 US-listed shares of SK Hynix ( SKHY ) rose 8% in premarket trading on Wednesday, after the memory maker's record profit and revenue quelled recent investor worries over the AI trade. South Korean SK Hynix shares ( 000660.KS ) jumped 10% while peer Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) gained 5%. US-based Micron ( MU ) also rose 2%. The South Korea-based company reported a 328% jump in quarterly revenue to roughly $78.7 billion, while operating profit surged 632% to about $62.7 billion, delivering an 80% operating margin. Revenue and operating profit increased by 32% and 38%, respectively, from the previous quarter. Growth was driven by surging AI data center demand, higher memory prices, and early shipments of HBM4, which SK Hynix expects to replace HBM3E as its mainstream product. Today at 11:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Fed expected to hold rates steady this week despite hot inflation — but signal they're not done hiking Yahoo Finance's Jennifer Schonberger previews what to expect and look for in the Federal Reserve's policy announcement and press conference on Wednesday afternoon: The Federal Reserve heads into its interest-rate decision this week facing hotter inflation, keeping the meeting live even as markets widely expect the central bank to hold interest rates steady just days before the midterm elections. Alan Blinder, a former Fed vice chair and a Princeton University economics professor, is expecting a "hawkish pause." Although Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh doesn't favor telegraphing the central bank's next move, Blinder said the moment calls for clarity. "This is a perfect time for clear forward guidance that doesn't quite say, but strongly hints, we're pausing now, but we stand ready to raise again and even give a hint that the next meeting might be the next interest rate hike." Today at 10:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell The stock market's best 6 months of the year start Monday Yahoo Finance's Jared Blikre writes: The stock market's favorite season starts Monday. For decades, November through April has beaten the rest of the year by a mile. That's the Halloween indicator , also called the "best six months" or "sell in May." Buy stocks at the end of October, hold them through April, then step aside for the summer. Yale Hirsch found the pattern in 1986. "You can divide the year into two sections and have practically all the gains in one six-month section and very little in the other," his son Jeffrey Hirsch, editor in chief of the Stock Trader's Almanac, wrote in the 2026 edition. news.Title: Meta, Snap Face Major Trial Over Teen Social Media Addiction
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Meta Platforms Inc. ( META , Financials ), the parent of Facebook and Instagram , is facing a major legal test as a youth social media addiction trial begins in Los Angeles.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 4 Warning Signs with INTC.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Two young plaintiffs allege that features such as autoplay, infinite scroll and streaks encouraged compulsive use and contributed to depression, anxiety and eating disorders.

Meta and Snap are the remaining defendants after TikTok and YouTube reached settlements before trial. One plaintiff also settled with Meta.

The case matters because it is being treated as a bellwether, meaning the outcome could influence how thousands of similar lawsuits are resolved.

More than 3,000 cases are consolidated in Los Angeles Superior Court, while another 3,800 lawsuits from states, school districts and individuals are pending in federal court.

Meta argues that youth mental health is shaped by many factors and says it has added protections for younger users.

A central legal issue is whether Section 230 shields social media companies from claims tied to platform design. The trial judge has ruled that it does not bar these claims.

The next catalyst is testimony from senior executives, including Mark Zuckerberg, as the trial proceeds over the coming weeks.

news.Title: ChatGPT Latest Stock Portfolio: 5 Stock Picks
news.Content:
Remember when everyone said AI could never pick stocks? Some of the early numbers are making that line look old. AI systems have improved fast, and early numbers are making that view harder to defend. FinQ launched two AI-managed ETFs in February, and they are up 25.35% and 23.98%, compared with 11.0% for the S&P 500 over the same period, Reuters reported on Oct. 14. Two Pacer ETFs that rely only on AI are up 10.34% and 10.33% since their early May launch, compared with 5.8% for the S&P 500.

A January paper by researcher Keywan Rasekhschaffe found that AI-written trading signals improved a stock-picking model. In its tests, the best combined setups raised the Sharpe ratio, a measure of return for each unit of risk, by 22% to 49% across three datasets.

ChatGPT's portfolio in the Rallies AI Arena is up 75.6% since March and has beaten the S&P 500, according to Rallies Arena. Rallies Arena said on X on Oct. 14 that it is still way too early to draw conclusions. Check out ChatGPT's top 10 stock picks.

How Rallies Tests ChatGPT

Rallies is an AI investing app that gives several leading AI models money to trade stocks. Models like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok each manage a $100,000 portfolio. Rallies told them to beat the S&P 500. We covered the Claude side of the experiment in our Claude AI Portfolio: 8 Best-Performing Stocks in 2026 .

We ranked the 10 stocks in ChatGPT's portfolio in ascending order based on the number of hedge fund investors at the end of the second quarter of 2026. The data comes from Insider Monkey's database of 1,006 hedge funds. The performance figure for each stock shows its gain or loss since ChatGPT bought it, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 14.

Number of Hedge Fund Investors: 112

ChatGPT bought Amphenol at $65.88, and the stock is up 28.5% since then, according to Rallies data as of Oct. 14. It makes up 9.2% of the portfolio. Amphenol makes electronic and fiber optic connectors. ChatGPT called it a cleaner way to ride AI spending. Baron Durable Advantage Fund says Amphenol benefits from the data center buildout as the leading supplier of high-speed copper interconnects. The hedge fund count held at 112 in both quarters. An analyst also picked Amphenol as a diversified AI stock beyond the chipmakers and cloud giants. See the full breakdown here .

Amphenol (NYSE:APH) makes the connectors and cables that link electronics in data centers, phones, cars, aircraft and defense systems. Customers rarely switch suppliers, because the parts are designed with Amphenol's engineers and need long testing and requalification, so cheaper makers struggle to win the business. Its business units each run like a small company, and that model has absorbed about several acquisitions since 2000. Nvidia picked Amphenol as a partner for its NVLink systems, and demand is widening into medical, factory automation and defense.

Giverny Capital Asset Management looked at why the stock lagged the market even as earnings grew. Read the Giverny letter here .

JPMorgan Chase (NYSE:JPM) is the bank bulls want to own if the economy slows. The case rests on management. Under CEO Jamie Dimon, the bank has posted a return on common equity between 17% and 24% through the years, well above the roughly 13% that is typical over the long run. JPMorgan is also diversified enough across lending, consumer banking and investment banking to handle the usual stress when inflation rises or credit weakens. It has led the other big money center banks over the past 10 years, and bulls expect it to keep outperforming in a downturn and to buy any weakness.

news.Title: Generac Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on C&I Strength, Revenues Miss
news.Content:
Generac Holdings Inc. GNRC reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $2.54, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.38 by 6.7%. Earnings increased 38.8% from $1.83 per share in the prior-year quarter.

Net sales increased 16% year over year to $1.29 billion but missed the consensus estimate of $1.31 billion. Strong Commercial & Industrial (C&I) demand, particularly from data centers, supported growth. The data center backlog increased significantly to nearly $4.5 billion, while Residential revenues rose 9% on higher home standby and portable generator shipments.

GNRC's C&I Segment Maintains Strong Momentum

C&I revenues increased approximately 28% year over year to $553 million from $432.4 million. The segment benefited from acquisitions, divestitures and foreign currency, which contributed approximately 4% to sales growth.

Core growth was primarily driven by accelerating revenues from products sold into the global data center market. However, lower shipments to the domestic industrial distributor and telecom channels offset broad-based regional growth internationally.

Adjusted EBITDA (before deducting for noncontrolling interest) for the segment increased to $69.3 million from $43.8 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12.5% from 10.1%, driven by higher sales volumes and a favorable impact from acquisitions and divestitures.

Generac's Data Center Agreements Boost Growth Visibility

GNRC entered into an agreement with Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN during the quarter, including the execution of a long-term supply agreement for backup power generators for Amazon data centers. Initial deliveries under the agreement are expected to total a combined $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028.

The Amazon agreement adds considerable scale and visibility to a data center business that is fast emerging as Generac's key growth engine.

Generac Holdings Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Generac Holdings Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Generac Holdings Inc. Quote

Management highlighted strong momentum in C&I operations and continues with its capacity expansion plans to capture growing demand. These initiatives are intended to support the company's ability to serve large-scale data center customers.

GNRC's Residential Sales Return to Growth

Residential segment revenues increased approximately 9% to $744.1 million from $685 million in the prior-year quarter. This improvement was supported by higher home standby and portable generator shipments, partly offset by lower shipments of energy storage systems.

Adjusted EBITDA increased to $200.8 million from $160.2 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 27% from 23.4%, supported by favorable pricing and operating leverage from higher shipment volumes. Lower operating expenses associated with energy technology solutions also contributed to profitability.

Story Continues

Generac's Profitability Improves Despite Higher Expenses

Gross profit increased to $516 million from $426.9 million. Gross margin expanded to 39.9% from 38.3%, primarily reflecting favorable price-cost impacts, including lower tariff costs. These benefits were partially offset by an unfavorable sales mix.

Operating expenses increased 10% year over year, or $31.6 million, to $355.5 million. The increase primarily reflected investments supporting C&I growth, higher marketing spending to drive product awareness, additional incentive compensation and intangible amortization expenses.

Operating income increased to $160.6 million from $103.1 million. Adjusted EBITDA before deducting noncontrolling interests reached $256 million, representing 19.8% of net sales, compared with $193 million, or 17.3%, a year earlier.

GNRC's Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Strengthen

Net cash provided by operating activities increased to $171 million from $118 million in the year-ago quarter. Free cash flow improved to approximately $132 million from $96 million, primarily driven by higher operating earnings, partially offset by higher capital expenditures.

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash and cash equivalents totaled $393.7 million, compared with $341.4 million as of Dec. 31, 2025.

Long-term borrowings and finance lease obligations stood at $1.24 billion, compared with $1.26 billion at the end of 2025.

Generac Reaffirms 2026 Sales Outlook

Generac maintained its full-year 2026 net sales growth guidance in the mid-to-high teens percentage range compared with the prior year. The outlook includes approximately 2% net favorable contribution from foreign currency, acquisitions and divestitures.

The company reiterated its net income margin guidance of 9-10%, before deducting noncontrolling interests. Generac raised the lower end of its 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance to 20.5-21% from the previous range of 20-21%.

GNRC's Zacks Rank

Generac currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Recent Performances of Other Companies in the Same Space

Dover Corporation DOV reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of $2.88 per share, rising 10% year over year and beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.83 by 1.77%. The improvement reflected broad-based demand for Dover, higher revenues and operational execution.

Revenues increased 7.5% year over year to $2.23 billion, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.20 billion by 1.47%. Organic revenues grew 7.1%. Dover's bookings totaled $2.31 billion compared with $2 billion in the year-ago quarter. Orders increased across all five segments, resulting in a book-to-bill ratio of 1.03.

Illinois Tool Works Inc. ITW reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $3 per share, which surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.99. Earnings increased 6.8% year over year.

Illinois Tool's revenues of $4.24 billion missed the consensus estimate of $4.26 billion. The top line increased 4.4% year over year, driven by organic sales growth of 3.8%. Favorable foreign currency translation and acquisitions each had a positive impact of 0.3% in the quarter.

Illinois Tool raised its full-year 2026 financial guidance. ITW now expects earnings to be in the range of $11.45-$11.55 per share compared with $11.35-$11.55 expected earlier. Revenues are expected to increase 4.5-5.5% while organic revenues are anticipated to rise 3-4%.

news.Title: Amazon Cracks Down on 'Tokenmaxxing' AI Use
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN , Financials ), the e-commerce and cloud computing company , is telling software engineers to avoid tokenmaxxing as artificial intelligence tools become more deeply embedded in development work.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMZN.

Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

According to an internal Amazon memo, metrics such as token usage, rates of AI tool use, and code updates are considered to be "deeply flawed" ways to assess engineering teams.The company claims that such actions might increase complexity, wasted expense, and unnecessary use, without improving output. Amazon has not imposed token constraints on any of its employees.The company has previously eliminated an internal scoreboard after learning that certain workers were abusing token use to raise their standings.Businesses using generative AI are facing a bigger problem, and the standards reflect that: how to measure production without rewarding labor per se.Amazon maintains that, regardless of shifts in industry norms, AI will remain an integral part of software engineering.Investors are worried that unregulated usage of artificial intelligence (AI) technology might increase processing costs, despite their intended productivity improvement.The next step in measuring AI efficiency is to observe whether the engineering team at Amazon develops any new measures based on outcomes.

news.Title: Top 5 AI Stocks in Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont’s Portfolios
news.Content:
Billionaires Ray Dalio and Philippe Laffont are two of the brightest minds in investing, and both have strong views on AI. Laffont runs Coatue Management and has built his hedge fund around the technology. Dalio founded Bridgewater Associates in 1975 and warns that AI has become a crowded trade. Let's start with Laffont.

Laffont: AI Is a Supercycle, and the Next $10 Trillion Company Could Come From It

Laffont sees a supercycle in AI, and Coatue's four biggest US long positions as of March 31 were all AI-related, Bloomberg reported. Coatue's flagship hedge fund lost 8.3% in July, its worst month in more than a year, but was still up 14.3% for the year (at the time of the Bloomberg report), after a gain in May that was its best month in 25 years, Bloomberg said in August. Check his top stock picks here.

Laffont expects a $10 trillion company within 10 to 15 years, he told CNBC in June. He thinks the winner could be a new AI name. There is "a good chance that OpenAI and Anthropic could be there," he said, and SpaceX could join them.

Agentic AI excites him most. Laffont described going to bed while a thousand AI agents do the work, and he says the productivity gains already show up in his own office. He does not expect AI models to become free, because people will pay for the best ones.

Dalio: AI Is a Great Tool and a Crowded Trade

Dalio built Bridgewater out of a two-bedroom apartment, and its flagship Pure Alpha fund rose 33% in 2025, Reuters reported. Click to read more about Dalio's portfolio.

A US debt crisis could hit within three years, he told Bloomberg Television in October. The government spends about 40% more than it takes in, he says, and debt payments squeeze out other spending. Stocks look expensive by most of his measures, and the extra return they offer over bonds has shrunk. AI adds to the risk, because a small group of AI stocks drives the market, and the big AI spenders now rely more on debt to fund their buildout. His one warning to investors is to avoid being "too concentrated in one particular asset," such as AI.

Dalio still likes AI as a tool. Using it to systematize investment decisions is the future, he says, and he expects gains to broaden from the AI builders to the companies that use the technology.

Both billionaires own AI stocks. Here are the 5 biggest AI holdings the two funds have in common. You can see the full list of 10 stocks here .

Methodology

We looked at the top 50 holdings in the second quarter 2026 13F filings of Ray Dalio's Bridgewater Associates and Philippe Laffont's Coatue Management. From the AI stocks that appear in both lists, we picked the 10 with the highest combined dollar value across the two stakes and ranked them in ascending order. Stake sizes and share changes come from the funds' 13F filings for the quarter ended June 30.

Story Continues

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 599.2% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 372 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can also watch our video about the top 10 AI picks of these two famous billionaires on YouTube by clicking the image below:

#5 GE Vernova Inc. (NYSE:GEV)

Coatue Stake $3.01 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $144.2 Million

GE Vernova makes the gas turbines and grid equipment that data centers need for power. Coatue trimmed 14,194 shares in the second quarter and held $3.01 billion, or 6.18% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 312,129 shares and held $144.2 million, or 0.59% of its portfolio. Bulls say the company's order backlog for AI data center power outweighs a recent earnings miss. See the full breakdown here.

GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV) is positioned to benefit from surging electricity demand driven by AI data centers. US data center electricity consumption is projected to increase 130% by 2030, creating opportunities across power generation and grid infrastructure. GE Vernova's gas turbine backlog and slot reservations reached 116 gigawatts, while data center orders exceeded $5 billion in the first half of 2026, more than double the total for 2025.

Second-quarter orders surged 88% year over year, lifting the company's total backlog to $176 billion. Its businesses span gas turbines, transformers, substations and electrical equipment, allowing it to benefit from multiple stages of data center development. Growing equipment installations could also generate long-term maintenance and service revenue.

However, not all is good. GE Vernova's valuation already reflects substantial growth expectations. The stock trades at 53.74 times forward non-GAAP earnings, compared with the sector median of 19.32 times. Its forward enterprise value-to-sales ratio of 4.52 is more than double the sector median. These premiums leave limited room for disappointment if AI-related electricity demand grows more slowly than anticipated. Supply chain constraints could also delay the conversion of GE Vernova's substantial backlog into revenue.

#4 Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT)

Coatue Stake $3.05 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $210.7 Million

Applied Materials sells the equipment and services that chipmakers use to manufacture semiconductors. Coatue trimmed 1,034,719 shares and held $3.05 billion, or 6.26% of its portfolio. Bridgewater trimmed 268,492 shares and held $210.7 million, or 0.86% of its portfolio. Jim Cramer thinks there is more to the stock than its earnings multiple shows. Check what he said here.

Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) makes the machines chipmakers use to build semiconductors. Without them, Nvidia, Micron and others could not produce the chips AI needs. Chip shortages are expected to last for years, with memory shortages forecast to run through 2030, so chipmakers must keep adding capacity. Cloud giants keep raising their AI spending, and asset managers are building new funds focused on data centers. In the latest quarter, margins and earnings grew faster than sales. The stock has fallen about 48% from its high, and its forward P/E has dropped from about 55 to 29.5, which gives long-term buyers a cheaper entry.

The bull case rests on AI demand lasting for years, and nobody can guarantee that. Some investors expect the boom to end quickly, and chip equipment orders can swing sharply when chipmakers pause spending. The stock is also very volatile, which makes it a poor fit for conservative investors. A valuation recovery, with the forward P/E climbing back toward 40, is not certain, and a lower multiple would cut any gains. A 48% drop can also mean the market sees a problem that the numbers do not yet show at Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT).

#3 Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Coatue Stake $2.82 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $482.8 Million

Coatue raised its Amazon stake by 50% in the second quarter, buying 3,904,033 shares, and held $2.82 billion, or 5.80% of its portfolio. Bridgewater cut 2,363,230 shares, which took the position from 4.08% to 1.98% of its portfolio. The stake is still worth $482.8 million. Amazon also ranks second on our list of President Trump and Nancy Pelosi's top picks. Read why here.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) owns huge data centers full of computers and rents them out over the internet through AWS, its cloud business. AI companies need an enormous amount of computing power, so they rent it from Amazon and pay every month, like tenants paying a landlord. AWS growth has sped up for five straight quarters, reaching 37% last quarter, and Amazon says its capacity is sold out through 2027. Customers have signed contracts for years of future use, and that backlog doubled in the first half of the year. Anthropic and OpenAI are two of the biggest tenants, and Amazon owns stakes in both, so it gets paid as their landlord and as an owner. Advertising adds another strong profit stream, up 26% last quarter.

Amazon is spending so much on new data centers that free cash flow has turned negative and its debt has grown. If AI demand slows, those buildings will be expensive to keep. Much of the backlog comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, two companies that spend far more than they earn. A possible Anthropic IPO, which would put a public price on Amazon's stake, could also price below its last funding round. AI shopping agents could skip the sponsored products that drive most of Amazon's ad revenue, and the FTC's antitrust trial starts in March 2027 for Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).

#2 Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)

Coatue Stake $3.63 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $134.7 Million

Micron makes the memory chips that go into data centers and AI servers. Coatue raised its stake by 1,794%, buying 2,976,338 shares, and the position grew from 0.19% to 7.46% of its portfolio. It was worth $3.63 billion at the end of the quarter. Bridgewater went the other way and trimmed 1,359,038 shares, which cut the weight from 2.23% to 0.55% of its portfolio. It held $134.7 million. A Chinese memory maker could match Micron's DRAM wafer capacity by 2029, and that is the core of the bear case. Read the full bear case here.

Micron (NASDAQ:MU) is trading at about 5 times forward earnings, against a sector median of 21.6. Its forward PEG ratio is 0.07, against 1.13 for the sector, and on trailing earnings it trades at 11.6 times, well below its five-year average of 18.3. Revenue grew 256% from a year ago, and earnings have surged with it.

But before you get too excited about the valuation, listen to the bear argument. Bears say a low P/E on record profits is a warning sign for a cyclical stock. They point to Micron's own history, where strong earnings and a low P/E came before a big drop at least three times in the past decade. Fabs cost billions and take two to three years to build, so new supply from SK hynix and Chinese makers will arrive later, as it did after the PC era, the dot-com bubble, the 2017 cloud surge and the pandemic boom. Even bears say the shortage may last into 2028, but they expect the stock to peak before it ends, and Micron is already well below its June high. AI spending cannot grow forever, and the big spenders already have negative cash flow, which is a risk for Micron (NASDAQ:MU).

#1 Lam Research Corporation (NASDAQ:LRCX)

Coatue Stake $4.09 Billion | Bridgewater Stake $406.6 Million

Lam Research makes the machines that chipmakers use to build chips. It is Coatue's second-largest position, at $4.09 billion or 8.41% of its portfolio, after Coatue trimmed 601,902 shares. Bridgewater trimmed 633,005 shares and held $406.6 million, or 1.67% of its portfolio. The stock was up about 73% for the year when we last covered it. Read our take on whether it is still a smart long-term AI pick here.

Lam Research (NASDAQ:LRCX) makes the etching and deposition machines chipmakers use to build wafers. Advanced AI chips need more of those steps and take longer to make, so manufacturers need more equipment even if unit volumes stay the same. Bulls also see Lam as a shelter if the AI market cools. If AI chip prices fall as costs normalize while volumes rise, chipmakers still have to buy the machines to make them. Sales grew 54% last quarter, operating margins reached a record high, and the stock has fallen 29% since June, which gives new buyers a cheaper entry.

Guidance for the next quarter points to just 4.6% growth from the last one, after 22% in the September quarter, because unusually strong China orders are returning to normal. The stock fell about 12% on the report. China's strength may only be a timing issue as chipmakers absorb equipment they already bought, and ASML and Applied Materials both say demand there remains strong. Even so, equipment orders come in lumps, and a real pullback in AI spending would hit Lam directly.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of LRCX as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than LRCX that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .Click to continue reading and see the expanded list of 10 Stocks Billionaires Laffont and Dalio are Piling Into

news.Title: Garmin Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Rise Y/Y
news.Content:
Garmin Ltd. GRMN reported pro forma earnings of $2.76 per share for the third quarter of 2026, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.38 by 15.97%. The bottom line increased 39% year over year from $1.99 reported in the year-ago quarter.

Net sales rose 12% to $1.99 billion and came in line with the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Fitness and Outdoor together accounted for 65% of sales, supported by demand for wearables and adventure watches. Gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%.

GRMN's Fitness Revenues Rise on Wearable Demand

Fitness revenues advanced 16% year over year to $694.3 million. The segment benefited from continued demand for wearables, with operating income increasing 19% to $230.6 million. Gross and operating margins were 63% and 33%, respectively.

During the quarter, Garmin launched the CIRQA Smart Band, a screenless wearable offering health and fitness insights. The company also recently introduced new Edge cycling computers, including the Edge 1060 with hands-free voice controls and the Edge Explore 3 series.

Garmin Ltd. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Garmin Ltd. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Garmin Ltd. Quote

Garmin's Outdoor Sales Surge on Adventure Watches

Outdoor revenues jumped 20% to $597.3 million, primarily driven by demand for adventure watches. Operating income climbed 37% to $233 million, while gross and operating margins reached 68% and 39%, respectively.

The company launched the f??nix 9 and f??nix 9 Pro adventure watch series during the quarter. It also introduced Garmin Drive GPS navigators featuring high-resolution ultrawide displays. The launches expanded Garmin's flagship adventure watch and navigation offerings.

GRMN Sees Growth Across Aviation and Marine

Aviation revenues increased 5% to $252.7 million, led by original equipment manufacturer product categories. Operating income rose 8% to $65.8 million. The segment recorded gross and operating margins of 78% and 26%, respectively.

Garmin unveiled the G2000 PRIME flight deck for high-performance piston and electric aircraft and announced certification of an all-glass retrofit cockpit for the original Cessna CitationJet.

Marine revenues grew 16% to $309.9 million, driven by broad-based demand led by sonar products. Marine operating income surged 90% to $94 million, while gross and operating margins were 64% and 30%, respectively. The company launched LiveScope 2 and received six Product of Excellence awards from the National Marine Electronics Association.

Garmin's Auto OEM Revenues Contract

Story Continues

Auto OEM revenues declined 20% year over year to $131.9 million, primarily due to domain controllers. The segment recorded a gross margin of 16% and an operating loss of $11.9 million compared with a loss of $16.7 million a year earlier.

Lower operating expenses helped narrow the operating loss despite the decline in sales. Garmin continues to work toward the launch of its Mercedes-Benz domain controller program.

Garmin's Operating Profitability Improves

Gross profit increased 20% year over year to $1.26 billion, while gross margin expanded 420 basis points to 63.3%. Operating income rose 34% to $611.6 million, with operating margin expanding 500 basis points to 30.8%. Favorable segment mix, lower product costs and approximately $33 million in refunds of previously paid tariffs supported profitability. GAAP earnings jumped 35% to $2.80 per share.

Operating expenses increased 10% to $646.1 million. Research and development expenses rose 9% to $312.9 million, mainly due to personnel costs. Selling, general and administrative expenses climbed 10% to $333.2 million, reflecting higher personnel-related and advertising expenses.

Garmin Returns Cash to Shareholders

Garmin generated $393.9 million in operating cash flow and $293.3 million in free cash flow during the quarter compared with $485.6 million and $425.1 million, respectively, a year earlier. Capital expenditures totaled $100.6 million. In the first three quarters of 2026, it generated operating and free cash flows of $1.33 billion and $1.04 billion, respectively. It incurred capital expenditure of $295 million during the first nine months of 2026.

The company paid $202 million in dividends and repurchased $41 million of shares. In the first three quarters of 2026, Garmin paid $578.5 million in dividends and bought shares worth $123.2 million. Approximately $407 million remained under its share repurchase authorization at the end of the third quarter. It ended the quarter with approximately $4.1 billion in cash and marketable securities and $2.25 billion in inventory.

Garmin Raises 2026 Outlook

Garmin now expects 2026 revenues of approximately $8.15 billion, up from its prior projection of $8.05 billion. Pro forma earnings are forecast at $10.80 per share compared with the previous outlook of $10.

The company raised its gross margin forecast to 61% from 59.7% and its operating margin estimate to 29% from 27%. The projected pro forma tax rate remains unchanged at 16.5%.

Management raised its 2026 guidance following record operating results and continued momentum heading into the holiday selling season.

GRMN's Zacks Rank and Stocks to Consider

news.Title: TXN's Gross Margin Crosses 64% in Q3: Can It Improve Further?
news.Content:
Texas Instruments Incorporated TXN delivered a strong improvement in profitability in the third quarter of 2026, raising hopes that its gross margin can climb further. The semiconductor maker reported a gross margin of 64.2%, up from 57.4% in the year-ago quarter and 61.4% in the previous quarter.

Texas Instruments' third-quarter gross profit rose 43% year over year to $3.89 billion, outpacing the 28% increase in revenues to $6.06 billion. Higher sales volumes supported the improvement, while better factory utilization, pricing and product mix also helped. These trends suggest that stronger demand can translate into better profitability when production facilities operate more efficiently.

Growth across key markets offers additional support. Industrial revenues increased more than 40% year over year, while automotive revenues grew at a mid-teens rate. Data center revenues surged about 95%, reflecting rising demand for chips used in expanding computing infrastructure. Continued strength in these markets could help TXN maintain higher production levels and spread manufacturing costs across more units.

Texas Instruments' 300-millimeter wafer manufacturing strategy could also support cost efficiency as output rises. Per the company, an unpackaged chip built on 300-millimeter wafers costs approximately 40% less than one built on 200-millimeter wafers. Texas Instruments has available cleanroom capacity in its Richardson, Sherman and Lehi facilities. Management plans to install additional equipment according to demand, supporting dependable supply and cost efficiency as production volumes increase.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues and earnings indicates year-over-year growth of 37.7% and 94.5%, respectively. These projections imply continued business activity, which could further expand Texas Instruments' margins.

How Do TXN's Competitors Compare on Gross Margin?

Analog Devices, Inc. ADI is a close competitor in analog chips and signal-processing technology. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, ADI's revenues rose 40% year over year to $4.02 billion, while its GAAP gross margin increased to 67.3% from 62.1% in the year-ago quarter.

Its adjusted gross margin reached 72.5% from 69.2% in the year-ago quarter, highlighting strong profitability. These results put Analog Devices ahead of TXN's 64.2% gross margin.

Microchip Technology Incorporated MCHP is another competitor, supplying microcontrollers and embedded-control chips. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenues grew 38% year over year to $1.49 billion.

Story Continues

Microchip Technology's GAAP gross margin improved to 63.2% from 53.6% in the year-ago quarter, while its non-GAAP gross margin reached 63.8% from 54.3%. Higher factory utilization and recovering demand supported the improvement.

Both companies show how stronger demand and manufacturing efficiency can lift margins. Analog Devices' higher reported margin sets a competitive benchmark, while Microchip Technology's performance highlights the benefits of better factory utilization.

Shares of Texas Instruments have surged 78.1% year to date compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry's 22.6% growth.

news.Title: SK Hynix Says Memory Is Sold Out Through 2029. Micron Is a Winner, Too
news.Content:
SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY), the South Korean memory chipmaker, reported its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 28, and the results didn't disappoint. But while the company is marking a record-setting quarter and a big jump in stock price today, I think Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) shareholders have plenty of reasons to be excited as well.

SK Hynix reported that its production of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) is effectively sold out through 2029, with memory shortages expected to last through 2030. The company said long-term supply agreements, combined with customer contracts still under discussion, account for its expected production over the next three years.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

"We expect it to be difficult to fully meet customers' volume requirements in the near term," Chief Financial Officer Woo-hyun Kim said on the company's earnings call. "Given the complexities involved in implementing leading-edge processes and the lead times required to construct new production facilities, a situation where supply cannot keep up with demand is expected to persist for some time, a constraint projected to continue through 2030."

That's outstanding news for SK Hynix. But it could be equally important for Micron , which competes with SK Hynix and Samsung in the global memory market.

Image source: Getty Images.

Micron has been warning about a memory shortage

Micron Executive Vice President and Chief Business Officer Sumit Sadana told investors at KeyBanc's Technology Leadership Forum in August that calendar 2027 would be "even tighter" than 2026.

Sadana also said Micron had no clear indication of when memory supply would finally catch up with demand. Now SK Hynix is telling investors essentially the same thing: The memory shortage issue won't disappear anytime soon.

And that could give Micron considerable pricing power.

Why HBM demand helps Micron's entire DRAM business

HBM is a specialized form of DRAM that stacks memory chips vertically to deliver the enormous bandwidth required by AI accelerators. Micron manufactures both HBM and conventional DRAM, and there's an interesting relationship between the two products.

Producing HBM requires considerably more manufacturing capacity than producing the same amount of conventional DRAM.

Story Continues

Sadana explained that manufacturing 100 bits of HBM3E consumes as much production capacity as manufacturing approximately 300 bits of standard DRAM. He said that the ratio increases to nearly 4-to-1 with the newer HBM4E technology.

As Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung pour resources into high-margin HBM products, they're reducing the capacity available for conventional DRAM -- a product essential for computers, smartphones, and data center servers. So, even if Micron doesn't lead the HBM market, it can still benefit from the industry's shift toward manufacturing more HBM.

A less available supply, combined with strong demand, creates opportunities for higher selling prices. And because memory manufacturing has substantial fixed costs, higher prices can deliver an outsize improvement in profit margins.

What does this mean for Micron investors?

SK Hynix's earnings illustrated the demand for memory -- as well as the profits that can be realized. Revenue was 104.62 trillion won ($77.99 billion), up 328% from a year ago. Operating profit was 83.33 trillion won ($62.12 billion), up 632% from last year. The company posted a net profit of 39.78 trillion won ($29.65 billion). SK Hynix stock was up 10% Wednesday morning, while Micron stock rose nearly 5%.

Memory chips have historically been a cyclical business. Strong demand leads to higher prices; manufacturers expand production; and, eventually, excess supply sends prices and profits tumbling.

That risk hasn't disappeared.

Micron is investing in additional manufacturing capacity, including new facilities in Idaho, and its competitors are expanding production as well. If demand slows or new capacity arrives faster than expected, today's favorable pricing conditions could weaken.

SK Hynix's announcement provides another reason to believe Micron's earnings growth could continue beyond the current year. And with the stock up more than 200% in 2026, that's great news for Micron stock investors.

news.Title: Will Sandisk Corporation (SNDK) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?
news.Content:
Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Sandisk Corporation (SNDK), which belongs to the Zacks Computer- Storage Devices industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

This company has an established record of topping earnings estimates, especially when looking at the previous two reports. The company boasts an average surprise for the past two quarters of 38.04%.

For the most recent quarter, Sandisk Corporation was expected to post earnings of $34.24 per share, but it reported $39.25 per share instead, representing a surprise of 14.63%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $14.5 per share, while it actually produced $23.41 per share, a surprise of 61.45%.

Price and EPS Surprise

Thanks in part to this history, there has been a favorable change in earnings estimates for Sandisk Corporation lately. In fact, the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) for the stock is positive, which is a great indicator of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Sandisk Corporation has an Earnings ESP of +4.34% at the moment, suggesting that analysts have grown bullish on its near-term earnings potential. When you combine this positive Earnings ESP with the stock's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), it shows that another beat is possibly around the corner. The company's next earnings report is expected to be released on October 29, 2026.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

news.Title: Lam Research Sees Record Foundry Sales: Can the Momentum Continue?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation LRCX is benefiting from rising demand for advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, its foundry business achieved record revenues, while the foundry's share of Systems revenues increased to 46% from 44% in the previous quarter. Demand came from leading-edge chipmaking and advanced packaging as well as mature-node capacity spending in China. The company's total Systems revenues soared 34.9% sequentially to $5.73 billion.

Advanced logic chips are becoming more complex as artificial intelligence (AI) workloads require greater computing power. This trend increases demand for advanced patterning, deposition and etch equipment, where Lam Research has established capabilities. Advanced packaging also creates opportunities as chipmakers seek better performance and power efficiency. LRCX's investments in these technologies could help it win more equipment orders and expand its market opportunity.

The broader outlook is encouraging. Lam Research expects wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to exceed $200 billion in calendar year 2027, up from the mid-$150 billion range expected for 2026. Management also identified leading-edge foundry and logic, alongside DRAM, as major sources of future growth. However, cleanroom shortages and supply constraints affecting certain components could limit the industry's ability to meet demand.

Rising AI-related demand and greater chipmaking complexity provide longer-term support for Lam Research's prospects. Rising mature-node capacity spending in China could further boost foundry revenues.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Lam Research's fiscal 2027 and 2028 revenues is currently pegged at $34.66 billion and $41.38 billion, respectively. The consensus mark for fiscal 2027 and 2028 top lines indicates year-over-year growth of 49.2% and 19.4%, respectively.

How Applied Materials and KLA Compete With Lam Research

Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT competes with Lam Research in semiconductor manufacturing equipment used to make advanced chips. Its tools support materials engineering, leading-edge foundry production and advanced packaging.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Applied Materials reported record revenues of $9.12 billion, up 25% year over year. Non-GAAP earnings per share climbed 41% year over year to $3.50. Its growth outlook highlights strong demand for advanced foundry and logic equipment, making it a serious competitor as chipmakers expand capacity.

KLA Corporation KLAC offers a different but relevant competitive challenge through inspection and process-control equipment that helps chipmakers detect defects and improve production yields.

Story Continues

In the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, KLA's revenues increased 15.2% year over year to $3.66 billion. Results benefited from AI infrastructure investment, leading-edge foundry/logic demand and rising process control intensity. Advanced packaging process control revenues are now expected to reach about $1.1 billion in calendar year 2026. The company's non-GAAP earnings increased 11.7% year over year to $1.05 per share.

Applied Materials competes more directly in equipment manufacturing, while KLA benefits from the growing need for chip quality control. Their growth underscores the opportunity and competitive pressure for Lam Research as foundry spending rises.

news.Title: HPE Benefits From AI Infrastructure Demand: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE is benefiting from demand for artificial intelligence (AI) workloads across Agentic AI, Enterprise AI, Private Cloud AI, AI fabs and hyperscalers, leading to multiyear revenue growth and record backlogs.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, HPE's Cloud & AI revenues reached $9 billion, up 25% year over year, with a 17% operating margin. Server revenues rose 35%, while traditional server orders increased 75% as customers favored AI-ready configurations and higher-value systems. HPE's fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 Cloud & AI revenues are expected to grow 60% to 72%.

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, AI systems orders were $2.4 billion, up more than 30% sequentially, while AI systems backlog rose 14% sequentially to $6.8 billion. Private Cloud AI orders increased triple digits year over year, showing wider adoption of HPE's on-premises AI factory approach.

HPE was also awarded a $3.5 billion inferencing deal with a hyperscaler customer, adding evidence that enterprise AI deployments are moving beyond pilots. Supporting its AI infrastructure, Hewlett Packard Enterprise is expanding its hybrid cloud operating model through GreenLake, which lets customers manage infrastructure and software across on-premises and cloud environments with consumption-based economics.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise has used acquisitions to add networking, cloud management, security and data-management capabilities around its hybrid IT model. These factors will support HPE's capabilities and long-term growth outlook.

How Competitors Fare Against HPE

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's closest competitors in this domain are Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO. Dell AI Factory combined with NVIDIA is arguably the most direct alternative for HPE private cloud AI.

Dell provides pre-integrated GPU servers, storage, networking and software for enterprise AI and competes head-to-head with HPE for Fortune 1000 AI deployments. Cisco focuses on AI networking and integrated AI Pods. Cisco has started competing strongly with HPE after acquiring Splunk and through its partnership with NVIDIA.

news.Title: Amazon Just Issues a Stark Warning to Employees About AI Productivity
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) has told its software engineers to avoid tokenmaxxing, or inflating the use of AI tools to look productive, according to a Tuesday company posting of an internal memo.

The document , first shared with staff in September, updates how Amazon defines the jobs of software development engineers and their managers. It says AI is only beginning to reshape the field and expects it to sit at the center of engineering work going forward.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMZN.

Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Tokens are the units of text that AI models process, and heavy token use can raise costs. Amazon said measures such as token counts, how widely AI tools are adopted, and the number of code changes or reviews are poor yardsticks for judging team performance. The company said those figures can add expense and complexity.

An Amazon spokesperson told CNBC the company has not set limits on how many tokens employees may use. Amazon shut down an internal leaderboard in May after finding that some workers were gaming it to rank higher.

news.Title: NXPI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Auto and Industrial Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors N.V. NXPI reported better-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, driven by higher automotive semiconductor content, industrial demand and data center infrastructure growth.

NXPI reported non-GAAP earnings of $4.20 per share, which increased 35% year over year and beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.45%.

Revenues increased 19.3% year over year to $3.79 billion, exceeding the consensus estimate by 0.41%. Automotive sales crossed $2 billion for the first time, while Industrial & IoT revenues surged 39% as customers expanded automation and intelligent-edge deployments.

NXPI's Automotive Business Benefits From Content Gains

Automotive revenues were $2.07 billion, up 13% year over year and 7% sequentially. Excluding the divested MEMS sensor business, automotive sales grew 17% year over year. Management attributed the strength to software-defined vehicles, electrification, connectivity and radar rather than an increase in vehicle production.

Software-defined vehicle revenues are running above $1.5 billion on an annualized basis, keeping NXPI on track for its $2 billion target in 2027. The company plans to begin shipping its S32K5 zonal processor and S32N central compute platforms next year. Volkswagen and Rivian's joint venture selected S32K5 for its zonal platform, supporting NXPI's position in the emerging vehicle architecture market.

NXP Semiconductors N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NXP Semiconductors N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NXP Semiconductors N.V. Quote

NXPI's Industrial and Infrastructure Sales Accelerate

Industrial & IoT revenues climbed 39% year over year and 6% sequentially to $802 million. The industrial portion grew nearly 50%, supported by data centers, factory automation and health care, and now accounts for about 70% of the end market's revenues.

Communication Infrastructure & Other generated $503 million, up 54% year over year and 11% sequentially, benefiting from data center and secure-card demand. Mobile revenues, however, declined 4% year over year to $411 million, despite a 17% sequential increase, reflecting a more uneven demand profile across NXPI's portfolio.

NXPI's Margins Improve With Higher Factory Utilization

Non-GAAP gross profit rose 22% year over year to $2.22 billion, while gross margin increased 160 basis points to 58.6%. Management cited higher factory utilization and improved revenue flow-through, alongside favorable product mix and operating efficiencies.

Non-GAAP operating income climbed 31% to $1.41 billion. Operating margin expanded 330 basis points to 37.1%, while non-GAAP operating expenses were $810 million, or 21.4% of revenues. Management expects manufacturing utilization to rise further in 2027 and gross margin to reach 60% during that year.

Story Continues

NXPI's Cash Generation Supports Larger Buybacks

Operating cash flow reached $1.26 billion in the quarter. After $50 million of net capital spending, non-GAAP free cash flow totaled $1.21 billion, representing 31.9% of revenues. NXPI returned $359 million through dividends and share repurchases.

The company finished the quarter with $3.94 billion in cash and $10.98 billion in debt, leaving net financial leverage at 1.3 times. Inventory days fell to 148 from 156 in the preceding quarter. Following quarter-end, the board authorized an additional $5 billion in share repurchases, bringing total authorization to about $6.3 billion.

NXPI Guides Fourth-Quarter Growth and Higher Earnings

For the fourth quarter of 2026, NXPI forecasts revenues between $3.75 billion and $3.95 billion. The $3.85 billion midpoint implies 15% year-over-year and 2% sequential growth. The company expects automotive and industrial sales to increase sequentially, while mobile demand remains weaker year over year.

Non-GAAP gross margin is projected at 59% at the midpoint, with an operating margin of 37.5%. Non-GAAP earnings per share are expected between $4.14 and $4.58, with a midpoint of $4.36. Looking to 2027, management anticipates double-digit revenue growth, supported by software-defined vehicles, industrial AI and data center infrastructure.

news.Title: The S&P 500 Is Approaching a Valuation Not Seen Since the Peak of the Dot-Com Bubble, and History Suggests a Crash Could Follow
news.Content:
The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) index has more than doubled from its 2022 bear market low point, driven by blistering returns from the technology sector which is home to many of the companies leading the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution.

The index's Shiller cyclically adjusted price-to-earnings (CAPE) ratio recently hit 41, a stone's throw away from its all-time high of 44.2 from the peak of the dot-com internet bubble in the year 2000. The CAPE ratio is calculated using the average earnings of the companies in the index over a 10-year period, adjusted for inflation, so it's a highly useful valuation metric.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The S&P 500 plummeted by 49% when the dot-com bubble eventually burst, and although I'm not predicting a similar decline this time around, the mounting risks to the current bull market are getting harder to ignore. Here's what I think investors should do.

Rising interest rates and an AI slowdown could crash the S&P 500

There is never a perfect time to invest. War, changes in interest rates, elections, and even new technologies can create uncertainty, and at least one of them is a factor basically all the time. However, several of them are actively fueling volatility in the stock market right now, making this environment especially difficult for investors to navigate.

The U.S. and Iran have been locked in a geopolitical conflict since late February, resulting in the closure of the Strait of Hormuz waterway, through which 25% of the world's seaborne oil travels each day. To make matters worse, the ongoing war between Saudi Arabia and Yemen recently took a turn for the worse, while Ukraine and Russia are actively targeting one another's energy infrastructure in their ongoing conflict.

These tensions are wreaking havoc in the energy markets by disrupting the supply of oil and refined products like diesel. In fact, West Texas Intermediate crude oil was trading for over $103 per barrel last Friday, a whopping 80% increase from its 2026 opening price of $57. Since oil is a massive input cost for practically every product that travels by truck, boat, or plane, American consumers are seeing price hikes almost everywhere, from the grocery store to their favorite retailers.

As a result, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation rose at an annualized rate of 3.7% in September, significantly above the Federal Reserve's 2% target, with the energy component soaring by 20.4%. This prompted the Fed to raise interest rates by 25 basis points last month, and more hikes will almost certainly follow if inflationary pressures persist.

Story Continues

Rising interest rates are often bad for stocks because they force consumers and businesses to tighten their belts, thus putting the brakes on the economy. Weaker corporate earnings can be a direct consequence of any slowdown in economic activity, and earnings drive stock prices over the long term. That's one of the reasons why the S&P 500 suffered a bear-market decline of over 20% during the Fed's last rate hiking cycle, which spanned from March 2022 to August 2023.

^SPX data by YCharts

Rising interest rates are also threatening the AI infrastructure boom, as neocloud companies like CoreWeave face soaring borrowing costs. Equity investors are now heading for the exits, sending CoreWeave stock plummeting by over 70% from its peak. But it's one of many casualties; earlier this month, Australian data center company, Firmus, had to cancel its blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) due to a lack of demand from investors, which sent a shockwave through the industry.

Recent reports suggest AI giants like Anthropic and OpenAI are also having their valuations slashed by investors. Anthropic, specifically, could face a whopping $500 billion haircut from its $2 trillion expected valuation at its upcoming IPO. These jitters are spreading to the public markets, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF already down 27% from its peak. It holds many of the chip stocks at the heart of the AI data center boom, including Nvidia and Micron Technology .

Here's what investors should do if the stock market plunges

The S&P 500 was only down 2.5% from its peak as of the market close last Friday, but growing headwinds and a rich valuation don't go well together, so I think further downside is ahead.

However, it's important to remember that volatility is a normal part of the investing journey. According to Capital Group, the S&P 500 suffers a decline of 10% or more every 18 months, on average. Bear-market declines of 20% tend to come around every six years, and we are already four years removed from the last bear market in 2022.

Here's the good news: The S&P 500 has delivered a compound annual return of 10.7% since it was established in 1957, even after factoring in every sell-off, correction, and bear market along the way. That means staying invested during periods of uncertainty is critical -- in fact, buying stocks during the scariest moments has been a winning strategy over the last seven decades.
