news.Title: HOG or TSLA: Which Is the Better Value Stock Right Now?
news.Content:
Investors interested in Automotive - Domestic stocks are likely familiar with Harley-Davidson (HOG) and Tesla (TSLA). But which of these two stocks is more attractive to value investors? We'll need to take a closer look to find out.

There are plenty of strategies for discovering value stocks, but we have found that pairing a strong Zacks Rank with an impressive grade in the Value category of our Style Scores system produces the best returns. The Zacks Rank is a proven strategy that targets companies with positive earnings estimate revision trends, while our Style Scores work to grade companies based on specific traits.

Right now, Harley-Davidson is sporting a Zacks Rank of #2 (Buy), while Tesla has a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold). This means that HOG's earnings estimate revision activity has been more impressive, so investors should feel comfortable with its improving analyst outlook. But this is only part of the picture for value investors.

Value investors analyze a variety of traditional, tried-and-true metrics to help find companies that they believe are undervalued at their current share price levels.

Our Value category grades stocks based on a number of key metrics, including the tried-and-true P/E ratio, the P/S ratio, earnings yield, and cash flow per share, as well as a variety of other fundamentals that value investors frequently use.

HOG currently has a forward P/E ratio of 44.88, while TSLA has a forward P/E of 239.49. We also note that HOG has a PEG ratio of 8.23. This figure is similar to the commonly-used P/E ratio, with the PEG ratio also factoring in a company's expected earnings growth rate. TSLA currently has a PEG ratio of 10.53.

Another notable valuation metric for HOG is its P/B ratio of 0.99. Investors use the P/B ratio to look at a stock's market value versus its book value, which is defined as total assets minus total liabilities. By comparison, TSLA has a P/B of 17.93.

These are just a few of the metrics contributing to HOG's Value grade of A and TSLA's Value grade of D.

HOG has seen stronger estimate revision activity and sports more attractive valuation metrics than TSLA, so it seems like value investors will conclude that HOG is the superior option right now.

news.Title: 3 "Magnificent Seven" Stocks to Buy Hand Over Fist in November
news.Content:
The "Magnificent Seven" is perhaps one of the most popular groups of companies on the market. It is made up of tech -- or tech-adjacent -- leaders that have delivered outstanding long-term results, specifically: Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) (NASDAQ: GOOGL), Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN), Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ: META), Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA), and Tesla (NASDAQ: TSLA). In my view, most are worth serious consideration for long-term investors, and three in particular that look attractive going into November are Nvidia, Meta Platforms, and Amazon. Here is why.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

1. Nvidia

Nvidia's fiscal year 2027 second-quarter update (for the period that ended July 2026) was phenomenal. The company's revenue increased by 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, while its GAAP earnings per share came in at $2.46, 128% higher than the year-ago period. Nvidia's results were so strong that its share price jumped post-earnings, which is saying something for a company for which the market has perpetual high expectations.

Nvidia will report its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results in November. They may or may not be quite as strong as the previous update, but the ongoing earnings season has already provided more evidence that the AI tailwind is far from over, and that's great for Nvidia.

It remains the leader in the GPU ( graphics processing unit ) market and has expanded its product offerings, thereby increasing its total addressable market. Nvidia also maintains a wide moat, thanks to its CUDA ecosystem, which creates high switching costs. It's a core reason behind the company's success in recent years. And even though Nvidia has already produced exceptional returns, it's not too late to invest in the stock.

2. Meta Platforms

Many investors remain skeptical of Meta's prospects, considering the company's significant AI-related spending has harmed free cash flow. However, Meta is slowly showing that its efforts are not in vain. The company's Muse AI agent has gained significant traction. Management reported that it has been set up by more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada, with 25% of them using it daily.

Muse is free to use for consumers (up to certain limits), but Meta could monetize it as a shopping assistant by charging merchants small per-transaction fees. Importantly, Meta has launched a small-business version of Muse and released more sophisticated models targeted at companies in expert domains, such as law and finance. Meta is still spending heavily to improve its AI capabilities, and the company's advertising business remains healthy. My view is that Muse's monetization could provide significant new revenue sources and, in the long run, the AI agent will help justify Meta's investments.

Story Continues

3. Amazon

Amazon's cloud business is booming, partly thanks to AI. During the second quarter, Amazon Web Services (AWS) reported its fastest growth rate in 18 quarters. That's a notable achievement, and what's even more exciting is that Amazon is seeing significant demand for its services several years ahead -- it is capacity constrained in the near term and has received orders for 2028.

Meanwhile, the company is working on various initiatives that could help it decrease operating costs. Amazon is increasingly using internally developed custom AI chips, which are often more cost-effective than those it buys from other corporations.

Let's also not ignore the impact AI could have on Amazon's core e-commerce business, which is still, by far, its biggest source of revenue. Various AI tools could improve consumers' search capabilities, making it easier for them to find exactly what they want. Others are helping merchants write better product descriptions faster and automate various other tasks.

These tools could help boost revenue while reducing expenses. Amazon's e-commerce business is a low-margin operation, but AI could help improve margins -- and even minor margin gains could mean billions more in profit over the long run at Amazon's scale. And of course, the company also benefits from a wide moat that stems from multiple sources, including its brand name, network effects, and switching costs. All these factors make Amazon a particularly attractive stock to buy and hold for the long term.

news.Title: Wall St choppy as megacap losses offset chip gains before Fed decision
news.Content:
By Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi

Oct 28 (Reuters) - US stocks wavered on Wednesday as weakness in megacaps such as Tesla and Apple offset chipmaker gains sparked by SK Hynix's bumper results, with focus squarely on hyperscaler earnings and the ‌Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision later in the day.

Memory chipmaker Micron Technology jumped 4.8% to its highest in over two ‌weeks after South Korean rival SK Hynix reported a more than sevenfold jump in quarterly profit. SK Hynix's US-listed shares gained 10.6%.

The Philadelphia chips index was up 0.9%, ​on track to gain for the fourth straight session.

Capping gains on the main benchmarks, Tesla dipped 1.9% after surging more than 9% in the last two sessions. Apple eased 0.6%, while SpaceX dropped 3.2%.

Alphabet advanced 1.2% following a media report that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips.

At 10:01 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 73.40 points, or 0.14%, to 52,450.97. The S&P 500 gained 6.10 points, or 0.09%, ‌to 7,729.20, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 7.13 ⁠points, or 0.03%, to 26,470.68.

Six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors advanced, with communication services leading gains, while real estate lagged.

The Nasdaq has risen about 2% so far this week, following a bruising first ⁠half of the month, as sentiment toward AI improved after Anthropic revealed its US IPO filing on Monday.

The focus now shifts to quarterly results from hyperscalers Microsoft and Alphabet, due after markets close on Wednesday, with both companies expected to report accelerating cloud growth.

Investors will closely scrutinize their capital ​expenditure ​plans for signs that massive AI investments are generating returns, as concerns ​over the viability of debt-funded spending amid rising borrowing ‌costs continue to weigh on the sector.

"We can still see that the AI demand has not paused... the number one worry for investors is not AI valuations anymore, but it's the financing through debt as debt goes through the roof in the US," said Nadia El Bilassy, senior market analyst at Equiti Group.

Also on the day, Vertiv jumped 14% after the digital infrastructure provider raised full-year profit and revenue forecasts, while also topping third-quarter expectations.

Boston Scientific shed 8.2% after the medical device maker trimmed its annual profit forecast.

Looking ahead, the US ‌Fed's policy announcement is due at 2 p.m. ET on Wednesday. The ​market consensus is widely tilted toward a pause following last month's hike, with investors ​more focused on remarks from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh ​and the policy outlook.

Story Continues

Market expectations, however, remain hawkish as traders see at least three 25-basis-point increases by late ‌2027, according to LSEG data, as persistently high inflation ​due to rising energy costs tied ​to the Middle East conflict bolster the case for tighter monetary policy.

September's Personal Consumption Expenditures report, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, could test those bets on Thursday. Third-quarter GDP, which is expected to show 3.2% growth, is also due this week.

Declining ​issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.06-to-1 ratio on ‌the NYSE, while advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.08-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 16 new ​52-week highs and nine new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 52 new highs and 96 new lows.

(Reporting by ​Shashwat Chauhan and Utkarsh Hathi in Bengaluru; Editing by Shilpi Majumdar)

news.Title: Dear Amazon Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for October 29
news.Content:
Amazon.com (AMZN) is set to report its third-quarter results for fiscal 2026 on Oct. 29, after the market closes. Ahead of the results, investors are waiting to see how the company's aggressive artificial intelligence (AI) spending will show up in its earnings and cash position. In August, Amazon pushed its capital spending estimate from $200 billion to $220 billion, mainly due to higher memory and component costs and continued build-out of AI and cloud infrastructure. This is supported by the continuous growth in its AWS segment.

Ahead of its earnings, let's take a closer look at the tech giant.

More News from Barchart

Micron Just Unveiled a New Bonus Plan. What That Means for MU Stock.

PLTR Stock Earnings Preview: What to Expect From Palantir's Q3 Report

Michael Burry Called It 'One of the More Common Frauds.' Oracle Stock Is Down 45% Since.

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

About Amazon Stock

Amazon, headquartered in Seattle, Washington, operates global e-commerce, cloud computing, logistics, advertising, streaming, and AI services. The popular tech giant has a massive market capitalization of $2.69 trillion.

Amazon is focusing on expanding its AI and cloud-computing capabilities while strengthening its retail and logistics operations. The company is investing heavily in data centers and AI services to meet growing demand from businesses and consumers. At the same time, it is updating consumer devices and integrating AI across shopping, delivery, entertainment, and business tools. These efforts reflect its broader strategy to deepen its technology ecosystem, improve customer experiences, and support long-term growth across its global operations.

Amazon's stock is up only 10.5% over the past 52 weeks because strong AWS and AI optimism has been offset by heavy spending and valuation concerns. Investors remain cautious about the company's large capital expenditures on data centers and AI infrastructure, which have weighed on free cash flow. The stock is down 2.4% over the past six months. It reached a 52-week high of $287.20 on Aug. 3, but is down 12% from that level.

AMZN stock is stretched compared to its peers. Its forward-adjusted price-to-earnings ratio of 19.29x is higher than the industry average of 16.05x.

Amazon Delivered Strong First-Half Results on AWS Growth

Amazon reported strong results during the first half of the year. The company's total net sales increased 18.2% year-over-year (YoY) to $382.13 billion. This was driven by AWS revenue, which rose 32.7% from the prior-year period to $79.82 billion. Management highlighted that this is AWS' fastest growth in 18 quarters. In Stores, Amazon set record delivery speeds for Prime members in the first half of the year, which reflects its efficiency. Amazon's EPS grew from $3.27 to $8.53 over the same period.

Story Continues

All eyes were set on Amazon's cash position to gauge the effect of Amazon's aggressive AI spending. For the 12 months ended in June 2026, net cash used in investing activities rose to $216.78 billion. Amazon had cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $80.93 billion, with long-term debt of $128.89 billion as of June 30.

Wall Street analysts are modestly optimistic about Amazon's future earnings. They expect the company's EPS to climb 3.1% YoY to $2.01 for the about-to-be-reported third quarter. For fiscal 2026, EPS is projected to surge 5.3% to $7.55, followed by a 41.1% growth to $10.65 in fiscal 2027.

What Do Analysts Think About AMZN Stock?

Ahead of Amazon's earnings, analysts at Morgan Stanley named AMZN stock a top pick and raised its price target from $335 to $350 while maintaining an "Overweight" rating. Analyst Brian Nowak pointed to faster cloud growth, higher profits, and several AI-related opportunities. Morgan Stanley raised its AWS growth forecasts to 47% in 2027 and 42% in 2028, up from prior estimates of 41% and 37%.

UBS analysts raised their price target on AMZN from $318 to $348, while keeping a "Buy" rating. UBS analyst Stephen Ju believes that analysts are underestimating how much profit AWS can generate from its expanding AI infrastructure. The bank forecasts AWS operating margins of 46% in 2027.

Meanwhile, analysts at Cantor Fitzgerald kept a cautious outlook by lowering the price target from $320 to $310, while maintaining a bullish "Overweight" rating. This revision reflects Amazon's efforts to manage intense competition in the consumer cyclical sector.

AMZN stock has been in the spotlight on Wall Street for some time now, with analysts awarding it a consensus "Strong Buy" rating overall. Of the 56 analysts rating the stock, a majority of 47 rate it a "Strong Buy," six rate it a "Moderate Buy," and three analysts take the middle-of-the-road approach with a "Hold" rating. The consensus price target of $330.18 represents 31% upside from current levels. Moreover, the Street-high price target of $405 indicates a 60% upside.

news.Title: Where Will Oracle Stock Be in 1 Year?
news.Content:
The past year has been a forgettable one for Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) investors, as shares of the cloud infrastructure giant have shed 54% of their value during this period.

This sharp drop in Oracle stock is primarily due to concerns about the massive debt the company has been taking on to fund the build-out of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. However, Wall Street anticipates a major turnaround in Oracle's fortunes over the coming year.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Let's see what Wall Street expects from Oracle stock and check if the AI infrastructure giant can indeed achieve the upside the market expects it to deliver in the next one year.

Oracle could jump over 80% in a year, according to Wall Street

Oracle's 12-month median price target of $240 implies an 84% jump from current levels. Another important point worth noting is that 36 of the 45 analysts, or 80%, rate the stock as a buy.

It is easy to see why Oracle is a Wall Street favorite. The company reported an incredible backlog of $664 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended on Aug. 31). Oracle's remaining performance obligation (RPO) , which refers to the total value of a company's unfulfilled contracts, is poised to drive stronger growth for the company over the coming year.

Oracle points out that its cloud infrastructure revenue increased by 121% in fiscal Q1. That was an improvement over the 93% year-over-year growth in cloud infrastructure revenue the company reported in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. So, Oracle is now converting its backlog into revenue at a stronger pace.

Even better, the company expects its cloud infrastructure revenue growth to accelerate for the rest of the fiscal year, driven by stronger conversion of its RPO into revenue. Not surprisingly, Oracle is anticipating a 34% increase in revenue in fiscal 2027 to at least $90 billion. What's more, analysts are expecting Oracle's revenue to increase at a stronger pace of 46% in fiscal 2028 to $131.8 billion.

This potential acceleration in Oracle's growth should ideally be rewarded with a premium valuation, which is why I expect the stock to easily achieve the price target discussed earlier.

The stock's attractive valuation should pave the way for solid upside

Oracle trades at just 5 times sales, a discount to its five-year average sales multiple of 6.6. For comparison, the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite index has a price-to-sales ratio of 5.1. Ideally, Oracle deserves to trade at a premium due to its huge RPO and its improving growth trajectory.

Story Continues

Assuming Oracle trades at even 7 times sales at the end of fiscal 2028, slightly higher than its five-year average sales multiple, its market cap could reach $923 billion (based on the $131.8 billion estimate noted earlier). That's 133% higher than Oracle's current market cap, indicating that the stock is poised for healthy gains over the next year and a half (as its fiscal 2028 will end in August that year).

As such, Oracle can indeed achieve the 12-month Wall Street target and then head higher, given its strong growth prospects and attractive valuation.

news.Title: 5 Dividend Stocks Yielding Over 5%, Ranked By Safety
news.Content:
Dividend investors can find some enticing yields in the stock market these days. Realty Income (NYSE:O), Verizon (NYSE:VZ), Clorox (NYSE:CLX), VICI Properties (NYSE:VICI), and UPS (NYSE:UPS) all offer payouts exceeding 5%, potentially providing investors with a substantial stream of passive income.

However, not all high-yield dividends are the same. Some payouts are on rock-solid ground while others are much riskier. Here's how these five stocks rank based on dividend safety from worst to first.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

No. 5: UPS

UPS has a strong dividend track record. The logistics giant has either maintained or increased its payment every year since going public in 1999. In its quarterly dividend press release, the company says that the "commitment to the dividend is one of UPS's core principles and a hallmark of the company's financial strength." That would seem to make its current 6.5% yield (which is several times the S&P 500 's current 1.1% yield) compelling. That's until you dig a little deeper into its financials.

The company currently expects to generate $6.1 billion of adjusted free cash flow this year after funding $3 billion in capital expenditures. With dividend payments expected to be around $5.4 billion, that's tight coverage. On a positive note, that's a meaningful improvement from last year when its free cash flow didn't cover the dividend. With UPS' financial results showing signs of improvement, the risk of a dividend reduction is fading.

No. 4: Clorox

Clorox has increased its dividend for 49 straight years, putting it one year shy of Dividend King status (a company with 50 or more years of annual dividend increases). That would seemingly make its 5.8%-yielding dividend attractive, especially given its business of selling leading consumer household products such as Clorox, Glad, and Purell.

However, like UPS, its underlying financial results tell a different story. The company currently pays $5.00 per share in dividends each year. In fiscal 2026, Clorox earned $4.81 per share, down from $6.52 in fiscal 2025 and below its dividend payment. Meanwhile, it generated only $405 million in free cash flow, short of the $602 million it paid in dividends (though it covered the dividend after adjusting for a $476 million payment to terminate a joint venture). On a positive note, Clorox expects its earnings to improve in fiscal 2027 while delivering strong cash flow generation. So the dividend isn't at risk of a reduction; it's just not as safe as you might expect from a company with its track record.

Story Continues

No. 3: VICI Properties

Vici Properties has increased its dividend every year since its formation in 2018. The real estate investment trust (REIT) has grown its payout at a 6.1% compound annual rate, much faster than other REITs focused on triple-net leased real estate (2.5% average growth rate). It currently yields 7.5%, one of the highest yields in the S&P 500.

The company owns a growing portfolio of market-leading gaming, hospitality, wellness, entertainment, and leisure destinations, secured by long-term net leases (average remaining term of 39.4 years). Its leases increasingly link rents to inflation (45% in 2026) and predominantly feature parent-company guarantees and master-lease protection (over 80%). Meanwhile, it pays out a conservative 75% of its stable cash flow as dividends, providing a nice cushion. The company's biggest weakness is high tenant concentration (its two largest tenants comprise 70% of its rent), though it's steadily diversifying.

No. 2: Verizon

Verizon has increased its dividend for 20 straight years. The telecom giant's payout currently yields 6.6%.

Unlike those of UPS and Clorox, Verizon's dividend is well covered by cash flow. The company has generated $18 billion in free cash flow through the first nine months of this year. That easily covered the $8.8 billion it paid in dividends, providing the company with excess cash to repurchase shares ($4 billion) and strengthen its already rock-solid balance sheet (A-/BBB+/Baa1 ratings). The reason it doesn't rank first is that Verizon faces significant competitive pressure ( including a potential new entrant in the U.S. mobile market ), which could weigh on its margins and growth prospects.

No. 1: Realty Income

Realty Income is also a REIT focused on triple-net leased real estate. However, it's much more diversified by property type (retail, industrial, gaming, data centers, and other properties) and tenant (its top two tenants supply only 6.4% of its rent). It also has a strong balance sheet (A-rated compared to BBB-/Baa3 for Vici).

The REIT has been a stellar dividend stock. It has increased its monthly dividend 136 times since its 1994 public market listing, growing it at a 4.1% compound annual rate. It generates resilient, steadily rising cash flow and has a conservative dividend payout ratio (below 75% of its cash flow). Its combination of diversification, stable cash flow, and conservative financial profile makes it the safest dividend payer in this group.

A dividend's safety matters more than its yield

All five of these stocks offer attractive dividend yields, but their payouts aren't equally secure. Realty Income and VICI Properties stand out because their recurring rental income provides solid dividend coverage, while Verizon's improving cash flow supports its generous payout. Clorox and UPS face greater challenges, with dividends consuming more cash than their businesses have recently generated. Realty Income and Verizon are the safest choices in this group for investors seeking dependable passive income.

news.Title: Why SK Hynix Stock Popped Today
news.Content:
Korean memory chip manufacturer SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) stock raced out of the gate Wednesday morning, shooting up 10.5% in the first 10 minutes of trading after exceeding expectations in its Q3 earnings report this morning.

Heading into the report, analysts expected SK Hynix to earn 77.5 trillion South Korean won for the quarter, but the company actually reported an operating profit of 83.3 trillion won -- about $62.1 billion -- for an operating profit margin of 80%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

SK Hynix Q3 earnings

Revenue surged ahead 328% year over year to 104.6 trillion won, and on the bottom line, net income was up 216% at 39.8 trillion won -- $29.7 billion, a net profit margin of 38%.

SK Hynix makes both NAND flash memory and DRAM, including DRAM high-bandwidth memory (HBM). The company credited sales of cutting-edge HBM4 products for much of its sales and profit margin growth, and predicted that HBM4 sales will, in fact, be its "mainstream product" in Q4 and beyond.

What's next for SK Hynix stock

If you think that sounds like good news for SK Hynix and its profits, get ready to be even more impressed. Management advised that it has secured long-term agreements for more than 50% of its expected production in the 2027-2028 time frame, locking in high profit margins for the next two years and mitigating the risk that any overproduction of memory might reverse its growth in profits.

Even absent this move, however, things would be going well for SK Hynix, which says it's seeing a "virtuous cycle... in which AI-driven productivity gains... lead to greater AI adoption, which in turn drives increased investment in infrastructure," growing both sales and profits.

Trading at less than 8x earnings today, SK Hynix looks like a long-term AI winner.

news.Title: SK Hynix sparks a chip rally: Two oversold enablers primed to rebound
news.Content:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.

Investing.com — A blowout quarterly report from memory titan SK Hynix has reignited the global semiconductor trade. Delivering a staggering 632% surge in operating profit alongside a planned $75.5 billion shareholder return, the South Korean chipmaker revealed an even bigger catalyst: the artificial intelligence memory shortage will persist through at least 2030, with over half of its 2027 and 2028 production capacity already sold out under long-term agreements.

Yet in an industry infamous for brutal boom-and-bust cycles, explosive earnings often trigger immediate fears of a cyclical peak. But this deficit cannot be solved overnight—eliminating the bottleneck requires producers to pour billions into new cleanrooms, wafer fabrication systems, and complex 3D packaging.

news.Title: Is Tesla's Narrative Shifting? Why the Stock Deserves a Second Look
news.Content:
Electric vehicle (EV) and tech giant Tesla TSLA has had a rough year in the markets, especially after a tough stretch of challenges that weighed on sentiment. Lately, though, the story seems to be turning. The stock gained 9.5% over the past two trading sessions. Two catalysts may explain the move.

Barclays upgraded Tesla to Overweight and raised its price target to $450 from $370, pointing to a possible SpaceX SPCX merger. Separately, Latvia authorized Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) software, per Teslarati, making it the 10th EU country to do so.

But the rally does not seem just headline-driven. The third-quarter numbers gave investors real reasons for optimism.

Tesla, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tesla, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tesla, Inc. Quote

Demand Outruns Supply as FSD Adoption Climbs

Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the last reported quarter, its second straight quarter above 480,000 units. It also posted its highest passenger vehicle order backlog in four years. Management said demand is running well ahead of production, helped by a broader product lineup and growing adoption of FSD.

Active paid FSD customers rose 67% year over year to 1.74 million. More than 75% of new North American deliveries included a paid FSD subscription at delivery. In Europe, regulatory approval has spread steadily since the Netherlands led in April, followed by Lithuania, Estonia, Denmark, Belgium, Slovenia, Czechia, Croatia and Slovakia. Latvia is the latest, with a software rollout to begin soon.

The product pipeline is widening too. The Semi has entered production, and the Roadster was revealed, with production targeted for 2028.

Margins Are Improving

Profitability moved in the right direction. Automotive gross margin improved to 18.5% from 17% a year earlier. The energy business also did well. Storage deployments reached 13.7 GWh, up 10% year over year, and energy gross margin jumped to 33.1% from 20.4% in the second quarter of 2026. Demand looks set to continue. CEO Elon Musk said Megapack supply for 2027 is almost sold out.

The AI and Robotaxi Chapter Is Taking Shape

Musk has framed AI, autonomous vehicles, robotaxis and robotics as Tesla's next growth chapters, and there is now visible progress. Tesla began deploying Cybercabs in Austin in September 2026. Cumulative unsupervised Robotaxi miles rose eightfold sequentially to nearly 2 million. Musk said the Austin Cybercab fleet has grown tenfold in roughly a month since launch.

Image Source: Tesla, Inc.

Story Continues

Management expects Robotaxi operations to contribute more meaningfully to revenues from next year. Customer-owned vehicles could start joining the fleet around the second quarter of 2027. Optimus has entered early production on a high-volume line in Fremont, though the ramp will be slow given it is an entirely new product.

Trimmed Capex & Balance Sheet Strength

Capital discipline was a key concern coming into the quarter, with heavy capex and negative free cash flow weighing on investors. Tesla addressed both. It ended the quarter with about $45.4 billion in cash and short-term investments. Free cash flow swung to positive $1.53 billion from negative $1.09 billion in the second quarter of 2026. Management also trimmed 2026 capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion and secured up to $30 billion in borrowing capacity, with no draws planned this year.

The SpaceX Factor

The SpaceX relationship adds another layer. Terafab, a joint project with SpaceX, aims to produce the advanced AI chips Tesla needs for Optimus and its wider AI ambitions. Securing compute is critical as Tesla expands beyond EVs, and a closer tie-up could give it access to capital, engineering talent and infrastructure that would take years to build alone.

A full merger is a different question. Both companies are pivoting toward AI, and consolidation promises meaningful synergies. But SpaceX would likely have to pay a substantial premium to win over Tesla shareholders. With a favorable regulatory climate expected in 2027, independent committees weighing fiduciary duties, and Tesla's strong cash position and voting structure, a valuation bump looks almost necessary.

The Risks Haven't Gone Away

None of this makes Tesla a risk-free story. Operating expenses remain high, supply chain challenges persist, and operating profits are expected to decline year over year in the coming quarters as costs rise to fund the next growth cycle. Robotaxi and Optimus revenues still depend on execution and regulatory approvals.

Our Take: TSLA Stock Worth Holding Now

These risks are real, but they are the price of a business trying to change shape. The shift is genuine. Demand is strong, margins are recovering, cash flow has turned positive, and the AI roadmap now has tangible milestones behind it.

But the next few quarters will be heavy on spending and light on profit, and the Robotaxi and Optimus payoffs still depend on regulators and execution. This may not be the moment to buy TSLA stock outright, but we think that the stock should earn a place on your watchlist again.

If Robotaxi revenues start showing up next year as management expects, today's skeptics may be late. For investors with a long horizon, dips from here look more like opportunities.

news.Title: AI giants' funding ambitions test Wall Street's appetite for risk
news.Content:
By Niket Nishant

Oct 28 (Reuters) - The heavyweights of the AI industry are facing a reckoning on Wall Street, reflecting concerns over who will bear the cost of the artificial intelligence buildout that has fueled much of this year's ‌stock market gains.

Anthropic revealed paperwork for its initial public offering on Monday, paving the way for a share sale reportedly worth $100 ‌billion as early as next month.

Meta also unveiled a plan this week that could bring it as much as $97.5 billion through equity offerings over the coming months.

The markets ​will also await signs of fundraising plans when Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings later on Wednesday.

By pressing ahead with their enormous funding plans, the biggest AI players are wagering that investors' fear of missing out on future returns will outweigh their fear of overpaying for them.

AI stocks accounted for nearly 75% of the S&P 500 index's return in the first half of 2026, according to an analysis by Carson Group.

"The growth of ‌the AI ecosystem over the last several years ⁠is quite astounding," said Ehren Stanhope, chief investment strategist at Franklin Templeton's Canvas. "The idea that such large firms can compound earnings at triple digits for multiple years seems to defy the laws of economics."

But Wall Street's ⁠reaction in recent weeks suggests ambition is no longer enough to get investors to open their wallets.

Meta's shares have fallen more than 11% since it unveiled plans last week to create a new class of stock to fund share sales and reported its first quarterly cash burn in more than ​a decade.

While ​Anthropic's soaring revenue helped ease AI growth concerns, its mounting losses have ​raised fresh questions. The company's net loss widened to $80.7 ‌billion in the first half of 2026 from $13 billion a year earlier.

"Not even Anthropic will get a blank check," said Matt Kennedy, senior strategist at Renaissance Capital.

The funding demands are coming amid growing circular financing arrangements, in which money invested in AI companies can flow back to their investors through spending on computing infrastructure and services.

SMALLER FIRMS FEEL THE HEAT

Companies that are relatively small but carry heavy debt are in a more bleak position. CoreWeave has seen its bond yields soar, raising questions about how much it would have to pay in interest ‌when it raises debt next.

"The danger (for CoreWeave) is the next loan. And how ​soon CoreWeave needs it matters as much as the price," said Matthew Tuttle, founder ​and CEO of Tuttle Capital Management.

Story Continues

Last week, CoreWeave's shares ​hit their lowest since May 2025 as concerns about its reliance on debt grew.

The stock has rebounded around ‌10% so far this week, but "a company surviving and its ​old shareholders winning are two different ​outcomes," Tuttle added.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk recently said neocloud companies could face significant consolidation and failures. He ruled out any acquisition of a neocloud company by SpaceX, saying such a deal would be "pointless."

Still, this year's AI capex by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle ​and Microsoft would likely equal their cumulative spend ‌since the November 2022 launch of ChatGPT, according to data from J.P. Morgan.

"In effect, the Street appears to be ​underwriting the AI data center monetization case," wrote Dubravko Lakos-Bujas, the brokerage's head of global markets strategy.

(Reporting by Niket ​Nishant in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Pritam Biswas; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

news.Title: This Nvidia chart shows why the AI compute shortage remains acute
news.Content:
This week has shown that the appetite to build out AI infrastructure and put it to use isn't slowing down, contrary to market jitters.

Rental rates for older-generation Nvidia ( NVDA ) GPUs, known as Blackwell and Hopper, continue to rise, suggesting that the shortage of compute remains acute, BCA Research chief economist Peter Berezin pointed out (see chart below).

An acute shortage occurs when demand outstrips supply.

"I think we are heading for an AI capex bust but probably not until 2028," Berezin said.

Add it to the fresh list of bullish indicators on AI, which has helped bring the bulls back into top momentum tech names such as Micron ( MU ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), and Broadcom ( AVGO ).

South Korean memory-chip player SK Hynix ( SKHY ) said on Wednesday it plans to return a total of $75 billion to shareholders this year through stock buybacks and dividends.

This was on the heels of the company's third quarter revenue and operating profit both hitting record highs for a sixth straight quarter.

"Tight supply and demand conditions continued due to growing demand for AI memory, leading to sustained rise in memory prices," SK Hynix CFO Woo-hyun Kim said on the earnings call.

Meanwhile, Anthropic's hotly anticipated IPO prospectus, which dropped on Monday, has been well-received by the markets.

Anthropic's ( ANTH.PVT ) first-half 2026 revenue surged to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion a year earlier, the prospectus showed.

Dive deeper into Anthropic's highly anticipated IPO

Anthropic publicly files IPO prospectus, noting strong revenue growth and massive spending

5 unexpected risk factors Anthropic is worried about

Anthropic is losing $80 billion on paper — and just made money where it counts

The prospectus shows Anthropic's revenue base has become more diversified this year, with customers outside the top five now making up about 79% of sales, up from 64% in the first quarter.

In its simplest form, the metric indicates broader adoption of Anthropic's technology.

"Overall, the numbers are showing massive eye-popping growth from a broadening group of customers as ANT aggressively goes after the enterprise market in this AI Revolution," Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives said.

Anthropic also had about $131.7 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026.

That is an impressive amount of liquidity for a company that's investing billions into AI infrastructure.

news.Title: 台股狂飆939點來真的？美伊和談重燃行情　郭哲榮點名這些低基期補漲股
news.Content:
台股今（28）日多頭氣勢強勁，終場加權指數狂飆 939.35 點，收在 47,035.58 點，成交量為 7,221.35 億元，期貨盤中更一度猛拉超過千點。面對這波驚天動地的漲勢， 摩爾投顧投資長郭哲榮（哲哲） 指出，台股爆發強勁反彈背後的核心推手，源於地緣政治迎來歷史性轉折，隨著美伊衝突與俄烏戰爭傳出和談曙光，觀望資金迅速回流，同時也為低基期補漲股開啟了絕佳的接棒舞台。

【美伊和談迎曙光！地緣政治解凍全球AI資金鏈】

中東與俄烏衝突長期推升油價與通膨，迫使聯準會維持高利率，高借貸成本也讓高度依賴資金灌溉的 AI 企業承受嚴峻考驗。郭哲榮分析，隨著伊朗最高領袖釋出談判訊號，雙方具備以戰逼和的交集。若和平協議達成，油價與通膨降溫將帶動企業資金成本大幅下降，被壓抑的 AI 科技股可望迎來資金回流派對，甚至為大盤帶來再向上推升一千至兩千點的龐大動能。

【AI裁員浪潮袭來！買進AI股票當職場失業保險】

除了宏觀資金面，AI 技術進步對就業市場的衝擊同樣值得關注。全球科技巨頭微軟規劃精簡高達 6 萬名員工，顯示企業導入 AI 提升效率、削減傳統人力的不可逆趨勢。面對被科技淘汰的風險，郭哲榮提出獨到觀點：與其消極擔心失業，不如主動布局 ASIC 晶片、自動駕駛與機器人等 AI 產業鏈，將投資 AI 股票視為個人的「失業保險」，讓科技紅利轉化為資本利得，對沖職場風險。

【低基期與黑馬股接棒！華新科、精材台股後市解析】

在個股與族群配置上，郭哲榮點名 強勢股 與 低基期補漲股 並進的關鍵標的：

1. 華新科（2492） ： 在 369 元附近低檔布局後，單日大漲近 7%，波段獲利已達 44%，展現被動元件低基期的強勁爆發力。

2. 精材（3374） ：受惠於強勢技術線型，股價由 180 至 190 元低位一路飆升至 500 元，波段漲幅高達 159%。不過因已遠離成本區， 特別叮嚀投資人切勿盲目追高。

3. 智原（3035） ：智原具備 ASIC 客製化晶片題材且基期較低，反彈動能備受期待。

4. 記憶體族群 ：AI伺服器對高效能記憶體的需求持續受到市場關注，SK 海力士優異財報帶動韓國股市打底完成，記憶體長線缺貨與需求趨勢依舊確立，低檔拉回仍是布局時機。

news.Title: All Eyes on Fed's FOMC Meeting Outcome
news.Content:
We have a solid slate of reports this morning, both of the earnings variety and regarding economic growth. Pre-market indexes continue marching into the green: the Dow +23 points, the Nasdaq +119 (on the continued AI outlook once again viewed favorably) and the S&P 500 +18 points. The small-cap Russell 2000 is currently up 1 point.

The AI trade — ahead of key hyperscalers reporting Q3 earnings this afternoon: Alphabet GOOGL and Microsoft MSFT — has usurped high oil price fears for the time being. Spot oil prices are now $102 per barrel (/bbl) on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) and $115/bbl on London-based Brent crude following a refinery attack in Saudi Arabia by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels of Yemen.

September Trade & Inventories Spell Economic Health

Ahead of today's open, the latest Advanced Trade Balance for September is out, dipping deeper into deficit territory to -$134.9 billion, from a slightly improved revision to -$132.1 billion the prior month. Both Imports and Exports were up roughly 2 1/2%, to $344.1 billion and $209.2 billion, respectively. Imports are coming in far ahead based largely on supplies for the grand AI buildout: computers, chips, etc.

Wholesale Inventories for September gained +0.6% month over month, 10 basis points (bps) higher than expected but -10 bps from the prior month's +0.7%. Year over year Wholesale Inventories are up +7.4% to $1.01 trillion this morning. Meanwhile, Retail Inventories came in at the prior month's level: +0.3%. Year over year, Retail Inventories are +4.8% to $885.3 billion.

Q3 Earnings at a Glance: ETSY, BIIB, PSX & More

Etsy ETSY is enjoying its best performance in recent memory of late, with Q3 earnings outperforming estimates by +15.67% to $1.55 per share. Revenues cruised to a beat of their own: $692.47 million, which is +3.5% ahead of the Zacks consensus and the year-ago $678 million reported. Shares had already gained +58% year to date, and are up another +6% in pre-market trading.

Biotech giant Biogen BIIB posted even more impressive numbers ahead of today's open, with earnings of $2.62 per share versus expectations of $2.06, for a +27.2% positive surprise. Revenues of $2.88 billion outpaced estimates by +8%. The drugmaker also raised guidance, but shares are flat pre-market. BIIB shares have gained +43% year to date.

Speaking as we were about oil prices, Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy)-rated oil refiner Phillips 66 PSX reported earnings of $14.08 per share, solidly ahead of the $11.97 per share expected. Revenues absolutely destroyed estimates in Q3: $51.51 billion versus the Zacks consensus forecast of $33.72 billion. Shares are up modestly ahead of the opening bell, but have gained +108% year to date.

Apparel brand company V.F. Corp. VFC also posted strong results in its fiscal Q2 report this morning, with earnings of $0.70 per share storming past expectations by +29.63%. Revenues also beat, but by a much more tame +0.07% to $2.70 billion in the quarter. The company did not raise earnings guidance, however, on weakness in its Vans brand. Shares are down -3% in early trading.

Story Continues

What to Expect from the Stock Market Today

At 2pm ET this afternoon, we'll hear the latest monetary policy decision from the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) , which is expected to remain unchanged in the +3.75-4.00% range, after a 25 bps hike during the last meeting. Odds for another 25 bps hike increase for the next and final meeting of the FOMC in 2026 on December 9th. Don't expect much being telegraphed ahead of time by Fed Chair Kevin Warsh; he doesn't believe in offering guidance on future rate policy.

After the close, Google and YouTube parent Alphabet is expected to have growth +2.44% on earnings year over year, with revenues up +27.82%. Microsoft's hyperscaling efforts are expected to be pronounced in fiscal Q1: +14% on earnings growth and +16.6% on revenues. ServiceNow NOW in anticipated to have advanced +6.25% in year-over-year earnings, +19.96% on revenues. Meanwhile, Ford F is seen as generating negative growth on both earnings and sales: -13.33% and -3.21%, respectively, in is Q3 report after today's close.

news.Title: If I Were Brand New to Investing, This Is the 1 Surefire ETF I'd Buy and Hold for the Next 30 Years
news.Content:
For inexperienced and experienced investors alike, investing in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT: VOO) is a fine idea -- especially if you aim to hold for many years or decades. It's an exchange-traded fund -- a fund that trades like a stock -- and it tracks the S&P 500 , which comprises 500 of America's biggest companies.

Indeed, while there are thousands of stocks in the U.S., these 500 make up around 80% of the total value of the U.S. stock market. That's why the S&P 500 is often used as a proxy for the total U.S. stock market.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

You can see that there's a lot of disparity in the weightings, and that's because, like many indexes, the S&P 500 is market-cap weighted , meaning that bigger companies will wield more influence than smaller ones. That can reasonably be viewed as a problem right now, because most of the index's value is held in the top holdings, and smaller index components will have little chance of moving the needle. (Those who would rather own a fund that holds each component in roughly equal measure should check out the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEMKT: RSP).)

Pretty good, eh? (Note, though, that over many decades, its average gain has been closer to 10%.)

Why invest in the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF?

Here are some reasons why I like this index fund:

It sports an ultra-low expense ratio (annual fee) of just 0.03%, costing you only $3 per $10,000 you invest in the fund.

It offers diversification, spanning many industries. When one drops sharply, the others can offset that to some degree.

It can outperform many growth stocks, especially overvalued ones.

It contains both growth stocks and value stocks, dividend payers and non-payers. It's broad!

I would also argue that the heavy weighting of big tech stocks isn't necessarily problematic. They're huge and influential because the companies have grown so robustly over the years -- because they're doing a lot of things right. Meanwhile, those who manage the S&P 500 index regularly cull less-well-performing stocks and add more relevant companies. It's not a static group of stocks.

Story Continues

Give this solid ETF some consideration for your long-term portfolio, understanding that when the market pulls back, as it occasionally will, so will this ETF. But over many years, the S&P 500 has always recovered from drops and gone on to set new highs.

news.Title: AMD, Broadcom, and Micron stocks lead chip sector higher for third day in a row
news.Content:
Semiconductor stocks edged higher on Wednesday, with the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) rising for a third day in a row.

Shares of AI chip heavyweight Nvidia ( NVDA ) rose almost 1% before trimming gains, while AMD ( AMD ) and Broadcom ( AVGO ) edged higher. Intel ( INTC ) also trimmed gains.

The move came after SK Hynix ( SKHY ) saw profits increase sevenfold last quarter . The South Korean memory maker sees a supply shortage for memory heading into 2030 as AI inference surges and adoption shifts from cloud providers to physical AI applications like robotics and autonomous driving.

Shares of peers Micron Technology ( MU ) and Samsung Electronics ( 005930.KS ) jumped 4% and 9%, respectively. Among semiconductor equipment makers, Applied Materials ( AMAT ) and Lam Research ( LRCX ) also rose more than 2%.

Semiconductor companies have been key beneficiaries of the AI build-out. Concerns over AI spending and neocloud debt weighed on the sector in recent weeks, but improving sentiment has driven chip stocks higher over the past three sessions.

Not all corners of the AI trade jumped. Seagate ( STX ) declined despite beating on both the top and bottom lines in its latest quarter. Total revenue jumped, but the actual volume of data storage shipped was flat compared to last quarter. Investors took profits after shares of the hard disk drive maker rose 140% year to date.

Meanwhile, peer Sandisk ( SNDK ), which reports on Thursday, gained more than 4% in premarket. The stock rose after Seagate confirmed that AI and data center demand remains white-hot, with customer storage commitments locked through 2028-2030.

Ines Ferre is a senior business reporter for Yahoo Finance.

news.Title: Sandisk Stock Is Down 45% From Its High. History Suggests This Is What Happens Next.
news.Content:
In February 2025, Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) spun off from Western Digital to become a stand-alone company for the second time, after Western Digital acquired it in May 2016. Since the spinoff, Sandisk has been one of the stock market's best performers, up nearly 3,400%.

Despite Sandisk's impressive track record, the past few months have been a roller-coaster ride. On June 25, the stock reached an all-time high, but it's now down 45% from that peak (as of Oct. 23). That's not ideal for those who bought near the peak, but history has some encouraging news for investors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Why Sandisk stock has become popular over the past year

As one of the premier flash memory and storage hardware manufacturers, Sandisk is a huge beneficiary of the ongoing artificial intelligence trend . Major tech companies are rushing to build data centers and other AI infrastructure that require this hardware to train and scale AI.

This huge increase in demand has led to a supply shortage, which isn't ideal for AI hyperscalers ( Amazon , Microsoft , Alphabet , and Meta Platforms ), but it has worked in Sandisk's favor, giving it significant pricing power.

For perspective, in the fourth quarter of its fiscal 2026 (ended July 3), Sandisk's revenue jumped 372% year over year to $9 billion, with two-thirds of that coming from higher pricing and the other third coming from higher volumes. Its gross margins also expanded from 26% to 85%.

SNDK Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts

What history says about the stock

No one can predict how any stock will perform -- and past happenings don't guarantee future happenings -- but looking at historical performance helps you gauge how much volatility to expect . In the short time since Sandisk became a public company, one thing has been clear: High volatility is par for the course. news.Title: IBM vs. Qualcomm: Which AI Tech Giant Has More Upside Now?
news.Content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM and Qualcomm Incorporated QCOM are legacy tech behemoths aggressively expanding into AI infrastructure and enterprise AI solutions, with growing exposure to edge computing and next-generation AI workloads. IBM offers cloud and data solutions that aid enterprises in digital transformation. In addition to hybrid cloud services, the company provides advanced information technology solutions, computer systems, quantum computing and supercomputing solutions, enterprise software, storage systems and microelectronics.

Qualcomm offers high-performance, low-power chip designs for mobile devices, PCs, XR (Extended Reality), automotive, wearable, robotics, connectivity and AI use cases. The company boasts a comprehensive intellectual property portfolio comprising 4G, 5G and other technologies. Qualcomm's brands include Snapdragon systems-on-chip, FastConnect Wi-Fi and Bluetooth systems, and Qualcomm-branded 4G, 5G and IOT equipment. The company is currently integrating on-device generative AI into all of its product lines.

Let us delve deeper into the companies' competitive dynamics to understand which is better positioned in the industry and warrants a place in your investment portfolio.

The Case for IBM

IBM is poised to benefit from healthy demand trends for hybrid cloud and AI, which drive the Software and Consulting segments. The company's growth is expected to be aided by analytics, cloud computing and security in the long term. With a surge in traditional cloud-native workloads and associated applications, along with a rise in generative AI deployment, there is a radical expansion in the number of cloud workloads that enterprises are currently managing. This has resulted in heterogeneous, dynamic and complex infrastructure strategies, which have led firms to undertake a cloud-agnostic and interoperable approach to highly secure multi-cloud management, translating into a healthy demand for IBM hybrid cloud solutions.

IBM has introduced a self-hosted deployment option for IBM Bob, its agentic software development platform. The move is aimed at helping enterprises adopt AI-powered software development and modernization tools while retaining greater control over sensitive data, source code and development environments. The offering can be deployed across on-premises, private-cloud, sovereign-cloud and air-gapped infrastructure, making it particularly relevant for organizations with stringent security, regulatory and data-residency requirements. By enabling customers to run supported AI models within controlled environments or connect to external models through hybrid configurations, IBM is seeking to address growing enterprise demand for secure and governed AI adoption.

Despite solid hybrid cloud and AI traction, IBM is facing stiff competition from Amazon.com, Inc. 's AMZN AWS and Microsoft Corporation 's MSFT Azure. Increasing pricing pressure is eroding margins, and profitability has trended down over the years, barring occasional spikes. The company faces a potent threat from AI firm Anthropic as the latter's Claude Code tool can modernize legacy COBOL systems — a foundational programming language deeply embedded in IBM's mainframe ecosystem. With Claude Code proposing to substantially automate code exploration, documentation, refactoring and security analysis, it threatened to reduce enterprises' reliance on specialized legacy service providers like IBM, putting its sustenance at stake.

Story Continues

The Case for QCOM

Qualcomm envisions solid growth opportunities within the mobile space, driven by the strength of its Snapdragon portfolio. Leveraging multi-core CPUs with cutting-edge features, advanced graphics and global network connectivity, Qualcomm Snapdragon mobile platforms deliver fast performance, superb power efficiency, brilliant camera capabilities and state-of-the-art security solutions. Smartphones and mobile devices built with Snapdragon mobile platforms enable immersive augmented reality and virtual reality experiences, brilliant camera capabilities, superior 4G LTE and 5G connectivity, and state-of-the-art security solutions.

The company is also foraying deeper into the realm of AI capabilities within the laptop and desktop business with the launch of the Snapdragon X chip for mid-range AI desktops and laptops. The strategy is aimed at moving beyond the slowing smartphone industry, which is its primary breadwinner. In addition to diversifying its revenue stream, this is likely to further extend QCOM's AI footprint. It is also gaining traction in the vehicle-to-everything (V2X) communication systems market with the buyout of Autotalks. With seamless access to Autotalks' comprehensive V2X expertise, it has been able to offer an extensive suite of automotive-qualified global V2X solutions for installation in vehicles, as well as two-wheelers and roadside infrastructure. The company's V2X chipsets offer production-ready standalone solutions purpose-built for global applications, resulting in direct communication becoming more pervasive.

Despite efforts to ramp up its AI initiatives, Qualcomm has been facing tough competition from Intel in the AI PC market. Shift in the share among OEMs at the premium tier has reduced Qualcomm's near-term opportunity to sell integrated chipsets from the Snapdragon platform. Memory supply constraints and related pricing are adversely impacting its handset revenues as OEMs (particularly in China) continued to draw down channel inventory. Management reiterated that QCT handset revenues from China-based customers are expected to bottom out in the fiscal third quarter and resume sequential growth in the following quarter as the inventory drawdown eases.

How Do Zacks Estimates Compare for IBM & QCOM?

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for IBM's 2026 sales implies a year-over-year rise of 4.4%, while that of EPS indicates growth of 7.1%. EPS estimates have been trending northward (up 0.5%) on average over the past 60 days.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Qualcomm's fiscal 2026 sales suggests a year-over-year fall of 2.8%, while that for EPS implies a decline of 12.6%. The EPS estimates have remained static over the past 60 days.

Price Performance & Valuation of IBM & QCOM

Over the past year, IBM has plunged 20% against the industry's growth of 109%. Qualcomm has gained 1.7% over the same period.

IBM looks more attractive than Qualcomm from a valuation standpoint. Going by the price/sales ratio, IBM's shares currently trade at 3.3 forward sales, lower than 4.4 for Qualcomm.

IBM or QCOM: Which is a Better Pick?

IBM carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) while Qualcomm has a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell).

You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

While IBM expects sales to improve in 2026, Qualcomm expects revenues to decrease year over year. Qualcomm has shown relatively steady revenue growth for years, while IBM has been facing a bumpy road. IBM is trading relatively cheaply compared with Qualcomm, although it has lagged the latter in terms of price performance.

With a better Zacks Rank, stable free cash flow and software-driven revenues leaning toward enterprise SaaS/AI transformation, IBM appears to be comparatively better placed than Qualcomm. Consequently, IBM seems to be the better investment option at the moment.

news.Title: Fed大考來襲 台指期夜盤又陷47K保衛戰 費半小漲1％
news.Content:
市場在聯準會（Fed）利率決議與科技巨頭財報公布前保持謹慎。台指期夜盤稍早雖一度續揚133點，報47382點，但隨後震盪翻黑，一度下挫157點，報47092點。周三（28日）美股一開盤，4大指數同步小漲，與台股連動密切的費城半導體指數漲幅逾1%。

周三美股未能跟隨亞洲股市的強勁漲勢。投資人還在等待Fed稍晚將公布的貨幣政策決定。市場普遍預計Fed將維持利率不變。摩根大通分析師在報告中指出，他們預計Fed政策制定者當中至少會出現2張反對票，這可能向市場釋放鷹派訊號。

如果Fed最終選擇按兵不動，主席華許（Kevin Warsh）可能面臨外界壓力，需要解釋政策制定者為何此時不採取行動，畢竟上個月Fed官員還一致投票支持升息，以應對不斷上升的通膨壓力。

除了Fed利率決策，微軟與Alphabet將於周三美股盤後公布的財報也是投資人關注的焦點。隨著市場重新相信AI領域的巨額投資最終能夠帶來回報，交易員正重新買入科技股。

news.Content:
Investing.com -- Quantum computing has had a rough ride on Wall Street. Not long ago, stocks tied to the technology were market darlings, fueled by visions of machines that could one day tackle problems beyond the reach of conventional computers. Now, many of the sector's best-known names have slumped, valuations are under scrutiny, and investors are asking a blunt question: When will the promise turn into a business?

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Enter Intel (NASDAQ:INTC). In a deal announced after the close of trading Monday, the chipmaker agreed to acquire Israeli quantum-software company Classiq. Bloomberg put the price at about $2.3 billion, although Intel did not disclose financial terms. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approvals.

The move matters because Classiq works on a crucial piece of the quantum puzzle: software. Its platform helps developers design quantum algorithms and translate them into instructions that can run on different types of quantum hardware. Intel, meanwhile, has spent more than a decade developing silicon-based "spin qubits" and the manufacturing technology needed to build them. Pairing those efforts could give Intel a more complete offering, from the underlying processor to the tools used to program it.

For Intel, this is more than a research project. The company wants quantum computing to become a commercially useful part of its broader computing business, rather than a science experiment confined to laboratories. A large acquisition sends a clear signal that a major chipmaker sees strategic value in the field—even if the financial payoff may still be years away.

That signal could give investors in quantum stocks a reason to look up. IONQ Inc (NYSE:IONQ), D Wave Quantum Inc (NASDAQ:QBTS), Rigetti Computing Inc (NASDAQ:RGTI) and Quantum Computing Inc (NASDAQ:QUBT) have all drawn interest from traders betting that quantum technology could become a major new market. Quantinuum (NASDAQ:QNT) is another closely watched name.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

But several quantum stocks have suffered steep declines. D-Wave recently touched a fresh 52-week low, while IonQ and Rigetti have also fallen sharply from earlier highs. The pressure reflects more than fading enthusiasm. Investors are weighing high valuations, potential share dilution, volatile markets and the long road from technical progress to repeatable revenue.

Story Continues

Intel's deal offers a fresh narrative: Quantum computing is not just a speculative theme for small, early-stage companies. An established technology giant is willing to spend billions to strengthen its position. It may also make software look more important to the industry's future. A powerful quantum processor is not enough by itself; customers need reliable tools, accessible programming and applications that solve real problems.

Still, one acquisition does not erase the sector's central challenge. Today's quantum systems remain difficult to scale, and practical advantages over classical computers are limited to specific tasks. A headline-grabbing price tag is not proof that widespread commercial adoption is around the corner. Nor does Intel buying Classiq automatically lift competitors: Each company has a different technology, product roadmap, funding position and path to revenue.

So, will this deal reignite quantum stocks? It could spark renewed attention and help put a floor under sentiment, especially if other large companies respond with investments of their own. But a lasting recovery will likely require more than deal headlines. Investors will want evidence of customer demand, better systems, growing revenue and milestones delivered on schedule.

For now, Intel has added a powerful vote of confidence to quantum computing. Whether Wall Street follows will depend on what comes next: not only what the technology might do someday, but what companies can prove it can do today.

news.Title: Stock market today: Dow wavers, S&P 500 and Nasdaq climb ahead of Fed decision, Big Tech earnings
news.Content: US stocks were mixed ahead of a critical day for markets, with a Fed decision and earnings results from Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Alphabet ( GOOG ) on deck. Sentiment in the tech trade has markedly improved this week, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posting back-to-back gains. Semiconductor stocks drove the rally on Tuesday after Broadcom's CEO negotiated for a consortium of banks to announce a $63 billion financing structure for building AI compute capacity. They continued to gain Wednesday after South Korean memory chipmaker SK Hynix ( SKHY , 000660.KS ) reported that profits grew 632% year over year. Micron ( MU ), Samsung ( 005930.KS ), and other chipmaker stocks also rose. Attention now turns toward the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision at 2 p.m. ET, where the Fed is expected to hold rates steady despite elevated inflation readings. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh's press conference will be closely watched for any signs of a hawkish bias. ( Follow live updates from the meeting .) Earnings season continues apace as two Big Tech giants and cloud leaders — Microsoft and Alphabet — deliver updates on AI demand and their capex plans after the bell. Microsoft's report comes just after it offered buyouts to up to 60,000 employees as it tries to streamline operations amid the AI build-out. Rounding out the earnings picture are Ford ( F ), GE Vernova ( GEV ), T-Mobile US ( TMUS ), eBay ( EBAY ), Chipotle Mexican Grill ( CMG ), and ServiceNow ( NOW ). The company warned in its third-quarter regulatory filing that the expansion creates "greater reputational risk" as the technology reaches more investors. In an interview last month, Robinhood said customers are responsible for trades executed by their agents. But the company now acknowledges that courts or regulators might not uphold its customer agreements that assign responsibility to its customers. The new warnings were added in the risk factor section of the company's 10-Q filing. news.Title: Not Nvidia. Not Micron. This Underappreciated AI Stock Could Be 2027's Biggest Winner.
news.Content:
Nvidia and Micron Technology have benefited big time from the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom, driven by their mission-critical chips that play a central role in handling training and inference workloads in data centers.

Both companies have been growing at a solid pace and, importantly, can sustain their healthy growth momentum in 2027. However, there is another AI stock that I think could outperform Nvidia and Micron in 2027.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Western Digital (NASDAQ: WDC) is an important player in the AI infrastructure ecosystem, manufacturing data storage devices that are deployed by hyperscalers and enterprises. Shares of the company have jumped by 103% in 2026, though the past few months have been quite rough for shareholders.

Specifically, Western Digital has dropped 49% from the 52-week high it reached on June 18. However, I think this is an opportunity for savvy investors to add a top growth stock to their portfolios. Let's look at the reasons why Western Digital can step on the gas and become a big winner in 2027.

AI-driven storage demand will help Western Digital sustain its terrific momentum

Western Digital released fiscal 2027 first-quarter results (for the three months ended Oct. 2) on Oct. 22. The company's revenue jumped by 55% from the year-ago period to $4.38 billion. Even better, its non-GAAP gross margin increased to 58.1% from 43.9% in the year-ago quarter. This impressive expansion in Western Digital's margins led to a 161% year-over-year increase in the company's non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) to $4.64.

Western Digital's numbers exceeded expectations. What's more, the company anticipates a stronger jump of 69% in revenue in the current quarter. Meanwhile, non-GAAP gross margin is poised to jump to a range of 60% to 61%, well above the year-ago period's reading of 46.1%. As a result, Western Digital expects adjusted EPS to jump to $5.80 from $2.13 in the year-ago period.

The healthy demand for data storage in AI data centers is behind this phenomenal growth. The company gets 88% of its revenue from the cloud segment, and the good part is that this segment is on track to continue growing at a robust pace over the long run. Western Digital estimates that the AI and cloud storage market will grow at a 25% compound annual growth rate (CAGR) through 2030.

Story Continues

The company also points out that 80% of cloud storage happens on hard disk drives (HDDs). An important point to note is that the AI-driven data storage boom has created a shortage of high-capacity HDDs. Western Digital's rival Seagate Technology notes that it has sold out its 2028 capacity already. Similarly, Western Digital has already received commitments for most of its 2027 capacity, and it is receiving orders for 2028 and 2029.

What's more, Western Digital's customer base is still expanding. The company will start shipping its first-generation heat-assisted magnetic recording (HAMR) high-capacity HDD to two hyperscale customers in the first half of next year. It anticipates adding two more customers for its HAMR solution in the first half of 2027.

So, Western Digital is poised to enjoy healthy demand next year, while the accompanying supply shortage should ensure further margin improvements. So, it is easy to see why analysts have become bullish about Western Digital's long-term earnings growth prospects. In fact, as the chart below shows, its EPS growth could outpace that of both Nvidia and Micron.

YCharts

The valuation makes Western Digital a solid buy

Western Digital trades at an incredibly attractive valuation. It is significantly cheaper than Nvidia and carries only a slight premium to Micron.

Also, Western Digital's 12-month median price target of $625 implies a 64% jump from current levels. That's higher than the implied upside of 47% for Nvidia, and slightly lower than the 70% upside expected in Micron, based on their 12-month median price targets. I won't be surprised to see Western Digital outperform Nvidia and Micron next year, given its exponential growth, solid prospects, and attractive valuation.

So, investors looking to buy a top stock trading at an attractive valuation can consider buying Western Digital right away before it starts soaring once again.

news.Title: Alphabet stock rises as OpenAI plans to buy Google’s TPUs

The TPU deal adds to a growing pattern of hyperscalers and AI labs diversifying away from a single chip architecture, though Nvidia's scale advantage remains substantial.

Apple is best known for the iPhone and the Apple ecosystem, which brings together advanced technology, data management, and artificial intelligence. Now, the tech giant is starting a fresh chapter under CEO John Ternus, who recently succeeded Tim Cook. Apple also just unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, which kills two birds with one stone: it opens more room for innovation and answers users looking for something new. On top of that, the company rolled out a more capable Siri, built in collaboration with Google's Gemini technology. That partnership puts the spotlight on Alphabet.

Alphabet's Bigger AI Ambitions Go Beyond Siri

Alphabet is already bringing AI into Google Search and YouTube, while Google Cloud offers another way to bring it to businesses. That is exactly the goal of the new Gemini agent, an AI tool designed to work across business applications and systems. This could open another growth opportunity for Alphabet. Meanwhile, Apple is investing in its existing product lines, while Alphabet is spending heavily on AI infrastructure to meet growing power demands. But how do these different approaches show up in the financials?

Apple vs. Alphabet: Growth, Earnings, and Valuation Compared

Financials tell the objective story, so I used Barchart's Stock Comparison Tool to see how the two stack up:

Apple is the bigger company, with a market cap of $5.02 trillion versus Alphabet's $3.87 trillion. But Alphabet's latest quarterly sales grew 24.2% year over year to $119.8 billion, outpacing Apple's 16.4% increase to $109.4 billion. Alphabet's lead holds over the long term too, with sales up 120.7% over the past five years, more than double Apple's 51.6%.

Story Continues

Net income looks similar at first glance. Apple's rose 27.1% year over year to $29.8 billion, while Alphabet's jumped 297.9% to $112.2 billion. That huge gap is driven largely by roughly $98 billion in investment gains, so it overstates Alphabet's underlying earnings power.

Valuation tips the scales further in Alphabet's favor. Its stock trades at 15.55x forward earnings, well below Apple's 36.23x. The same goes for price-to-cash-flow, where Alphabet trades at 25.27x compared with Apple's 41.53x, making it the cheaper stock on both counts. So Alphabet is winning the scorecard, but one more metric could turn the tables for Apple: dividends.

Which Pays More Dividends: Apple or Alphabet?

Neither company is particularly known for dividends, but here is what each offers. Apple pays a forward annual dividend of $1.08 per share, for a yield of about 0.31%. Its payout ratio is about 12.4%, meaning only about a tenth of earnings go to dividends. Meanwhile, Alphabet pays $0.88 annually, for a yield of roughly 0.27%. Its payout ratio is even lower, around 4.4%, though that figure is skewed by unusually large investment gains. With the income picture this thin on both sides, the analyst view matters more. So how does Wall Street see the two stocks from here?

How Wall Street Rates Apple and Alphabet Stock Today

A consensus of 40 analysts rates Apple a "Moderate Buy," with high target prices suggesting about 15% upside over the next year.

Wall Street is clearly more bullish on Alphabet, though, with 53 analysts rating it a "Strong Buy." Its high target prices imply about 61% upside if achieved. With the numbers and analyst views in hand, which stock deserves the nod?

Verdict: Why Alphabet Edges Out Apple for Investors

Apple and Alphabet are two of the world's biggest companies and could easily survive the next 20, or even 50, years. Both are benefiting from the AI boom, so the question is which offers better rewards. For now, Alphabet is more convincing, with stronger growth, a cheaper valuation, and a massive AI footprint. Apple looks better on yield, but the gap isn't wide enough to make a strong case for it as the better investment, especially after Alphabet's recent performance. Plus, Apple's higher valuation makes it harder to pick today.

By investor type, Alphabet fits growth-minded investors who want AI exposure at a more reasonable price, while Apple suits those who prefer a steadier, more established name and are willing to pay a premium for it. Neither is an income play, but for investors weighing technology against shareholder value, Alphabet has the stronger case.
