news.Title: FFIV Q4 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Systems Growth
news.Content:
F5, Inc. FFIV reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results. Non-GAAP earnings of $4.42 per share increased 0.7% year over year and surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.3%.

Revenues rose 13% year over year to $917 million, beating the consensus mark by 3.7%. Results benefited from robust systems demand, software expansion and hybrid multicloud adoption. Product revenues advanced 23%, marking the ninth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth.

FFIV's Q4 Revenue Details

Product revenues, representing 56% of total revenues, increased 23% year over year to $510 million. Systems revenues jumped 29% to $239 million, driven by infrastructure refreshes, capacity expansion, competitive displacements and investments in digital sovereignty and AI readiness.

Software revenues rose 19% to $271 million. Subscription-based software revenues increased 16% to $229 million, representing 85% of software revenues. Perpetual license revenues climbed 37% to $42 million. Services revenues, accounting for 44% of total revenues, grew 3% to $408 million.

F5, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

F5, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | F5, Inc. Quote

Recurring revenue sources contributed 68% of quarterly revenues. Geographically, EMEA led growth with a 31% increase, representing 30% of total revenue. APAC revenues rose 14%, contributing 17%, while Americas revenues increased 5%, accounting for 53%.

F5 Benefits From Hybrid Multicloud and AI Demand

Management highlighted sustained demand from hybrid multicloud adoption, application security modernization and AI inference workloads. Platform consolidation remained a key opportunity, with 29% of F5's top 1,000 customers adopting three or more product families, up from 22% in fiscal 2025.

During the quarter, a large North American financial institution selected F5 for an eight-figure application delivery and security deployment, displacing four incumbent vendors. An Asian central bank technology authority also selected F5 for a national financial services cloud, replacing two competitors.

AI-related opportunities accelerated. Direct AI use-case bookings exceeded $100 million in fiscal 2026, growing nearly 300% year over year. The customer base for these solutions expanded fourfold to more than 200, supported by demand for AI data delivery, runtime security and AI factory load balancing.

FFIV Expands Security and Software Opportunities

F5 continued expanding its AI-powered security portfolio as enterprises sought protection against increasingly sophisticated application and API threats. Its AI-powered Distributed Cloud WAF capabilities attracted more than 300 customers since their March launch, with over 75% operating in blocking mode.

Story Continues

The company also gained more than 200 F5 Insight customers since its March launch. The platform provides automated fleet management and upgrade orchestration, helping enterprises reduce operational complexity and accelerate security updates.

For fiscal 2026, software revenues increased 8% to $870 million. SaaS and managed services annualized recurring revenues reached $211 million, up 14% year over year. Core SaaS and managed services ARR grew 24%, while total security-related revenues increased 10% to approximately $1.3 billion.

F5's Operating Margins Face Cost Pressures

Non-GAAP gross margin contracted 30 basis points year over year to 84%. Non-GAAP operating margin declined 330 basis points to 33.7%, reflecting higher operating expenses despite strong revenue growth.

Management attributed higher operating expenses partly to investments in sales capacity, AI security specialists and marketing. Strong year-end performance also increased commission and bonus expenses.

Non-GAAP operating income increased to $309 million from $299 million.

FFIV Maintains Solid Liquidity and Shareholder Returns

F5 generated $118 million in operating cash flow and $91 million in free cash flow during the quarter. Working capital investments, including inventory accumulation and supplier prepayments, affected cash generation as management secured components for future systems demand.

Cash and investments totaled $1.62 billion at quarter-end. The company repurchased $100 million of shares during the quarter, bringing fiscal 2026 repurchases to $600 million. Its board authorized an additional $1.5 billion for share repurchases, supplementing the $322 million remaining under the existing program.

F5 Issues Fiscal 2027 Growth Outlook

For the first quarter of fiscal 2027, F5 expects revenues between $875 million and $895 million. Non-GAAP earnings are projected in the range of $4.25-$4.37 per share. Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 81.5% and 82.5%.

For fiscal 2027, management projects revenue growth of 8-9% and non-GAAP earnings of $18.00-$18.30 per share. The company anticipates upper-single-digit systems growth, double-digit software growth and low-to-mid-single-digit services growth.

Non-GAAP gross margin is expected between 80.5% and 82.5%, suggesting higher component costs. Non-GAAP operating margin is projected at 33-35%. Management expects systems growth to be stronger in the first half, while software growth should accelerate in the second half of fiscal 2027 due to subscription renewal timing.

FFIV's Zacks Rank and Stocks to Consider

Currently, F5 carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

Some better-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector are Analog Devices ADI , Applied Materials AMAT and Cisco Systems CSCO , each carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Shares of Analog Devices have rallied 54.4% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for ADI's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $13.00 per share, up by a penny over the past seven days, indicating an increase of 66.9% year over year.

Shares of Applied Materials have jumped 54.5% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for AMAT's fiscal 2026 earnings is pegged at $12.79 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating a rise of 35.8% year over year.

Cisco Systems shares have surged 45.3% year to date. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for CSCO's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $5.11 per share, unchanged over the past 30 days, indicating an increase of 18% year over year.

news.Title: If You'd Invested $10,000 in Apple Stock 10 Years Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Today
news.Content:
Creating a diversified portfolio of excellent stocks benefits investors in so many ways. One of them is access to a variety of growth opportunities. You only need one stock to really take off, supercharge your portfolio, and make up for any losses.

For some lucky investors, that stock has been Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL). If you'd invested $10,000 in the device powerhouse stock 10 years ago, here's how much money you'd have today.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The most powerful device ecosystem

Apple's premier product is the iPhone, which accounts for about half of its revenue, but it has a large ecosystem of products that draws users and keeps them buying. Loyal fans tend to upgrade, staying in the system and generating more revenue. Sales increased 16% year over year in the 2026 fiscal third quarter (ended June 27).

This has resulted in a powerful business, and for a long time, Apple was the most valuable company in the world. It's been knocked to second place by Nvidia , but it's the only other company worth more than $5 trillion.

Including dividends, Apple stock has gained 1,190% over the past 10 years, more than three times the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC). That means a $10,000 investment is worth more than $128,000 at today's price.

It's unlikely to deliver the same gains over the next 10 years, but it still has robust growth opportunities and can offer value to investors . Apple is an excellent stock to keep in your diversified portfolio that may include the next multibagger stock.

news.Title: Nvidia & AMD Bet $4B on Meta: Grab These ETFs to Own the AI Ecosystem
news.Content:
In a striking consolidation of artificial intelligence (AI) interests, Nvidia NVDA and Advanced Micro Devices AMD have committed to investing a combined $4 billion in Meta Platforms META, with NVDA contributing $3 billion and AMD $1 billion. This capital injection supports Meta's massive $95 billion equity raise aimed at financing its AI infrastructure and "personal superintelligence" ambitions.

Meanwhile, Broadcom AVGO has also expressed its interest in participating in Meta's massive stock offering alongside Nvidia and AMD.

For investors, this presents a compelling opportunity to gain exposure not only to Meta but also to the broader group of technology giants, including Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, which are increasingly interconnected through capital investments and hardware dependencies within the AI ecosystem.

Against this backdrop, rather than betting on a single winner in this complex web, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) with these tech behemoths in their top holdings offer investors a diversified vehicle to capture the collective upside of these billion-dollar investments.

Before identifying specific funds, it is important to understand how these investments could benefit the broader AI industry and why diversified ETF exposure may offer advantages over picking individual stocks, as discussed below.

The Investment Mega Rally in AI Ecosystem

The investment commitments, like those recently made by NVDA and AMD, are not merely financial maneuvers; they are strategic moves to lock in the hardware ecosystem and stave off threats from custom silicon.

By investing in Meta, Nvidia and AMD secure a massive customer for their high-margin AI accelerators. Meta, in turn, secures prioritized access to essential compute power to scale its rapidly growing Muse AI agent, which runs on Nvidia infrastructure and AMD's EPYC processors.

This creates a feedback loop: Meta's AI success drives demand for chips, which funds further chip innovation, benefiting the entire supply chain within the AI ecosystem.

This is, in fact, part of a broader trend in 2026 where tech giants are vertically integrating via capital injection.

Nvidia has aggressively invested in the AI ecosystem, participating in 121 funding rounds this year, a massive jump from just 13 in 2022.

Similarly, AMD recently committed up to $5 billion to Anthropic.

Furthermore, interest from Broadcom, an already established critical custom-chip partner of Meta, in Meta's latest equity offering highlights that the AI infrastructure buildout is a multi-vendor race requiring immense capital.

Story Continues

The Significance of ETF As the Best Possible Strategy

The intricate web of investments mentioned above creates competitive threats within the AI ecosystem, along with financing risks like dilution, making individual stock picking risky.

For instance, Meta's stock fell roughly 1.9% on the very announcement of its $95 billion equity raise, as investors worried about dilution and negative free cash flow — even as AMD jumped over 5% on the same day for its $1 billion investment in Meta in connection to this equity offering. In other words, the same string of events that was a clear win for one company became a near-term drag for another, proving that picking the "right" stock in this ecosystem is far from straightforward.

An ETF approach mitigates this single-company risk while ensuring you own the entire value chain that benefits from this capex supercycle.

NVDA holds the second position with 8.43% weight.

META holds the third spot with 8.34% weight. IGPT has soared 53.6% year to date and charges 57 basis points (bps) in fees. It traded at a volume of 0.06 million shares in the last trading session.

This fund, with assets under management (AUM) worth $1.70 billion, offers exposure to 40 companies involved in the investment theme of AI, generative AI and related technologies. NVDA holds the top spot in this fund, carrying 7.34% weight, while AMD holds the fifth position with 3.82% weight.

This fund, with net assets worth $3.85 billion, includes 50 companies contributing to AI technologies across software, infrastructure and services. AMD holds the top spot in this fund, carrying a 5.59% weight, while NVDA holds the third position with a 4.65% weight.

news.Title: Amazon (AMZN) vs. MSFT and GOOGL: Can Higher-Margin Businesses Turn Amazon Into an AI-Driven Compounder?
news.Content:
Is AMZN a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Amazon.com, Inc. on Quality Stocks | GARP Investment Research's Substack. Since the thesis was published on August 26th, AMZN shares have edged lower amid concerns that heavy AI infrastructure spending could pressure near-term cash flow, creating a short-term headwind while strong AWS growth supports the long-term case. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on AMZN. Amazon.com, Inc.'s share was trading at $253.10 as of October 27th 2026. AMZN's trailing and forward P/E were 20.04 and 23.10 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

This isn't the first time we see a technology company pitched as a great investment. AMZN shares gained 9.90% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Alphabet gained 16.76% during the same period. Why are technology stocks rising, and does AMZN's slower climb leave room for it to catch up?

Gil C / Shutterstock.com

In July, we published an article about the 12 Best Dow Stocks to Invest In Right Now and AMZN ranked 1st in that article. AMZN has gained modestly since then, keeping the bullish call in positive territory but giving investors little to celebrate so far. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on AMZN. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.

Amazon.com, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) operates one of the largest consumer, cloud computing, advertising, and logistics ecosystems in the world. Its investment case increasingly depends on AWS, artificial intelligence infrastructure, advertising, and a shift toward higher-margin businesses rather than traditional e-commerce. Sales growth has been strong and steady, rising 12% in 2024 and an estimated 15% in 2025, with a similar pace expected in 2026 as Amazon.com, Inc. moves toward $1 trillion in annual revenue.

Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential

AWS alone generated $45.6 billion in operating income in 2025, underlining how central cloud computing has become to the company's profits. The stock trades around 21 times earnings at $262 per share, a multiple that rises closer to 30 times once one-time, non-operating gains are stripped out — a reminder that investors are really paying for future AWS growth, AI monetization, and margin improvement rather than today's reported earnings.

The bullish case rests on several growth engines reinforcing one another. Higher-margin segments such as AWS, advertising, third-party seller services, and subscriptions are letting profits grow faster than overall sales. Online retail is still the biggest source of revenue for Amazon.com, Inc., but advertising and third-party services are more profitable, while AWS remains both the company's main earnings driver and its gateway into the AI boom. As more companies increase spending on AI infrastructure, AWS stands to benefit from rising demand for computing power, storage, databases, and AI tools such as Amazon Bedrock, opening up a fresh growth cycle for the business.

Story Continues

The AI ambitions of Amazon.com, Inc. go beyond AWS. The company is also applying artificial intelligence to warehouse automation, logistics, advertising targeting, product recommendations, and tools that help third-party sellers run their businesses more efficiently. AWS's growth rate has accelerated sharply, from 18% to 35%, a sign that Amazon.com, Inc. remains competitive even as Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud post faster growth of their own. Even so, the company still has to prove that its heavy AI investments will generate strong returns and turn into durable earnings growth ( see whether Amazon's custom AI chips can outpace its capital spending ).

Operating leverage is a key part of the investment case, as Amazon.com, Inc. shifts toward more profitable businesses and becomes more efficient across its operations. Management expects capital spending of around $200 billion in 2026, mostly for AI infrastructure, data centers, and chips — spending large enough to push free cash flow into negative territory. Bulls see this as growth investment rather than routine maintenance spending, but it also means Amazon.com, Inc. needs strong AWS growth and sustained AI demand to justify spending at this scale over the coming years.

The revenue mix of Amazon.com, Inc. is steadily shifting toward higher-value services. Advertising, third-party seller services, subscriptions, and AWS are becoming a larger part of the business relative to lower-margin first-party retail. This shift matters because it lets profits grow faster than revenue as these segments gain a bigger share of the overall mix. Based on this trajectory, expected returns work out to roughly 12.1% annualized, driven by organic growth, expanding margins, and an overall improvement in business quality.

On valuation, the stock already reflects a good deal of optimism. A base-case fair value estimate puts shares of Amazon.com, Inc. around $251, with a bull-case scenario reaching $305 if revenue growth and operating margins come in stronger than expected. At current levels, the stock doesn't look dramatically overvalued, but it also doesn't offer much of a safety cushion, since investors are already paying up for faster AWS growth, AI-driven gains, and improving profitability. If AI spending falls short of expectations, AWS growth slows, or operating leverage disappoints, the premium built into the stock could come under pressure.

The biggest risk to this thesis is that AI demand may stay concentrated among a small number of large customers, even as it requires enormous upfront investment. The $200 billion capital spending plan of Amazon.com, Inc. could pay off handsomely if cloud demand keeps accelerating, but weaker AI adoption, pricing pressure, or slower monetization could leave the company with high infrastructure costs and limited profit growth. Competition across cloud computing, advertising, retail, logistics, and AI — along with regulatory scrutiny — adds further uncertainty to the long-term picture.

Another risk for the stock is disruption to the systems that support AWS and Amazon's wider operations. Customers rely on these services to keep applications, payments, and business processes running, making reliability central to the cloud franchise. Amazon warns that system failures or security incidents can interrupt services, cause data loss, and expose it to liability. A prolonged outage could disrupt customers and require costly remediation. Repeated incidents could also weaken confidence and make businesses more cautious about placing additional workloads on AWS. These pressures could hurt growth and profitability even if demand for AI computing remains strong. In our opinion, Amazon's premium valuation becomes harder to defend if reliability problems undermine its main earnings engine.

Hedge fund positioning shows a strong signal for Amazon.com, Inc. As per our database, 369 hedge fund portfolios held the stock at the end of the second quarter, up from 353 in the previous quarter. This steady rise in institutional ownership suggests hedge funds remained constructive on Amazon.com, Inc.'s AWS growth, AI opportunity, advertising business, and long-term margin expansion potential. By comparison, Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) was held by 273 hedge fund portfolios, down from 282, Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) was held by 195 hedge funds, down from 201, and Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL) was held by 119 hedge funds, up from 115. The rise in ownership of Amazon.com, Inc. and Oracle Corporation, against declines for Microsoft Corporation and Alphabet Inc., points to relatively stronger institutional conviction toward Amazon.com, Inc. during the period, even as funds continue weighing its premium valuation and heavy AI spending against its long-term growth potential.

Short interest data also paints a fairly calm picture for Amazon.com, Inc. relative to its peers. About 0.88% of Amazon.com, Inc.'s float is sold short, slightly higher than Microsoft Corporation at 0.82%, but below Alphabet Inc. at 1.37% and well below Oracle Corporation at 2.60%. This suggests Amazon.com, Inc. is drawing similarly limited skepticism to Microsoft Corporation, while bearish bets remain less aggressive than those against Alphabet Inc. and Oracle Corporation, even as investors weigh its valuation and capital spending.

Valuation Analysis

AMZN's forward P/E is 23.10x. Microsoft Corporation, Oracle Corporation, and Alphabet Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 26.88x, 15.54x, and 20.24x, respectively. AMZN's own forward P/E was 22.96x on December 31, 2025, making its current valuation approximately 0.6% higher. We believe the current valuation reflects expectations for AWS growth, advertising expansion, and improving margins, balanced against concerns about heavy AI spending and uncertain investment returns. However, the valuation appears reasonable rather than deeply discounted, as Amazon trades below Microsoft but above Oracle and Alphabet. AWS generated $45.6 billion in operating income in 2025, while Amazon's approximately $200 billion capital spending plan for 2026 underscores how much future growth depends on earning adequate returns from new infrastructure. We believe AMZN can justify its current valuation if higher-margin businesses sustain earnings growth while absorbing rising depreciation and financing costs. If Amazon maintains its cloud momentum and successfully turns AI investment into lasting profits and cash flow, the current valuation could offer a reasonable entry point despite the risks surrounding its infrastructure expansion.

Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN) by FluentInQuality in May 2025, which highlighted AWS growth, logistics infrastructure, Prime ecosystem, advertising strength, and Amazon's five interconnected category leaders. news.Title: NXPI Q3 Earnings Call Highlights SDV and Data Center Growth
news.Content:
NXP Semiconductors N.V. NXPI emphasized software-defined vehicles (SDVs), industrial artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure as key growth drivers during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call.

The company exceeded the Zacks Consensus Estimate for both earnings and revenues. Management also outlined expectations for double-digit revenue growth in 2027, margin expansion and accelerated shareholder returns while addressing supply constraints and pricing trends.

NXP Beat Q3 Earnings and Revenue Estimates

NXPI reported third-quarter non-GAAP earnings of $4.20 per share, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $4.14 by $0.06. Earnings increased 35% year over year from $3.11.

Revenues totaled $3.79 billion, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.77 billion. The top line increased 19% year over year and 8% sequentially.

NXP Semiconductors N.V. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

NXP Semiconductors N.V. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | NXP Semiconductors N.V. Quote

CFO Bill Betz attributed the improvement to higher factory utilization and operating leverage. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 58.6%, while operating margin expanded to 37.1%.

NXPI Targets Higher Automotive Content Through SDVs

President and CEO Rafael Sotomayor highlighted the accelerating adoption of zonal and centralized computing architectures, which provide two to three times greater semiconductor content per vehicle.

Automotive revenues reached $2.07 billion, increasing 13% year over year. The SDV business exceeded a $1.5 billion annualized revenue run rate, supporting its $2 billion target for 2027.

Sotomayor highlighted RV Tech's decision to standardize its zonal platform on NXP's S32K5 processor. Initial shipments into China are expected in early 2027, with broader production ramps anticipated in 2028.

NXP Expands Its Data Center Revenue Ambitions

Sotomayor raised expectations for NXP's data center business, projecting revenues above $500 million in 2026 and exceeding $1 billion by 2028.

Responding to questions from Bank of America Securities, he explained that NXP focuses on control-plane processors, networking and security rather than discrete power components.

Management emphasized that growth depends on product introductions, customer design wins and software deployments, positioning data centers as another source of revenue diversification.

NXPI Sees Industrial AI Adoption Accelerating

Industrial & IoT revenues increased 39% year over year to $802 million, supported by factory automation, health care and data center demand.

Story Continues

Sotomayor expects AI-enabled processors to account for approximately 15% of Industrial & IoT processor revenues in 2026, more than doubling their contribution from 2025.

NXP also secured its first S32K5 design win in humanoid robotics. Its Ara discrete neural processing unit continues to attract customer interest, with volume production expected in 2028.

NXP Addresses Supply Tightness and Inventory Trends

During the Goldman Sachs discussion, Sotomayor said widespread automotive customer restocking had not materialized despite improving demand visibility.

Betz subsequently told JPMorgan that book-to-bill remained well above one across all end markets and regions. Approximately 80% of lead times exceeded 16 weeks compared with 25% a year earlier.

Addressing questions from UBS, Betz identified tight back-end manufacturing capacity and potential front-end constraints in 2027. Planned capacity investments are intended to support additional demand.

NXPI Outlines Margin Expansion and 2027 Growth

For the fourth quarter, management guided revenues to $3.75-$3.95 billion and non-GAAP earnings between $4.14 per share and $4.58 per share.

Betz expects non-GAAP gross margin of 59% at the midpoint, supported by improved utilization. Management targets a 60% gross margin during 2027 and further expansion in 2028.

During the Barclays discussion, Betz attributed margin improvements primarily to operational efficiencies rather than price increases. For 2027, management anticipates double-digit revenue growth and capital expenditures around 5% of revenues.

NXP Prioritizes Cash Generation and Shareholder Returns

Third-quarter free cash flow reached $1.21 billion, representing approximately 32% of revenues and supporting manufacturing investments and shareholder distributions.

The board authorized an additional $5 billion in repurchases, bringing the total authorization to approximately $6.3 billion. Betz expects buybacks to accelerate during the fourth quarter and throughout 2027.

Management's priorities remain executing product ramps, expanding manufacturing capacity and improving profitability while returning excess free cash flow to shareholders.

What NXPI's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

NXPI currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), indicating favorable near-term prospects based on earnings estimate revisions. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Its Value Score of C indicates average valuation characteristics, while Growth, Momentum and VGM Score of D reflect less favorable positioning across these investment styles.

The combination indicates that NXPI's positive Zacks Rank is not reinforced by strong Style Scores, which generally favor A- or B-rated stocks alongside top Zacks Ranks. The Zacks Rank can change as analysts revise earnings estimates following the latest quarterly results.

news.Title: Is Zuckerberg pulling the rug out from under Anthropic?
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Meta Platforms is making an extraordinarily expensive push into artificial intelligence, and the timing could hardly be more challenging for Anthropic.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

Just as the Claude developer prepares for what it hopes could be the largest initial public offering ever, Mark Zuckerberg's company is raising as much as $97.5 billion to accelerate its own AI ambitions.

The collision comes at a particularly sensitive moment: Anthropic's newly released IPO prospectus reveals explosive revenue growth and improving profitability, but also enormous future spending commitments that make continued access to capital essential.

Meanwhile, Meta's newest AI models are beginning to rival Claude on important performance benchmarks, often at significantly lower prices.

The central question for potential IPO investors is no longer who has the smartest and fastest-growing AI, but whether Anthropic can build a sustainable technological and economic lead against a rival with vastly greater financial resources, an established global distribution network and a willingness to spend and price dump aggressively.

Anthropic's extraordinary growth comes with an extraordinary price tag

Anthropic's financial disclosures offer one of the clearest pictures yet of the economics behind the AI boom: according to its IPO prospectus, the company generated $16.29 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, compared with just $1.16 billion a year earlier.

More importantly, its operating loss narrowed to $693 million, while adjusted operating income turned positive at $1.62 billion. That is meaningful progress for a company spending billions to develop frontier AI models.

The headline net loss of $80.7 billion looks considerably worse, although roughly $72.4 billion reflects a noncash accounting charge related to the rising value of convertible financing instruments rather than money lost through everyday operations.

Still, the real challenge lies ahead.

Anthropic has entered over $600 billion in compute and infrastructure agreements stretching over the coming years. Those are not all immediately payable, and some are contingent on capacity delivery, but they illustrate the extraordinary scale of future investment.

Amazon and Alphabet are central to that strategy, providing both capital and access to computing infrastructure - and while the backing gives Anthropic substantial resources, it also leaves the company dependent on continued growth, infrastructure availability and the willingness of investors and partners to keep the capital flowing.

Story Continues

Zuckerberg's $97.5 billion challenge

Meta on October 27 expanded its massive equity financing initiative to $97.5 billion, including $25 billion in common stock priced at $625 per share and $12.5 billion in preferred securities.

A further at-the-market offering of up to $60 billion is planned following the expected launch of Meta's nonvoting Class C shares in early 2027.

Chipmakers Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom have also expressed interest in participating in the financing, underscoring how closely interconnected the industry's capital and infrastructure investments have become.

The result is an unusually direct competition for investor capital.

Anthropic is preparing to ask institutional investors to assign an enormous valuation to a rapidly growing but still capital-intensive AI developer. At virtually the same time, Meta is offering investors exposure to an established technology giant pouring billions into its own AI expansion.

Meta's spending is not without consequences: the company reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive cash flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier, while raising its full-year capital expenditure forecast to between $135 billion and $145 billion.

But Zuckerberg has one advantage Anthropic cannot easily replicate: Meta's established advertising business generates substantial revenue and cash flow that can help fund continued AI development.

For Anthropic, raising capital remains central to building its business. For Meta, AI investment can also be supported by an enormous business that already exists.

Meta's most dangerous weapon may be its pricing

Money alone does not guarantee technological superiority, but Meta is increasingly demonstrating that it may not need the best AI to become a formidable competitor.

Anthropic's Claude models remain among the industry's leaders in advanced reasoning, coding and enterprise applications. Yet independent benchmarks published in October show Meta's Muse models closing the gap across several important categories.

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Muse Wonder Full scored 56, matching Claude Sonnet 5.5 and trailing Claude Opus 5.5's score of 58.

Claude retained a meaningful advantage on the ProgramBench coding evaluation, while Meta's model outperformed it on the longer-duration SWE-Marathon test.

The results are mixed, but the broader implication is difficult to ignore: Meta is already delivering competitive AI capabilities without consistently matching Anthropic's most advanced models.

And it is doing so at substantially lower published prices.

Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 costs $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens, compared with $4 and $20, respectively, for Claude Opus 5.5.

The models are not directly equivalent in capability, and the total cost of completing a task can differ from their per-token pricing. Nonetheless, Meta is establishing itself as an aggressive lower-cost alternative.

For enterprise customers, this could become increasingly difficult to ignore.

A business using AI to process hunderds of thousands of customer inquiries, analyze documents or perform routine coding tasks may find that a slightly less capable model is more than sufficient, particularly when the cost difference becomes substantial at scale.

The threat to Anthropic is therefore not theoretical: as competing models become capable enough to handle more commercial workloads, the number of applications in which Claude can command a meaningful premium could begin to shrink.

And for a company seeking a valuation of $1.5 trillion or more, simply hoping to remain a little better than everyone else is a questionable long-term strategy.

Is Meta actually cheaper, or just willing to lose money?

There is, however, an important distinction between offering AI at a lower price and actually producing it more efficiently.

Meta has not publicly disclosed sufficiently detailed unit economics for its Muse models to establish whether its aggressive pricing reflects a durable cost advantage or just its willingness to sacrifice profitability to gain market share.

There are reasons to believe its technology is becoming more efficient. Meta has emphasized improvements in model architecture, inference optimization and utilization of computing infrastructure.

Zuckerberg also said during Meta's latest earnings call that the company expects to improve Muse's compute cost efficiency by more than tenfold over the next year.

But those are projections, not proof that Muse is already cheaper to operate than Claude - Zuckerberg openly has acknowledged that Muse remains unprofitable and requires enormous resources to operate and improve.

Independent benchmarks also suggest the pricing comparison is more complicated than it first appears: although Muse Spark's per-token prices are considerably lower, some evaluations show that it consumes significantly more tokens to complete comparable tasks. That can narrow or even eliminate the cost advantage on an individual assignment.

In other words, Meta may be selling AI more cheaply without necessarily producing each successful result more cheaply.

Yet that distinction offers Anthropic only limited comfort.

Even if Meta is effectively subsidizing AI usage, it has the financial resources to sustain aggressive pricing for a considerable period - in the third quarter alone, Meta generated $32.79 billion in operating cash flow, supported overwhelmingly by its established advertising operations.

That cash flow is under pressure from enormous infrastructure spending, and Meta is itself turning to equity markets for additional capital, but, unlike Anthropic, it does not need its AI products to generate sufficient revenue to support the entire business.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Zuckerberg can also justify AI investment through benefits that do not appear directly in Muse's revenue, including improved advertising performance, user engagement and commerce.

For Anthropic, the economics are considerably less forgiving. Selling access to AI is its central business, and continued investment in increasingly expensive infrastructure depends on making that business financially sustainable.

Even if Meta's pricing strategy proves unprofitable in the near term, Anthropic still faces the challenge of competing against a company that can potentially absorb those losses for longer.

The bull case: Anthropic can fight back, but not on technology alone

None of this means Anthropic is destined to lose.

In fact, its IPO disclosures provide considerable evidence that it has already built a viable commercial foundation: revenue is seeing extraordinary growth, operating losses have narrowed substantially, and adjusted operating income has turned positive.

Those improvements suggest Anthropic is learning to convert technical capabilities into a more efficient business, rather than simply spending ever larger amounts to produce better models.

Sustaining that progress, however, will require more than defending Claude's position at the top of AI leaderboards.

One potential response is to compete on efficiency itself.

Anthropic can reduce inference costs through improved model architectures, more efficient use of computing capacity and increasingly capable smaller models. It can also lower prices where necessary while reserving premium pricing for workloads that genuinely require its most advanced technology.

This is particularly important because a technological lead is not automatically an economic moat. If achieving slightly better benchmark results requires substantially more spending, that lead may eventually become too expensive to maintain.

Another opportunity lies in moving beyond selling access to models.

Anthropic's growing enterprise relationships, development tools and integration into corporate workflows offer potential ways to make Claude more valuable than the underlying technology alone.

A business that has embedded Claude into its software development processes, internal systems and employee workflows may be less inclined to switch providers simply because another model is cheaper.

That would allow Anthropic to compete increasingly on the value of its broader ecosystem rather than the price of individual tokens.

Its partnerships with Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud also provide access to enterprise distribution channels and substantial infrastructure resources.

And while these arrangements create dependencies, they give Anthropic a path to scale without building every part of its commercial ecosystem independently.

The strongest bullish scenario is therefore not one in which Claude remains the world's most capable model indefinitely, but one in which Anthropic uses its technological position and early commercial success to build a business that customers find difficult to replace, while steadily bringing down the cost of delivering its technology.

The bear case: Meta can afford a longer price war

The more troubling scenario is one in which Meta continues narrowing the performance gap while maintaining its substantially lower prices.

At that point, Anthropic may face an increasingly uncomfortable choice: protect margins and risk losing customers, or match competitors' prices and sacrifice profitability.

Neither option is particularly attractive for a company with hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure agreements and substantial future financing requirements.

There is also a potentially damaging feedback loop: if Anthropic lowers prices to remain competitive, it may need to sell significantly more AI usage to generate the same revenue. That additional demand could require greater computing capacity, particularly if efficiency improvements fail to keep pace with price reductions, resulting in a business growing rapidly in usage but struggling to translate that growth into sustainable profits.

Meta, meanwhile, could continue using its advertising cash flow to support AI investment, even if its models take longer to become profitable.

That does not make the company immune to financial pressure: its own CapEx have grown enormously, free cash flow has turned negative, and shareholders are already questioning the scale of Zuckerberg's spending.

But Meta has considerably more flexibility in how it monetizes AI and how long it can tolerate weak direct returns.

Its distribution network compounds that advantage. Zuckerberg said during the company's latest earnings call that Meta serves approximately 500 million businesses across its platforms, providing a potentially enormous cross- and upselling opportunity.

For Anthropic, the risk is that AI capabilities become increasingly interchangeable before it has established enough customer loyalty, proprietary workflows and cost advantages to defend its business.

And if Meta can produce comparable models at genuinely lower costs, rather than merely subsidizing prices, the challenge becomes more serious still.

The IPO adds another layer of pressure

Anthropic's planned Nasdaq debut, expected before Thanksgiving under the ticker ANT, could raise as much as $100 billion and value the business between $1.5 trillion and $2 trillion.

But valuation expectations have already become less certain as investors reassess the industry's spending requirements and competitive outlook, making Meta's financing particularly significant.

The companies are not necessarily seeking capital from identical investors, and Meta's proposed $60 billion at-the-market program would be spread over time rather than raised in a single offering.

Nevertheless, both are asking financial markets to fund enormous AI ambitions at a time when investors are becoming increasingly selective.

For Anthropic, the stakes extend far beyond the success of a single listing: the company's long-term ability to compete will depend not just on generating revenue, but on raising enough capital at attractive terms to fund infrastructure, development and expansion.

A successful IPO would strengthen its balance sheet and provide additional financial flexibility.

But even a strong debut would not resolve the fundamental challenge of competing against a rival that can fund AI investment through a much larger, established business.

A disappointing valuation, meanwhile, could make future financing significantly more expensive, particularly if investors begin questioning whether Anthropic can defend its tech lead and pricing power.

That makes the IPO an unusually important test of whether financial markets believe an independent AI developer can sustain its position against the world's largest technology companies.

Bottom line: Anthropic needs more than the best AI

Anthropic has already demonstrated that it can build world-class AI technology and turn it into a rapidly growing commercial business. Its improving operating results suggest the company is much more than an expensive research experiment.

But Meta is challenging the assumption that superior AI technology necessarily translates into durable pricing power, and Zuckerberg is ready to deploy his empire's full financial resources to narrow the gap.

Whether Muse's low prices reflect genuine efficiency gains or deliberate margin sacrifices remains unclear, but one thing is certain: Meta has the resources, distribution and existing cash-generating businesses to sustain aggressive competition.

Anthropic can counter that challenge through better economics, stronger enterprise relationships and products that customers value beyond their underlying models, but it cannot just rely on remaining slightly ahead on benchmarks and charging substantially more.

For a company seeking a valuation of as high as $2 trillion and facing extraordinary future infrastructure commitments, technological superiority alone is unlikely to be enough.

The IPO will provide an early verdict.

news.Title: Earnings Preview: Cirrus Logic (CRUS) Q2 Earnings Expected to Decline
news.Content:
Wall Street expects a year-over-year decline in earnings on lower revenues when Cirrus Logic (CRUS) reports results for the quarter ended September 2026. While this widely-known consensus outlook is important in gauging the company's earnings picture, a powerful factor that could impact its near-term stock price is how the actual results compare to these estimates.

The earnings report, which is expected to be released on November 4, might help the stock move higher if these key numbers are better than expectations. On the other hand, if they miss, the stock may move lower.

While the sustainability of the immediate price change and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's discussion of business conditions on the earnings call, it's worth handicapping the probability of a positive EPS surprise.

Zacks Consensus Estimate

This chipmaker is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.44 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of -13.8%.

Revenues are expected to be $540.56 million, down 3.6% from the year-ago quarter.

Estimate Revisions Trend

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has been revised 5.6% lower over the last 30 days to the current level. This is essentially a reflection of how the covering analysts have collectively reassessed their initial estimates over this period.

Investors should keep in mind that an aggregate change may not always reflect the direction of estimate revisions by each of the covering analysts.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Earnings Whisper

Estimate revisions ahead of a company's earnings release offer clues to the business conditions for the period whose results are coming out. Our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction) -- has this insight at its core.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Thus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate. However, the model's predictive power is significant for positive ESP readings only.

A positive Earnings ESP is a strong predictor of an earnings beat, particularly when combined with a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), 2 (Buy) or 3 (Hold). Our research shows that stocks with this combination produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time, and a solid Zacks Rank actually increases the predictive power of Earnings ESP.

Story Continues

Please note that a negative Earnings ESP reading is not indicative of an earnings miss. Our research shows that it is difficult to predict an earnings beat with any degree of confidence for stocks with negative Earnings ESP readings and/or Zacks Rank of 4 (Sell) or 5 (Strong Sell).

How Have the Numbers Shaped Up for Cirrus Logic?

For Cirrus Logic, the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, suggesting that analysts have recently become bearish on the company's earnings prospects. This has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.82%.

On the other hand, the stock currently carries a Zacks Rank of #5.

So, this combination makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Cirrus Logic will beat the consensus EPS estimate.

Does Earnings Surprise History Hold Any Clue?

While calculating estimates for a company's future earnings, analysts often consider to what extent it has been able to match past consensus estimates. So, it's worth taking a look at the surprise history for gauging its influence on the upcoming number.

For the last reported quarter, it was expected that Cirrus Logic would post earnings of $1.8 per share when it actually produced earnings of $1.84, delivering a surprise of +2.22%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has beaten consensus EPS estimates four times.

Bottom Line

An earnings beat or miss may not be the sole basis for a stock moving higher or lower. Many stocks end up losing ground despite an earnings beat due to other factors that disappoint investors. Similarly, unforeseen catalysts help a number of stocks gain despite an earnings miss.

That said, betting on stocks that are expected to beat earnings expectations does increase the odds of success. This is why it's worth checking a company's Earnings ESP and Zacks Rank ahead of its quarterly release. Make sure to utilize our Earnings ESP Filter to uncover the best stocks to buy or sell before they've reported.

Cirrus Logic doesn't appear a compelling earnings-beat candidate. However, investors should pay attention to other factors too for betting on this stock or staying away from it ahead of its earnings release.

Expected Results of an Industry Player

Lattice Semiconductor (LSCC), another stock in the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, is expected to report earnings per share of $0.55 for the quarter ended September 2026. This estimate points to a year-over-year change of +96.4%. Revenues for the quarter are expected to be $255.13 million, up 91.3% from the year-ago quarter.

The consensus EPS estimate for Lattice has been revised 5.4% higher over the last 30 days to the current level. However, a lower Most Accurate Estimate has resulted in an Earnings ESP of -0.60%.

When combined with a Zacks Rank of #1 (Strong Buy), this Earnings ESP makes it difficult to conclusively predict that Lattice will beat the consensus EPS estimate. Over the last four quarters, the company surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times.

news.Title: TSLA Q3 Earnings Call Highlights Autonomy and Expansion Plans
news.Content:
Tesla, Inc. TSLA emphasized accelerating autonomous driving adoption, expanding Robotaxi operations and scaling manufacturing capacity during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management positioned these initiatives as central to future growth while acknowledging substantial investment requirements.

The discussion highlighted strengthening vehicle demand, emerging robotics opportunities and rising infrastructure spending, with executives outlining commercialization milestones and operational constraints.

Tesla reported third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings of 48 cents per share, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 45 cents. Revenues totaled $28.05 billion, exceeding the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $27.78 billion. Adjusted earnings declined 4% year over year, while revenues remained relatively flat.

Tesla, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Tesla, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Tesla, Inc. Quote

TSLA Sees FSD Adoption Driving Vehicle Demand

CEO Elon Musk identified Full Self-Driving (FSD) as a major driver of vehicle demand, stating that customer interest was exceeding production capacity. Tesla ended the quarter with its largest passenger vehicle backlog in four years.

Chief financial officer Vaibhav Taneja stated that more than 75% of North American deliveries included paid FSD sign-ups. Active FSD customers exceeded 1.7 million globally, with subscriptions accounting for half.

During questions from RBC Capital Markets, executives defended Tesla's competitive positioning in autonomous driving. Taneja emphasized technical differentiation while acknowledging ongoing efforts to secure broader regulatory approval in China.

Tesla Targets Wider Robotaxi Deployment

Tesla expanded its Robotaxi service by introducing Cybercabs in Austin during September. Cumulative unsupervised miles increased eightfold sequentially, approaching 2 million by quarter-end.

Executive officer Ashok Elluswamy outlined plans to launch Cybercab operations in Dallas in November. He also described efforts to expand operating hours, improve software capabilities and accommodate additional driving conditions.

Responding to Wolfe Research, Musk said Robotaxi operations could become financially noticeable during the second quarter of 2027 and more significant later that year. Taneja acknowledged that operating costs remain above Tesla's targeted 30 cents per mile, emphasizing utilization improvements and fleet expansion.

TSLA Advances Energy Storage Amid Strong Demand

Musk indicated that Tesla's Megapack production capacity for 2027 was nearly sold out, reflecting substantial demand from data centers and energy infrastructure customers.

Story Continues

Taneja reported energy storage deployments of 13.7 gigawatt-hours, while segment gross margin improved sequentially from 20.4% to 33.1%. Tariff refunds and warranty adjustments contributed to the margin improvement.

Tesla began production at Megafactory Texas, which has planned annual capacity of 50 gigawatt-hours. Management expects higher selling prices and additional margin improvements as production expands to address demand.

Tesla Outlines Optimus Commercialization Timeline

Musk confirmed that early Optimus production had begun at Fremont, although several engineering challenges remain unresolved. He highlighted robot dexterity, reliability and artificial intelligence capabilities as critical development priorities.

Management expects initial deliveries to external commercial customers toward the end of 2027, with industrial applications prioritized. Integrating Tesla's AI5 chip represents another important development milestone.Responding to Deutsche Bank, Musk identified robotic hands as particularly challenging. Executive Konstantinos Laskaris explained that mechanical complexity and component durability remain areas requiring refinement before commercial scaling.

TSLA Plans Heavy Investment in Manufacturing

Tesla's 2026 capital expenditure outlook was revised to approximately $20 billion. The company also secured borrowing capacity of up to $30 billion to support future investment, without planning withdrawals during 2026.

Management expects spending to increase over subsequent years as Tesla develops semiconductor manufacturing, robotics facilities, autonomous fleets and computing infrastructure.

During questioning from Deutsche Bank, Musk indicated that the Terafab semiconductor initiative would require tens of billions of dollars through early 2028. He described initial research fabrication milestones in 2027 and targeted meaningful production beginning in late 2028.

Tesla Balances Expansion With Execution Priorities

Management maintained an ambitious outlook for manufacturing expansion, targeting approximately 5 million annual vehicle units by 2030. Battery availability remains a constraint on near-term production growth.

Taneja emphasized that research, development and preproduction expenditures would continue increasing until new products reach commercialization. The company's priorities remain centered on expanding capacity while supporting autonomous driving, robotics and energy businesses.

news.Title: Volkswagen Bets $4B on Audi's U.S. Expansion: What's Ahead?
news.Content:
Volkswagen VWAGY is strengthening its manufacturing and technological capabilities through two strategic initiatives. Its luxury brand Audi plans to invest approximately $4 billion in its first U.S. manufacturing facility in Georgia, while Volkswagen has expanded its partnership with NXP Semiconductors NXPI to advance its software-defined vehicle technology.

These initiatives could help Volkswagen reduce tariff exposure, improve cost efficiency and strengthen its global competitiveness, although significant investments and execution risks remain.

Audi's $4B U.S. Plant to Reduce Tariff Exposure

Audi plans to invest approximately $4 billion in a Georgia manufacturing facility, creating around 4,500 jobs. Construction is scheduled to begin in 2027, with production expected in the early 2030s. The plant will have an annual capacity of up to 200,000 vehicles, manufacturing premium SUVs, including the Q7, Q8 and Q9. Roughly half of the output is expected to be exported.

The investment could strengthen Audi's position in the U.S. premium automotive market, where deliveries remained roughly flat through the first nine months of 2026 after declining 16% in 2025. Local production could improve its competitiveness against BMW and Mercedes-Benz, which already have U.S. manufacturing operations.

Importantly, the facility could reduce tariff-related costs. Audi incurred approximately €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) in tariff expenses in 2025, with all U.S.-bound vehicles imported from Europe or Mexico. With tariffs on German vehicle imports currently at 15%, localized manufacturing could lower import expenses, logistics costs and currency risks.

The plant would also establish North America as Audi's third major production hub alongside Europe and China, improving geographic diversification. However, significant upfront capital expenditures, construction risks and Volkswagen's ongoing European restructuring could pressure near-term cash flows.

NXP Partnership to Improve Volkswagen's Operating Efficiency

Volkswagen has expanded its collaboration with NXP Semiconductors to develop its next-generation software-defined vehicle architecture. NXP's S32K5 microcontrollers will be a common component of the zonal architecture Volkswagen is developing through its joint venture with Rivian Automotive RIVN. The first vehicle featuring the technology is planned for 2027.

The architecture will consolidate multiple vehicle functions into fewer electronic control units, reducing hardware complexity and component requirements. Standardizing this technology across Volkswagen's brands could generate economies of scale, lower development costs and accelerate the introduction of advanced digital features.

Story Continues

What Lies Ahead for Volkswagen?

Volkswagen's initiatives could improve its long-term profitability by addressing high import-related expenses and growing vehicle technology costs. Audi's U.S. expansion may support premium vehicle sales and margins, while semiconductor standardization could deliver group-wide manufacturing and development efficiencies.

Nevertheless, the benefits will materialize gradually, with the new semiconductor architecture expected in 2027 and Audi's U.S. production beginning in the early 2030s. Substantial capital requirements, ongoing restructuring and execution risks could constrain near-term earnings.

news.Title: Lumentum vs. Sandisk: Which Tech Stock Is the Better Buy in November?
news.Content:
As the digital economy expands, choosing the right infrastructure backbone is essential for long-term growth. Should you bet on Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) or Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) for your portfolio?

Lumentum focuses on optical and photonic technologies that power high-speed data centers, while Sandisk specializes in flash-memory solutions for everything from consumer gadgets to massive cloud systems. Both play critical roles in the artificial intelligence build-out, making them top contenders in the hardware space.

The case for Lumentum

Lumentum designs and manufactures optical components that enable high-speed data transmission for cloud infrastructure and telecommunications. The company serves a diverse range of industries, including industrial manufacturing and sensing, but relies heavily on a small group of major customers.

In its latest annual report, the company noted that Customer A accounted for nearly 26.6% of net revenue and Customer B accounted for 15%. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business because the loss of one partner can drastically impact the bottom line.

Financial performance recently showed a massive surge in top-line growth. As of the June-ending fiscal year, trailing 12-month revenue reached $3 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of approximately 83%.

However, despite this growth, the company reported a net loss of nearly $6.9 billion for the period due to a one-time non-operating loss. Operating income, measuring profit before interest and taxes, was $525 million, an improvement over fiscal 2025's $180 million loss.

The balance sheet remains relatively stable despite the reported net loss. As of its June 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, meaning the company has $0.40 of total debt for every dollar of shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover its short-term debts with its short-term assets, is approximately 1.7x.

Fiscal 2026 free cash flow, which is the cash left over after paying for capital investments, was $300 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 22.7% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow. Investors often monitor semiconductor stocks like Lumentum for their role in next-generation networking.

The case for Sandisk

Sandisk operates as a vertically integrated producer of flash-memory and storage technologies. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, cloud service providers, and retailers across the gaming, automotive, and data center markets. Unlike many of its peers, the company maintains a broad customer base, with no single client accounting for more than 10% of net revenue in fiscal year 2026. This diversification helps provide more stable demand and reduces the risk of relying on a handful of large contracts.

Story Continues

The growth trajectory for the storage specialist has been explosive. In fiscal 2026 (ending in July), revenue reached $20 billion, an increase of approximately 175% over the previous fiscal period. This growth translated into substantial profitability, with net income totaling nearly $11.4 billion.

The financial foundation appears very robust based on the July 2026 balance sheet. The debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0x, showing the company carries negligible total debt relative to its equity. Its current ratio is close to 2.3x, which compares a firm's liquid assets to its short-term liabilities.

Free cash flow for the year reached nearly $11.5 billion, representing cash generated after accounting for spending on buildings and equipment. Stock-based compensation was only 2% of cash from operations, meaning reported cash flows are largely derived from actual business transactions.

Risk profile comparison

Lumentum faces significant pressure from global trade dynamics and export control laws. U.S. government restrictions have already ended Huawei's relationship with the U.S., and potential new tariffs could further impact its sales to China.

Sandisk is heavily dependent on its Flash Ventures partnership with Kioxia for its supply of memory wafers. This arrangement requires the company to pay half of the fixed costs regardless of the actual output, creating financial strain if market demand unexpectedly drops. The company also faces stiff competition from industry giants such as Micron Technology , Samsung Electronics , and its former parent Western Digital . Managing manufacturing operations concentrated in Asia also leaves the company vulnerable to regional geopolitical instability or supply chain disruptions.

Valuation comparison

Sandisk appears significantly more attractive on a price basis, sporting a much lower earnings multiple than its peer.

Metric

Lumentum

Sandisk

Forward P/E

P/S ratio

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The P/S ratio measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months. The Forward P/E ratio compares the stock price to its future earnings estimates for the coming year.

Which stock would I buy in 2026?

Sandisk may offer higher upside over the next year, but the challenge is trying to predict what happens if supply catches up to demand in the next three years. As a long-term investor, I would rather buy Lumentum right now. Its forward P/E is higher, but it should deliver steadier earnings growth.

During Citi' s 2026 Global TMF conference in September, Lumentum's President of Global Business Units Wupen Yuen said: "Demand is just absolutely crazy." The company doesn't expect laser supply gaps to close anytime soon.

For Sandisk, soaring prices and margins from flash memory are causing a flood of new capital to go toward meeting supply. But the long-term customer agreements that many suppliers are signing are not enough to cover all revenue if selling prices weaken as supply catches up to demand.

With Sandisk, investors are faced with the double-edged risk of a slowdown in AI data center spending and the negative impact of lower memory prices. Lumentum doesn't face the same degree of pricing risk as Sandisk, which operates in an industry notorious for boom-and-bust cycles, which is why Lumentum stock commands a higher valuation.

Moreover, Lumentum should benefit over the long term as AI models become more complex and advanced. This is expected to shift more spending toward optical interconnects, providing a tailwind for long-term growth. As someone not looking to trade, but to stick with a growth stock that can compound in value over many years, I would rather hold Lumentum.

news.Content:
Semiconductor stocks gained on Wednesday with the PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) rising for a third day in a row.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts See Marvell (MRVL) as a Buy: Should You Invest?
news.Content:
When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Marvell Technology (MRVL) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Marvell currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.38, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 40 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.38 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 40 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 31 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 77.5% and 7.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for MRVL

Check price target & stock forecast for Marvell here>>>

The ABR suggests buying Marvell, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

Analysts employed by brokerage firms have been and continue to be overly optimistic with their recommendations. Since the ratings issued by these analysts are more favorable than their research would support because of the vested interest of their employers, they mislead investors far more often than they guide.

In contrast, the Zacks Rank is driven by earnings estimate revisions. And near-term stock price movements are strongly correlated with trends in earnings estimate revisions, according to empirical research.

Furthermore, the different grades of the Zacks Rank are applied proportionately across all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide earnings estimates for the current year. In other words, at all times, this tool maintains a balance among the five ranks it assigns.

Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a company's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Should You Invest in MRVL?

In terms of earnings estimate revisions for Marvell, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 0.2% over the past month to $4.21.

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

The size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, has resulted in a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) for Marvell. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>>

Therefore, the Buy-equivalent ABR for Marvell may serve as a useful guide for investors.

news.Title: Prediction: $10,000 Invested in Nvidia Will Be Worth This Much by Late 2029 -- If the AI Spending Boom Continues
news.Content:
Nvidia 's (NASDAQ: NVDA) fortunes have been lifted remarkably by the artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. Over the past three years, during a period when data center spending among hyperscalers really kicked into high gear, the company's shares have rocketed 410% higher (as of Oct. 23). Since it produces the most advanced and most popular graphics processing units for AI data centers, it has benefited like no other business has.

This AI stock is trading at around $211 right now. If you buy $10,000 worth of Nvidia shares today, I predict that it will grow remarkably by 2029 -- if the AI spending boom holds up.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The company must deliver strong earnings growth

The consensus estimate of the sell-side analyst community is that Nvidia's earnings per share will increase at a compound annual rate of 65% from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2029. This doesn't look like a stretch. Between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2026, that profitability metric climbed at a yearly clip of 204%. That was certainly the most powerful tailwind driving the stock higher.

If Wall Street's forecast proves correct, then Nvidia's share price should mimic this bottom-line gain. That would turn a $10,000 investment in the chipmaker made today into a position worth $45,000 in three years. A 350% return in 36 months is impossible to complain about.

This premise assumes that the company's valuation multiple doesn't change. Nvidia stock currently trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of 26.7 .

This bull case is definitely within the realm of possibility. Indeed, while it may sound hard to believe, if the stock does rise at 65% annually between now and late 2029, it would result in a slightly lower rate of return than the business posted over the prior three years. However, for that to occur, Nvidia will need the AI industry's momentum to continue.

It all comes down to AI-related spending. While Nvidia can still prosper even if it slows down slightly, it can't decelerate too much. According to a forecast from investment firm Vanguard (itself a giant with $13 trillion in assets under management), the five big hyperscalers, which represent a significant customer cohort for Nvidia, will spend more than $1 trillion on AI capex each year from 2027 through 2030.

Story Continues

The AI spending frenzy may not last

The bear case also shouldn't be ignored, though. The amount of capital flowing through the AI industry, coupled with the speed of model development, is unprecedented. While AI looks like it could be a revolutionary technology, no one has a clue how its adoption will play out, or to what degree those investments will pay off. These innovative capabilities don't mean that the infrastructure providers -- or the hardware giants that support them -- will continue to be winners.

If at some point in the coming years, AI infrastructure spending slows down dramatically faster than the market currently expects, Nvidia could be in trouble. Under that scenario, demand for its GPUs would fall, taking the wind out of its jaw-dropping revenues and profits. This could happen because of softening end-user demand for AI models. There could also be cracks forming in the complex web of financing between the key players in the space.

Additionally, emerging competitive threats to Nvidia's dominant position in the AI accelerator market coming from peers are something investors need to keep tabs on. The chips being developed by both its longtime peers and some of its largest hyperscaler customers could materially eat away at Nvidia's share of the data center chip market.

Under that downbeat scenario, it's possible that its EPS will only grow 15% or 20% per year. And the earnings multiple the stock trades at could contract as growth investors head for the exits.

If negative sentiment hits Nvidia, it will surely spread through the market and impact other AI stocks. Because of how concentrated the value of the stock market is right now in companies connected to the AI trend, such a retreat could crush equities broadly. And that would resemble a bubble bursting.

Given how much momentum the AI ecosystem seems to have, investors may struggle to envision the bear case becoming a reality. Pay close attention to hyperscalers' capital expenditures. Revenue trends at AI labs Anthropic and OpenAI are also worth watching. Weakness there might indicate that things are cooling down.

Between the bear and bull cases, I still lean toward the former. However, I accept that uncertainty is extremely high.

news.Title: 美股季節性「黃金半年」將啟動 投資人該準備進場了嗎？
news.Content:
美股歷史上最受矚目的「萬聖節指標」(Halloween indicator)，或稱「最佳六個月」效應將於11月正式啟動。這項策略主張投資人於10月底買進股票並持有至次年4月，隨後在夏季5月至10月淡出股市。

此規律最早由Yale Hirsch於1986年發現，其子、《股票交易員年鑑》(Stock Trader's Almanac)總編輯Jeffrey Hirsch於2026年版中引述並指出：「你可以將一年畫分為兩個階段，幾乎所有的漲幅都集中在其中半年的時間，而另外半年則所剩無幾。」

歷史統計顯示，自1950年至1987年間，道瓊工業指數在11月至4月的平均漲幅約為7%，而5月至10月僅有不到1%。若自1950年起，每年僅將1萬美元投入於淡季半年，資產將萎縮至約4,300美元；反之，若僅投資於旺季半年，1萬美元則大幅成長至約130萬美元。

即使在規律發表後的39年間(1986年之後)，黃金半年的1萬美元投資，也已累積至約120萬美元，相較於淡季半年的5,800美元，展現出極為顯著的報酬差異。

然而，近年來傳統「5月賣股離場」策略正面臨環境轉變。自1988年以來，夏季半年的平均漲幅已提升至約3%。在過去十年間，淡季與旺季半年的平均報酬率甚至平分秋色，均達到約7%，其中5月至10月更有5個年份表現超越旺季，包含2025年夏季高達約23%的漲幅。

對此，Jeffrey Hirsch分析表示：「搶先布局者、文化行為的改變以及更快速的資訊流，近年來已改變了季節性效應。」 此外，指數型基金與401(k)退休金計畫的定期定額資金持續流入，也成為支撐夏季股市的重要推手。

儘管季節性效應出現質變，但在美國國會期中選舉年份，「黃金六個月」的優勢依然極為亮眼。數據顯示，自1950年以來，期中選舉年隨後的11月至4月期間已連續19次上揚，平均漲幅高達約15%。

據《Yahoo財經》報導指出，雖然夏季未必完全風險重重，但歷史上包含2001年大跌約15%、2002年跌幅約18%及2008年重挫約30%等極端行情，均發生於夏季，因此對現代投資人而言，更明智的作法或許是在5月進行「避險」而非完全「離場」。

news.Title: Vertiv stock surges as orders double amid AI build-out: 'Evolving faster than ever'
news.Content:
Vertiv ( VRT ) stock surged 15% in premarket trading as the data center infrastructure player showed it continues to benefit from the massive capex spending from the likes of Google ( GOOG ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ).

"We are in the middle of the largest infrastructure buildout and it's accelerating," Vertiv's CEO Giordano Albertazzi stated in the company's earnings release . "The demands on data center infrastructure are evolving faster than ever, and Vertiv's role in that buildout keeps expanding."

Vertiv makes power and cooling hardware for data centers and enterprise networks. The company explained that as AI fuels demand for this infrastructure, its orders have doubled year over year. The company counts Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia ( NVDA ), and Amazon ( AMZN ) among its customers, per S&P Global Market Intelligence.

That demand, plus strong third quarter results, have given Vertiv the confidence to raise its full-year outlook. In 2026, the company expects net sales of $14.45 billion to $14.85 billion, up from $13.8 billion to $14.2 billion.

Adjusted diluted earnings per share are expected to be $7.10-$7.20 for the year, representing earnings growth of 69%-71%. The midpoint of that range is above the $6.73 per share forecast Wall Street analysts penciled in.

In the third quarter, Vertiv reported net sales of $4.31 billion, beating Wall Street's expectations of $3.76 billion. Adjusted diluted earnings per share of $2.21 grew 78% year over year, also beating estimates of $1.82 per share.
